bsb.24:19: As drought and heat consume the melting snow, so Sheol steals those who have sinned.
bsb.24:20: The womb forgets them; the worm feeds on them; they are remembered no more. So injustice is like a broken tree.
bsb.24:21: They prey on the barren and childless, and show no kindness to the widow.
bsb.24:22: Yet by His power, God drags away the mighty; though rising up, they have no assurance of life.
bsb.24:23: He gives them a sense of security, but His eyes are on their ways.
bsb.24:24: They are exalted for a moment, then they are gone; they are brought low and gathered up like all others; they are cut off like heads of grain.
bsb.24:25: If this is not so, then who can prove me a liar and reduce my words to nothing?”
bsb.25:2: “Dominion and awe belong to God; He establishes harmony in the heights of heaven.
bsb.25:3: Can His troops be numbered? On whom does His light not rise?
bsb.25:4: How then can a man be just before God? How can one born of woman be pure?
bsb.25:5: If even the moon does not shine, and the stars are not pure in His sight,
bsb.25:6: how much less man, who is but a maggot, and the son of man, who is but a worm!”
bsb.26:2: “How you have helped the powerless and saved the arm that is feeble!
bsb.26:3: How you have counseled the unwise and provided fully sound insight!
bsb.26:4: To whom have you uttered these words? And whose spirit spoke through you?
bsb.26:5: The dead tremble— those beneath the waters and those who dwell in them.
bsb.26:6: Sheol is naked before God, and Abaddon has no covering.
bsb.26:7: He stretches out the north over empty space; He hangs the earth upon nothing.
bsb.26:8: He wraps up the waters in His clouds, yet the clouds do not burst under their own weight.
bsb.26:9: He covers the face of the full moon, spreading over it His cloud.
bsb.26:10: He has inscribed a horizon on the face of the waters at the boundary between light and darkness.
bsb.26:11: The foundations of heaven quake, astounded at His rebuke.
bsb.26:12: By His power He stirred the sea; by His understanding He shattered Rahab.
bsb.26:13: By His breath the skies were cleared; His hand pierced the fleeing serpent.
bsb.26:14: Indeed, these are but the fringes of His ways; how faint is the whisper we hear of Him! Who then can understand the thunder of His power?”
bsb.27:2: “As surely as God lives, who has deprived me of justice— the Almighty, who has embittered my soul—
bsb.27:3: as long as my breath is still within me and the breath of God remains in my nostrils,
bsb.27:4: my lips will not speak wickedness, and my tongue will not utter deceit.
bsb.27:5: I will never say that you are right; I will maintain my integrity until I die.
bsb.27:6: I will cling to my righteousness and never let go. As long as I live, my conscience will not accuse me.
bsb.27:7: May my enemy be like the wicked and my opponent like the unjust.
bsb.27:8: For what is the hope of the godless when he is cut off, when God takes away his life?
bsb.27:9: Will God hear his cry when distress comes upon him?
bsb.27:10: Will he delight in the Almighty? Will he call upon God at all times?
bsb.27:11: I will instruct you in the power of God. I will not conceal the ways of the Almighty.
bsb.27:12: Surely all of you have seen it for yourselves. Why then do you keep up this empty talk?
bsb.27:13: This is the wicked man’s portion from God— the heritage the ruthless receive from the Almighty.
bsb.27:14: Though his sons are many, they are destined for the sword; and his offspring will never have enough food.
bsb.27:15: His survivors will be buried by the plague, and their widows will not weep for them.
bsb.27:16: Though he heaps up silver like dust and piles up a wardrobe like clay,
bsb.27:17: what he lays up, the righteous will wear, and his silver will be divided by the innocent.
bsb.27:18: The house he built is like a moth’s cocoon, like a hut set up by a watchman.
bsb.27:19: He lies down wealthy, but will do so no more; when he opens his eyes, all is gone.
bsb.27:20: Terrors overtake him like a flood; a tempest sweeps him away in the night.
bsb.27:21: The east wind carries him away, and he is gone; it sweeps him out of his place.
bsb.27:22: It hurls itself against him without mercy as he flees headlong from its power.
bsb.27:23: It claps its hands at him and hisses him out of his place.
bsb.28:1: “Surely there is a mine for silver and a place where gold is refined.
bsb.28:2: Iron is taken from the earth, and copper is smelted from ore.
bsb.28:3: Man puts an end to the darkness; he probes the farthest recesses for ore in deepest darkness.
bsb.28:4: Far from human habitation he cuts a shaft in places forgotten by the foot of man. Far from men he dangles and sways.
bsb.28:5: Food may come from the earth, but from below it is transformed as by fire.
bsb.28:6: Its rocks are the source of sapphires, containing flecks of gold.
bsb.28:7: No bird of prey knows that path; no falcon’s eye has seen it.
bsb.28:8: Proud beasts have never trodden it; no lion has ever prowled over it.
bsb.28:9: The miner strikes the flint; he overturns mountains at their base.
bsb.28:10: He hews out channels in the rocks, and his eyes spot every treasure.
bsb.28:11: He stops up the sources of the streams to bring what is hidden to light.
bsb.28:12: But where can wisdom be found, and where does understanding dwell?
bsb.28:13: No man can know its value, nor is it found in the land of the living.
bsb.28:14: The ocean depths say, ‘It is not in me,’ while the sea declares, ‘It is not with me.’
bsb.28:15: It cannot be bought with gold, nor can its price be weighed out in silver.
bsb.28:16: It cannot be valued in the gold of Ophir, in precious onyx or sapphire.
bsb.28:17: Neither gold nor crystal can compare to it, nor jewels of fine gold be exchanged for it.
bsb.28:18: Coral and quartz are unworthy of mention; the price of wisdom is beyond rubies.
bsb.28:19: Topaz from Cush cannot compare to it, nor can it be valued in pure gold.
bsb.28:20: From where then does wisdom come, and where does understanding dwell?
bsb.28:21: It is hidden from the eyes of every living thing and concealed from the birds of the air.
bsb.28:22: Abaddon and Death say, ‘We have heard a rumor about it.’
bsb.28:23: But God understands its way, and He knows its place.
bsb.28:24: For He looks to the ends of the earth and sees everything under the heavens.
bsb.28:25: When God fixed the weight of the wind and measured out the waters,
bsb.28:26: when He set a limit for the rain and a path for the thunderbolt,
bsb.28:27: then He looked at wisdom and appraised it; He established it and searched it out.
bsb.28:28: And He said to man, ‘Behold, the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom, and to turn away from evil is understanding.’”
bsb.29:2: “How I long for the months gone by, for the days when God watched over me,
bsb.29:3: when His lamp shone above my head, and by His light I walked through the darkness,
bsb.29:4: when I was in my prime, when the friendship of God rested on my tent,
bsb.29:5: when the Almighty was still with me and my children were around me,
bsb.29:6: when my steps were bathed in cream and the rock poured out for me streams of oil!
bsb.29:7: When I went out to the city gate and took my seat in the public square,
bsb.29:8: the young men saw me and withdrew, and the old men rose to their feet.
bsb.29:9: The princes refrained from speaking and covered their mouths with their hands.
bsb.29:10: The voices of the nobles were hushed, and their tongues stuck to the roofs of their mouths.
bsb.29:11: For those who heard me called me blessed, and those who saw me commended me,
bsb.29:12: because I rescued the poor who cried out and the fatherless who had no helper.
bsb.29:13: The dying man blessed me, and I made the widow’s heart sing for joy.
bsb.29:14: I put on righteousness, and it clothed me; justice was my robe and my turban.
bsb.29:15: I served as eyes to the blind and as feet to the lame.
bsb.29:16: I was a father to the needy, and I took up the case of the stranger.
bsb.29:17: I shattered the fangs of the unjust and snatched the prey from his teeth.
bsb.29:18: So I thought: ‘I will die in my nest and multiply my days as the sand.
bsb.29:19: My roots will spread out to the waters, and the dew will rest nightly on my branches.
bsb.29:20: My glory is ever new within me, and my bow is renewed in my hand.’
bsb.29:21: Men listened to me with expectation, waiting silently for my counsel.
bsb.29:22: After my words, they spoke no more; my speech settled on them like dew.
bsb.29:23: They waited for me as for rain and drank in my words like spring showers.
bsb.29:24: If I smiled at them, they did not believe it; the light of my countenance was precious.
bsb.29:25: I chose their course and presided as chief. So I dwelt as a king among his troops, as a comforter of the mourners.
bsb.30:1: “But now they mock me, men younger than I am, whose fathers I would have refused to entrust with my sheep dogs.
bsb.30:2: What use to me was the strength of their hands, since their vigor had left them?
bsb.30:3: Gaunt from poverty and hunger, they gnawed the dry land, and the desolate wasteland by night.
bsb.30:4: They plucked mallow among the shrubs, and the roots of the broom tree were their food.
bsb.30:5: They were banished from among men, shouted down like thieves,
bsb.30:6: so that they lived on the slopes of the wadis, among the rocks and in holes in the ground.
bsb.30:7: They cried out among the shrubs and huddled beneath the nettles.
bsb.30:8: A senseless and nameless brood, they were driven off the land.
bsb.30:9: And now they mock me in song; I have become a byword among them.
bsb.30:10: They abhor me and keep far from me; they do not hesitate to spit in my face.
bsb.30:11: Because God has unstrung my bow and afflicted me, they have cast off restraint in my presence.
bsb.30:12: The rabble arises at my right; they lay snares for my feet and build siege ramps against me.
bsb.30:13: They tear up my path; they profit from my destruction, with no one to restrain them.
bsb.30:14: They advance as through a wide breach; through the ruins they keep rolling in.
bsb.30:15: Terrors are turned loose against me; they drive away my dignity as by the wind, and my prosperity has passed like a cloud.
bsb.30:16: And now my soul is poured out within me; days of affliction grip me.
bsb.30:17: Night pierces my bones, and my gnawing pains never rest.
bsb.30:18: With great force He grasps my garment; He seizes me by the collar of my tunic.
bsb.30:19: He throws me into the mud, and I have become like dust and ashes.
bsb.30:20: I cry out to You for help, but You do not answer; when I stand up, You merely look at me.
bsb.30:21: You have ruthlessly turned on me; You oppose me with Your strong hand.
bsb.30:22: You snatch me up into the wind and drive me before it; You toss me about in the storm.
bsb.30:23: Yes, I know that You will bring me down to death, to the place appointed for all the living.
bsb.30:24: Yet no one stretches out his hand to a ruined man when he cries for help in his distress.
bsb.30:25: Have I not wept for those in trouble? Has my soul not grieved for the needy?
bsb.30:26: But when I hoped for good, evil came; when I looked for light, darkness fell.
bsb.30:27: I am churning within and cannot rest; days of affliction confront me.
bsb.30:28: I go about blackened, but not by the sun. I stand up in the assembly and cry for help.
bsb.30:29: I have become a brother of jackals, a companion of ostriches.
bsb.30:30: My skin grows black and peels, and my bones burn with fever.
bsb.30:31: My harp is tuned to mourning and my flute to the sound of weeping.
bsb.31:1: “I have made a covenant with my eyes. How then could I gaze with desire at a virgin?
bsb.31:2: For what is the allotment of God from above, or the heritage from the Almighty on high?
bsb.31:3: Does not disaster come to the unjust and calamity to the workers of iniquity?
bsb.31:4: Does He not see my ways and count my every step?
bsb.31:5: If I have walked in falsehood or my foot has rushed to deceit,
bsb.31:6: let God weigh me with honest scales, that He may know my integrity.
bsb.31:7: If my steps have turned from the path, if my heart has followed my eyes, or if impurity has stuck to my hands,
bsb.31:8: then may another eat what I have sown, and may my crops be uprooted.
bsb.31:9: If my heart has been enticed by my neighbor’s wife, or I have lurked at his door,
bsb.31:10: then may my own wife grind grain for another, and may other men sleep with her.
bsb.31:11: For that would be a heinous crime, an iniquity to be judged.
bsb.31:12: For it is a fire that burns down to Abaddon; it would root out my entire harvest.
bsb.31:13: If I have rejected the cause of my manservant or maidservant when they made a complaint against me,
bsb.31:14: what will I do when God rises to judge? How will I answer when called to account?
bsb.31:15: Did not He who made me in the womb also make them? Did not the same One form us in the womb?
bsb.31:16: If I have denied the desires of the poor or allowed the widow’s eyes to fail,
bsb.31:17: if I have eaten my morsel alone, not sharing it with the fatherless—
bsb.31:18: though from my youth I reared him as would a father, and from my mother’s womb I guided the widow—
bsb.31:19: if I have seen one perish for lack of clothing, or a needy man without a cloak,
bsb.31:20: if his heart has not blessed me for warming him with the fleece of my sheep,
bsb.31:21: if I have lifted up my hand against the fatherless because I saw that I had support in the gate,
bsb.31:22: then may my arm fall from my shoulder and be torn from its socket.
bsb.31:23: For calamity from God terrifies me, and His splendor I cannot overpower.
bsb.31:24: If I have put my trust in gold or called pure gold my security,
bsb.31:25: if I have rejoiced in my great wealth because my hand had gained so much,
bsb.31:26: if I have beheld the sun in its radiance or the moon moving in splendor,
bsb.31:27: so that my heart was secretly enticed and my hand threw a kiss from my mouth,
bsb.31:28: this would also be an iniquity to be judged, for I would have denied God on high.
bsb.31:29: If I have rejoiced in my enemy’s ruin, or exulted when evil befell him—
bsb.31:30: I have not allowed my mouth to sin by asking for his life with a curse—
bsb.31:31: if the men of my house have not said, ‘Who is there who has not had his fill?’—
bsb.31:32: but no stranger had to lodge on the street, for my door has been open to the traveler—
bsb.31:33: if I have covered my transgressions like Adam by hiding my guilt in my heart,
bsb.31:34: because I greatly feared the crowds and the contempt of the clans terrified me, so that I kept silent and would not go outside—
bsb.31:35: (Oh, that I had one to hear me! Here is my signature. Let the Almighty answer me; let my accuser compose an indictment.
bsb.31:36: Surely I would carry it on my shoulder and wear it like a crown.
bsb.31:37: I would give account of all my steps; I would approach Him like a prince.)—
bsb.31:38: if my land cries out against me and its furrows weep together,
bsb.31:39: if I have devoured its produce without payment or broken the spirit of its tenants,
bsb.31:40: then let briers grow instead of wheat and stinkweed instead of barley.” Thus conclude the words of Job.
bsb.32:1: So these three men stopped answering Job, because he was righteous in his own eyes.
bsb.32:2: This kindled the anger of Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite, of the family of Ram. He burned with anger against Job for justifying himself rather than God,
bsb.32:3: and he burned with anger against Job’s three friends because they had failed to refute Job, and yet had condemned him.
bsb.32:4: Now Elihu had waited to speak to Job because the others were older than he.
bsb.32:5: But when he saw that the three men had no further reply, his anger was kindled.
bsb.32:6: So Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite declared: “I am young in years, while you are old; that is why I was timid and afraid to tell you what I know.
bsb.32:7: I thought that age should speak, and many years should teach wisdom.
bsb.32:8: But there is a spirit in a man, the breath of the Almighty, that gives him understanding.
bsb.32:9: It is not only the old who are wise, or the elderly who understand justice.
bsb.32:10: Therefore I say, ‘Listen to me; I too will declare what I know.’
bsb.32:11: Indeed, I waited while you spoke; I listened to your reasoning; as you searched for words,
bsb.32:12: I paid you full attention. But no one proved Job wrong; not one of you rebutted his arguments.
bsb.32:13: So do not claim, ‘We have found wisdom; let God, not man, refute him.’
bsb.32:14: But Job has not directed his words against me, and I will not answer him with your arguments.
bsb.32:15: Job’s friends are dismayed, with no more to say; words have escaped them.
bsb.32:16: Must I wait, now that they are silent, now that they stand and no longer reply?
bsb.32:17: I too will answer; yes, I will declare what I know.
bsb.32:18: For I am full of words, and my spirit within me compels me.
bsb.32:19: Behold, my belly is like unvented wine; it is about to burst like a new wineskin.
bsb.32:20: I must speak and find relief; I must open my lips and respond.
bsb.32:21: I will be partial to no one, nor will I flatter any man.
bsb.32:22: For I do not know how to flatter, or my Maker would remove me in an instant.
bsb.33:1: “But now, O Job, hear my speech, and listen to all my words.
bsb.33:2: Behold, I will open my mouth; my address is on the tip of my tongue.
bsb.33:3: My words are from an upright heart, and my lips speak sincerely what I know.
bsb.33:4: The Spirit of God has made me, and the breath of the Almighty gives me life.
bsb.33:5: Refute me if you can; prepare your case and confront me.
bsb.33:6: I am just like you before God; I was also formed from clay.
bsb.33:7: Surely no fear of me should terrify you; nor will my hand be heavy upon you.
bsb.33:8: Surely you have spoken in my hearing, and I have heard these very words:
bsb.33:9: ‘I am pure, without transgression; I am clean, with no iniquity in me.
bsb.33:10: Yet God finds occasions against me; He counts me as His enemy.
bsb.33:11: He puts my feet in the stocks; He watches over all my paths.’
bsb.33:12: Behold, you are not right in this matter. I will answer you, for God is greater than man.
bsb.33:13: Why do you complain to Him that He answers nothing a man asks?
bsb.33:14: For God speaks in one way and in another, yet no one notices.
bsb.33:15: In a dream, in a vision in the night, when deep sleep falls upon men as they slumber on their beds,
bsb.33:16: He opens their ears and terrifies them with warnings
bsb.33:17: to turn a man from wrongdoing and keep him from pride,
bsb.33:18: to preserve his soul from the Pit and his life from perishing by the sword.
bsb.33:19: A man is also chastened on his bed with pain and constant distress in his bones,
bsb.33:20: so that he detests his bread, and his soul loathes his favorite food.
bsb.33:21: His flesh wastes away from sight, and his hidden bones protrude.
bsb.33:22: He draws near to the Pit, and his life to the messengers of death.
bsb.33:23: Yet if there is a messenger on his side, one mediator in a thousand, to tell a man what is right for him,
bsb.33:24: to be gracious to him and say, ‘Spare him from going down to the Pit; I have found his ransom,’
bsb.33:25: then his flesh is refreshed like a child’s; he returns to the days of his youth.
bsb.33:26: He prays to God and finds favor; he sees God’s face and shouts for joy, and God restores His righteousness to that man.
bsb.33:27: Then he sings before men with these words: ‘I have sinned and perverted what was right; yet I did not get what I deserved.
bsb.33:28: He redeemed my soul from going down to the Pit, and I will live to see the light.’
bsb.33:29: Behold, all these things God does to a man, two or even three times,
bsb.33:30: to bring back his soul from the Pit, that he may be enlightened with the light of life.
bsb.33:31: Pay attention, Job, and listen to me; be silent, and I will speak.
bsb.33:32: But if you have something to say, answer me; speak up, for I would like to vindicate you.
bsb.33:33: But if not, then listen to me; be quiet, and I will teach you wisdom.”
bsb.34:2: “Hear my words, O wise men; give ear to me, O men of learning.
bsb.34:3: For the ear tests words as the mouth tastes food.
bsb.34:4: Let us choose for ourselves what is right; let us learn together what is good.
bsb.34:5: For Job has declared, ‘I am righteous, yet God has deprived me of justice.
bsb.34:6: Would I lie about my case? My wound is incurable, though I am without transgression.’
bsb.34:7: What man is like Job, who drinks up derision like water?
bsb.34:8: He keeps company with evildoers and walks with wicked men.
bsb.34:9: For he has said, ‘It profits a man nothing that he should delight in God.’
bsb.34:10: Therefore listen to me, O men of understanding. Far be it from God to do wrong, and from the Almighty to act unjustly.
bsb.34:11: For according to a man’s deeds He repays him; according to a man’s ways He brings consequences.
bsb.34:12: Indeed, it is true that God does not act wickedly, and the Almighty does not pervert justice.
bsb.34:13: Who gave Him charge over the earth? Who appointed Him over the whole world?
bsb.34:14: If He were to set His heart to it and withdraw His Spirit and breath,
bsb.34:15: all flesh would perish together and mankind would return to the dust.
bsb.34:16: If you have understanding, hear this; listen to my words.
bsb.34:17: Could one who hates justice govern? Will you condemn the just and mighty One,
bsb.34:18: who says to kings, ‘You are worthless!’ and to nobles, ‘You are wicked,’
bsb.34:19: who is not partial to princes and does not favor rich over poor? For they are all the work of His hands.
bsb.34:20: They die in an instant, in the middle of the night. The people convulse and pass away; the mighty are removed without human hand.
bsb.34:21: For His eyes are on the ways of a man, and He sees his every step.
bsb.34:22: There is no darkness or deep shadow where the workers of iniquity can hide.
bsb.34:23: For God need not examine a man further or have him approach for judgment.
bsb.34:24: He shatters the mighty without inquiry and sets up others in their place.
bsb.34:25: Therefore, He recognizes their deeds; He overthrows them in the night and they are crushed.
bsb.34:26: He strikes them for their wickedness in full view,
bsb.34:27: because they turned aside from Him and had no regard for any of His ways.
bsb.34:28: They caused the cry of the poor to come before Him, and He heard the outcry of the afflicted.
bsb.34:29: But when He remains silent, who can condemn Him? When He hides His face, who can see Him? Yet He watches over both man and nation,
bsb.34:30: that godless men should not rule or lay snares for the people.
bsb.34:31: Suppose someone says to God, ‘I have endured my punishment; I will offend no more.
bsb.34:32: Teach me what I cannot see; if I have done wrong, I will not do it again.’
bsb.34:33: Should God repay you on your own terms when you have disavowed His? You must choose, not I; so tell me what you know.
bsb.34:34: Men of understanding will declare to me, and the wise men who hear me will say:
bsb.34:35: ‘Job speaks without knowledge; his words lack insight.’
bsb.34:36: If only Job were tried to the utmost for answering like a wicked man.
bsb.34:37: For he adds rebellion to his sin; he claps his hands among us and multiplies his words against God.”
bsb.35:1: And Elihu went on to say:
bsb.35:2: “Do you think this is just? You say, ‘I am more righteous than God.’
bsb.35:3: For you ask, ‘What does it profit me, and what benefit do I gain apart from sin?’
bsb.35:4: I will reply to you and to your friends as well.
bsb.35:5: Look to the heavens and see; gaze at the clouds high above you.
bsb.35:6: If you sin, what do you accomplish against Him? If you multiply your transgressions, what do you do to Him?
bsb.35:7: If you are righteous, what do you give Him, or what does He receive from your hand?
bsb.35:8: Your wickedness affects only a man like yourself, and your righteousness only a son of man.
bsb.35:9: Men cry out under great oppression; they plead for relief from the arm of the mighty.
bsb.35:10: But no one asks, ‘Where is God my Maker, who gives us songs in the night,
bsb.35:11: who teaches us more than the beasts of the earth and makes us wiser than the birds of the air?’
bsb.35:12: There they cry out, but He does not answer, because of the pride of evil men.
bsb.35:13: Surely God does not listen to empty pleas, and the Almighty does not take note of it.
bsb.35:14: How much less, then, when you say that you do not see Him, that your case is before Him and you must wait for Him,
bsb.35:15: and further, that in His anger He has not punished or taken much notice of folly!
bsb.35:16: So Job opens his mouth in vain and multiplies words without knowledge.”
bsb.36:2: “Bear with me a little longer, and I will show you that there is more to be said on God’s behalf.
bsb.36:3: I get my knowledge from afar, and I will ascribe justice to my Maker.
bsb.36:4: For truly my words are free of falsehood; one perfect in knowledge is with you.
bsb.36:5: Indeed, God is mighty, but He despises no one; He is mighty in strength of understanding.
bsb.36:6: He does not keep the wicked alive, but He grants justice to the afflicted.
bsb.36:7: He does not take His eyes off the righteous, but He enthrones them with kings and exalts them forever.
bsb.36:8: And if men are bound with chains, caught in cords of affliction,
bsb.36:9: then He tells them their deeds and how arrogantly they have transgressed.
bsb.36:10: He opens their ears to correction and commands that they turn from iniquity.
bsb.36:11: If they obey and serve Him, then they end their days in prosperity and their years in happiness.
bsb.36:12: But if they do not obey, then they perish by the sword and die without knowledge.
bsb.36:13: The godless in heart harbor resentment; even when He binds them, they do not cry for help.
bsb.36:14: They die in their youth, among the male shrine prostitutes.
bsb.36:15: God rescues the afflicted by their affliction and opens their ears in oppression.
bsb.36:16: Indeed, He drew you from the jaws of distress to a spacious and broad place, to a table full of richness.
bsb.36:17: But now you are laden with the judgment due the wicked; judgment and justice have seized you.
bsb.36:18: Be careful that no one lures you with riches; do not let a large bribe lead you astray.
bsb.36:19: Can your wealth or all your mighty effort keep you from distress?
bsb.36:20: Do not long for the night, when people vanish from their homes.
bsb.36:21: Be careful not to turn to iniquity, for this you have preferred to affliction.
bsb.36:22: Behold, God is exalted in His power. Who is a teacher like Him?
bsb.36:23: Who has appointed His way for Him, or told Him, ‘You have done wrong’?
bsb.36:24: Remember to magnify His work, which men have praised in song.
bsb.36:25: All mankind has seen it; men behold it from afar.
bsb.36:26: Indeed, God is great—beyond our knowledge; the number of His years is unsearchable.
bsb.36:27: For He draws up drops of water which distill the rain from the mist,
bsb.36:28: which the clouds pour out and shower abundantly on mankind.
bsb.36:29: Furthermore, who can understand how the clouds spread out, how the thunder roars from His pavilion?
bsb.36:30: See how He scatters His lightning around Him and covers the depths of the sea.
bsb.36:31: For by these He judges the nations and provides food in abundance.
bsb.36:32: He fills His hands with lightning and commands it to strike its mark.
bsb.36:33: The thunder declares His presence; even the cattle regard the rising storm.
bsb.37:1: “At this my heart also pounds and leaps from its place.
bsb.37:2: Listen closely to the thunder of His voice and the rumbling that comes from His mouth.
bsb.37:3: He unleashes His lightning beneath the whole sky and sends it to the ends of the earth.
bsb.37:4: Then there comes a roaring sound; He thunders with His majestic voice. He does not restrain the lightning when His voice resounds.
bsb.37:5: God thunders wondrously with His voice; He does great things we cannot comprehend.
bsb.37:6: For He says to the snow, ‘Fall on the earth,’ and to the gentle rain, ‘Pour out a mighty downpour.’
bsb.37:7: He seals up the hand of every man, so that all men may know His work.
bsb.37:8: The wild animals enter their lairs; they settle down in their dens.
bsb.37:9: The tempest comes from its chamber, and the cold from the driving north winds.
bsb.37:10: By the breath of God the ice is formed and the watery expanses are frozen.
bsb.37:11: He loads the clouds with moisture; He scatters His lightning through them.
bsb.37:12: They swirl about, whirling at His direction, accomplishing all that He commands over the face of all the earth.
bsb.37:13: Whether for punishment or for His land, He accomplishes this in His loving devotion.
bsb.37:14: Listen to this, O Job; stand still and consider the wonders of God.
bsb.37:15: Do you know how God dispatches the clouds or makes the lightning flash?
bsb.37:16: Do you understand how the clouds float, those wonders of Him who is perfect in knowledge?
bsb.37:17: You whose clothes get hot when the land lies hushed under the south wind,
bsb.37:18: can you, like Him, spread out the skies to reflect the heat like a mirror of bronze?
bsb.37:19: Teach us what we should say to Him; we cannot draw up our case when our faces are in darkness.
bsb.37:20: Should He be told that I want to speak? Would a man ask to be swallowed up?
bsb.37:21: Now no one can gaze at the sun when it is bright in the skies after the wind has swept them clean.
bsb.37:22: Out of the north He comes in golden splendor; awesome majesty surrounds Him.
bsb.37:23: The Almighty is beyond our reach; He is exalted in power! In His justice and great righteousness He does not oppress.
bsb.37:24: Therefore, men fear Him, for He is not partial to the wise in heart.”
bsb.38:1: Then the LORD answered Job out of the whirlwind and said:
bsb.38:2: “Who is this who obscures My counsel by words without knowledge?
bsb.38:3: Now brace yourself like a man; I will question you, and you shall inform Me.
bsb.38:4: Where were you when I laid the foundations of the earth? Tell Me, if you have understanding.
bsb.38:5: Who fixed its measurements? Surely you know! Or who stretched a measuring line across it?
bsb.38:6: On what were its foundations set, or who laid its cornerstone,
bsb.38:7: while the morning stars sang together and all the sons of God shouted for joy?
bsb.38:8: Who enclosed the sea behind doors when it burst forth from the womb,
bsb.38:9: when I made the clouds its garment and thick darkness its blanket,
bsb.38:10: when I fixed its boundaries and set in place its bars and doors,
bsb.38:11: and I declared: ‘You may come this far, but no farther; here your proud waves must stop’?
bsb.38:12: In your days, have you commanded the morning or assigned the dawn its place,
bsb.38:13: that it might spread to the ends of the earth and shake the wicked out of it?
bsb.38:14: The earth takes shape like clay under a seal; its hills stand out like the folds of a garment.
bsb.38:15: Light is withheld from the wicked, and their upraised arm is broken.
bsb.38:16: Have you journeyed to the vents of the sea or walked in the trenches of the deep?
bsb.38:17: Have the gates of death been revealed to you? Have you seen the gates of the shadow of death?
bsb.38:18: Have you surveyed the extent of the earth? Tell Me, if you know all this.
bsb.38:19: Where is the way to the home of light? Do you know where darkness resides,
bsb.38:20: so you can lead it back to its border? Do you know the paths to its home?
bsb.38:21: Surely you know, for you were already born! And the number of your days is great!
bsb.38:22: Have you entered the storehouses of snow or observed the storehouses of hail,
bsb.38:23: which I hold in reserve for times of trouble, for the day of war and battle?
bsb.38:24: In which direction is the lightning dispersed, or the east wind scattered over the earth?
bsb.38:25: Who cuts a channel for the flood or clears a path for the thunderbolt,
bsb.38:26: to bring rain on a barren land, on a desert where no man lives,
bsb.38:27: to satisfy the parched wasteland and make it sprout with tender grass?
bsb.38:28: Does the rain have a father? Who has begotten the drops of dew?
bsb.38:29: From whose womb does the ice emerge? Who gives birth to the frost from heaven,
bsb.38:30: when the waters become hard as stone and the surface of the deep is frozen?
bsb.38:31: Can you bind the chains of the Pleiades or loosen the belt of Orion?
bsb.38:32: Can you bring forth the constellations in their seasons or lead out the Bear and her cubs?
bsb.38:33: Do you know the laws of the heavens? Can you set their dominion over the earth?
bsb.38:34: Can you command the clouds so that a flood of water covers you?
bsb.38:35: Can you send the lightning bolts on their way? Do they report to you, ‘Here we are’?
bsb.38:36: Who has put wisdom in the heart or given understanding to the mind?
bsb.38:37: Who has the wisdom to count the clouds? Or who can tilt the water jars of the heavens
bsb.38:38: when the dust hardens into a mass and the clods of earth stick together?
bsb.38:39: Can you hunt the prey for a lioness or satisfy the hunger of young lions
bsb.38:40: when they crouch in their dens and lie in wait in the thicket?
bsb.38:41: Who provides food for the raven when its young cry out to God as they wander about for lack of food?
bsb.39:1: “Do you know when mountain goats give birth? Have you watched the doe bear her fawn?
bsb.39:2: Can you count the months they are pregnant? Do you know the time they give birth?
bsb.39:3: They crouch down and bring forth their young; they deliver their newborn.
bsb.39:4: Their young ones thrive and grow up in the open field; they leave and do not return.
bsb.39:5: Who set the wild donkey free? Who released the swift donkey from the harness?
bsb.39:6: I made the wilderness his home and the salt flats his dwelling.
bsb.39:7: He scorns the tumult of the city and never hears the shouts of a driver.
bsb.39:8: He roams the mountains for pasture, searching for any green thing.
bsb.39:9: Will the wild ox consent to serve you? Will he stay by your manger at night?
bsb.39:10: Can you hold him to the furrow with a harness? Will he plow the valleys behind you?
bsb.39:11: Can you rely on his great strength? Will you leave your hard work to him?
bsb.39:12: Can you trust him to bring in your grain and gather it to your threshing floor?
bsb.39:13: The wings of the ostrich flap joyfully, but cannot match the pinions and feathers of the stork.
bsb.39:14: For she leaves her eggs on the ground and lets them warm in the sand.
bsb.39:15: She forgets that a foot may crush them, or a wild animal may trample them.
bsb.39:16: She treats her young harshly, as if not her own, with no concern that her labor was in vain.
bsb.39:17: For God has deprived her of wisdom; He has not endowed her with understanding.
bsb.39:18: Yet when she proudly spreads her wings, she laughs at the horse and its rider.
bsb.39:19: Do you give strength to the horse or adorn his neck with a mane?
bsb.39:20: Do you make him leap like a locust, striking terror with his proud snorting?
bsb.39:21: He paws in the valley and rejoices in his strength; he charges into battle.
bsb.39:22: He laughs at fear, frightened of nothing; he does not turn back from the sword.
bsb.39:23: A quiver rattles at his side, along with a flashing spear and lance.
bsb.39:24: Trembling with excitement, he devours the distance; he cannot stand still when the ram’s horn sounds.
bsb.39:25: At the blast of the horn, he snorts with fervor. He catches the scent of battle from afar— the shouts of captains and the cry of war.
bsb.39:26: Does the hawk take flight by your understanding and spread his wings toward the south?
bsb.39:27: Does the eagle soar at your command and make his nest on high?
bsb.39:28: He dwells on a cliff and lodges there; his stronghold is on a rocky crag.
bsb.39:29: From there he spies out food; his eyes see it from afar.
bsb.39:30: His young ones feast on blood; and where the slain are, there he is.”
bsb.40:1: And the LORD said to Job:
bsb.40:2: “Will the faultfinder contend with the Almighty? Let him who argues with God give an answer.”
bsb.40:4: “Behold, I am insignificant. How can I reply to You? I place my hand over my mouth.
bsb.40:5: I have spoken once, but I have no answer— twice, but I have nothing to add.”
bsb.40:6: Then the LORD answered Job out of the whirlwind and said:
bsb.40:7: “Now brace yourself like a man; I will question you, and you shall inform Me.
bsb.40:8: Would you really annul My justice? Would you condemn Me to justify yourself?
bsb.40:9: Do you have an arm like God’s? Can you thunder with a voice like His?
bsb.40:10: Then adorn yourself with majesty and splendor, and clothe yourself with honor and glory.
bsb.40:11: Unleash the fury of your wrath; look on every proud man and bring him low.
bsb.40:12: Look on every proud man and humble him; trample the wicked where they stand.
bsb.40:13: Bury them together in the dust; imprison them in the grave.
bsb.40:14: Then I will confess to you that your own right hand can save you.
bsb.40:15: Look at Behemoth, which I made along with you. He feeds on grass like an ox.
bsb.40:16: See the strength of his loins and the power in the muscles of his belly.
bsb.40:17: His tail sways like a cedar; the sinews of his thighs are tightly knit.
bsb.40:18: His bones are tubes of bronze; his limbs are rods of iron.
bsb.40:19: He is the foremost of God’s works; only his Maker can draw the sword against him.
bsb.40:20: The hills yield him their produce, while all the beasts of the field play nearby.
bsb.40:21: He lies under the lotus plants, hidden among the reeds of the marsh.
bsb.40:22: The lotus plants conceal him in their shade; the willows of the brook surround him.
bsb.40:23: Though the river rages, Behemoth is unafraid; he remains secure, though the Jordan surges to his mouth.
bsb.40:24: Can anyone capture him as he looks on, or pierce his nose with a snare?
bsb.41:1: “Can you pull in Leviathan with a hook or tie down his tongue with a rope?
bsb.41:2: Can you put a cord through his nose or pierce his jaw with a hook?
bsb.41:3: Will he beg you for mercy or speak to you softly?
bsb.41:4: Will he make a covenant with you to take him as a slave for life?
bsb.41:5: Can you pet him like a bird or put him on a leash for your maidens?
bsb.41:6: Will traders barter for him or divide him among the merchants?
bsb.41:7: Can you fill his hide with harpoons or his head with fishing spears?
bsb.41:8: If you lay a hand on him, you will remember the battle and never repeat it!
bsb.41:9: Surely hope of overcoming him is false. Is not the sight of him overwhelming?
bsb.41:10: No one is so fierce as to rouse Leviathan. Then who is able to stand against Me?
bsb.41:11: Who has given to Me that I should repay him? Everything under heaven is Mine.
bsb.41:12: I cannot keep silent about his limbs, his power and graceful form.
bsb.41:13: Who can strip off his outer coat? Who can approach him with a bridle?
bsb.41:14: Who can open his jaws, ringed by his fearsome teeth?
bsb.41:15: His rows of scales are his pride, tightly sealed together.
bsb.41:16: One scale is so near to another that no air can pass between them.
bsb.41:17: They are joined to one another; they clasp and cannot be separated.
bsb.41:18: His snorting flashes with light, and his eyes are like the rays of dawn.
bsb.41:19: Firebrands stream from his mouth; fiery sparks shoot forth!
bsb.41:20: Smoke billows from his nostrils as from a boiling pot over burning reeds.
bsb.41:21: His breath sets coals ablaze, and flames pour from his mouth.
bsb.41:22: Strength resides in his neck, and dismay leaps before him.
bsb.41:23: The folds of his flesh are tightly joined; they are firm and immovable.
bsb.41:24: His chest is as hard as a rock, as hard as a lower millstone!
bsb.41:25: When Leviathan rises up, the mighty are terrified; they withdraw before his thrashing.
bsb.41:26: The sword that reaches him has no effect, nor does the spear or dart or arrow.
bsb.41:27: He regards iron as straw and bronze as rotten wood.
bsb.41:28: No arrow can make him flee; slingstones become like chaff to him.
bsb.41:29: A club is regarded as straw, and he laughs at the sound of the lance.
bsb.41:30: His undersides are jagged potsherds, spreading out the mud like a threshing sledge.
bsb.41:31: He makes the depths seethe like a cauldron; he makes the sea like a jar of ointment.
bsb.41:32: He leaves a glistening wake behind him; one would think the deep had white hair!
bsb.41:33: Nothing on earth is his equal— a creature devoid of fear!
bsb.41:34: He looks down on all the haughty; he is king over all the proud.”
bsb.42:1: Then Job replied to the LORD:
bsb.42:2: “I know that You can do all things and that no plan of Yours can be thwarted.
bsb.42:3: You asked, ‘Who is this who conceals My counsel without knowledge?’ Surely I spoke of things I did not understand, things too wonderful for me to know.
bsb.42:4: You said, ‘Listen now, and I will speak. I will question you, and you shall inform Me.’
bsb.42:5: My ears had heard of You, but now my eyes have seen You.
bsb.42:6: Therefore I retract my words, and I repent in dust and ashes.”
bsb.42:7: After the LORD had spoken these words to Job, He said to Eliphaz the Temanite, “My wrath is kindled against you and your two friends. For you have not spoken about Me accurately, as My servant Job has.
bsb.42:8: So now, take seven bulls and seven rams, go to My servant Job, and sacrifice a burnt offering for yourselves. Then My servant Job will pray for you, for I will accept his prayer and not deal with you according to your folly. For you have not spoken accurately about Me, as My servant Job has.”
bsb.42:9: So Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite went and did as the LORD had told them; and the LORD accepted Job’s request.
bsb.42:10: After Job had prayed for his friends, the LORD restored his prosperity and doubled his former possessions.
bsb.42:11: All his brothers and sisters and prior acquaintances came and dined with him in his house. They consoled him and comforted him over all the adversity that the LORD had brought upon him. And each one gave him a piece of silver and a gold ring.
bsb.42:12: So the LORD blessed Job’s latter days more than his first. He owned 14,000 sheep, 6,000 camels, 1,000 yoke of oxen, and 1,000 female donkeys.
bsb.42:13: And he also had seven sons and three daughters.
bsb.42:14: He named his first daughter Jemimah, his second Keziah, and his third Keren-happuch.
bsb.42:15: No women as beautiful as Job’s daughters could be found in all the land, and their father granted them an inheritance among their brothers.
bsb.42:16: After this, Job lived 140 years and saw his children and their children to the fourth generation.
bsb.42:17: And so Job died, old and full of years.

asv.1:1: There was a man in the land of Uz, whose name was Job; and that man was perfect and upright, and one that feared God, and turned away from evil.
asv.1:2: And there were born unto him seven sons and three daughters.
asv.1:3: His substance also was seven thousand sheep, and three thousand camels, and five hundred yoke of oxen, and five hundred she-asses, and a very great household; so that this man was the greatest of all the children of the east.
asv.1:4: And his sons went and held a feast in the house of each one upon his day; and they sent and called for their three sisters to eat and to drink with them.
asv.1:5: And it was so, when the days of their feasting were gone about, that Job sent and sanctified them, and rose up early in the morning, and offered burnt-offerings according to the number of them all: for Job said, It may be that my sons have sinned, and renounced God in their hearts. Thus did Job continually.
asv.1:6: Now it came to pass on the day when the sons of God came to present themselves before Jehovah, that Satan also came among them.
asv.1:7: And Jehovah said unto Satan, Whence comest thou? Then Satan answered Jehovah, and said, From going to and fro in the earth, and from walking up and down in it.
asv.1:8: And Jehovah said unto Satan, Hast thou considered my servant Job? for there is none like him in the earth, a perfect and an upright man, one that feareth God, and turneth away from evil.
asv.1:9: Then Satan answered Jehovah, and said, Doth Job fear God for nought?
asv.1:10: Hast not thou made a hedge about him, and about his house, and about all that he hath, on every side? thou hast blessed the work of his hands, and his substance is increased in the land.
asv.1:11: But put forth thy hand now, and touch all that he hath, and he will renounce thee to thy face.
asv.1:12: And Jehovah said unto Satan, Behold, all that he hath is in thy power; only upon himself put not forth thy hand. So Satan went forth from the presence of Jehovah.
asv.1:13: And it fell on a day when his sons and his daughters were eating and drinking wine in their eldest brother’s house,
asv.1:14: that there came a messenger unto Job, and said, The oxen were plowing, and the asses feeding beside them;
asv.1:15: and the Sabeans fell upon them, and took them away: yea, they have slain the servants with the edge of the sword; and I only am escaped alone to tell thee.
asv.1:16: While he was yet speaking, there came also another, and said, The fire of God is fallen from heaven, and hath burned up the sheep and the servants, and consumed them; and I only am escaped alone to tell thee.
asv.1:17: While he was yet speaking, there came also another, and said, The Chaldeans made three bands, and fell upon the camels, and have taken them away, yea, and slain the servants with the edge of the sword; and I only am escaped alone to tell thee.
asv.1:18: While he was yet speaking, there came also another, and said, Thy sons and thy daughters were eating and drinking wine in their eldest brother’s house;
asv.1:19: and, behold, there came a great wind from the wilderness, and smote the four corners of the house, and it fell upon the young men, and they are dead; and I only am escaped alone to tell thee.
asv.1:20: Then Job arose, and rent his robe, and shaved his head, and fell down upon the ground, and worshipped;
asv.1:21: and he said, Naked came I out of my mother’s womb, and naked shall I return thither: Jehovah gave, and Jehovah hath taken away; blessed be the name of Jehovah.
asv.1:22: In all this Job sinned not, nor charged God foolishly.
asv.2:1: Again it came to pass on the day when the sons of God came to present themselves before Jehovah, that Satan came also among them to present himself before Jehovah.
asv.2:2: And Jehovah said unto Satan, From whence comest thou? And Satan answered Jehovah, and said, From going to and fro in the earth, and from walking up and down in it.
asv.2:3: And Jehovah said unto Satan, Hast thou considered my servant Job? for there is none like him in the earth, a perfect and an upright man, one that feareth God, and turneth away from evil: and he still holdeth fast his integrity, although thou movedst me against him, to destroy him without cause.
asv.2:4: And Satan answered Jehovah, and said, Skin for skin, yea, all that a man hath will he give for his life.
asv.2:5: But put forth thy hand now, and touch his bone and his flesh, and he will renounce thee to thy face.
asv.2:6: And Jehovah said unto Satan, Behold, he is in thy hand; only spare his life.
asv.2:7: So Satan went forth from the presence of Jehovah, and smote Job with sore boils from the sole of his foot unto his crown.
asv.2:8: And he took him a potsherd to scrape himself therewith; and he sat among the ashes.
asv.2:9: Then said his wife unto him, Dost thou still hold fast thine integrity? renounce God, and die.
asv.2:10: But he said unto her, Thou speakest as one of the foolish women speaketh. What? shall we receive good at the hand of God, and shall we not receive evil? In all this did not Job sin with his lips.
asv.2:11: Now when Job’s three friends heard of all this evil that was come upon him, they came every one from his own place: Eliphaz the Temanite, and Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite; and they made an appointment together to come to bemoan him and to comfort him.
asv.2:12: And when they lifted up their eyes afar off, and knew him not, they lifted up their voice, and wept; and they rent every one his robe, and sprinkled dust upon their heads toward heaven.
asv.2:13: So they sat down with him upon the ground seven days and seven nights, and none spake a word unto him: for they saw that his grief was very great.
asv.3:1: After this opened Job his mouth, and cursed his day.
asv.3:3: Let the day perish wherein I was born, And the night which said, There is a man-child conceived.
asv.3:4: Let that day be darkness; Let not God from above seek for it, Neither let the light shine upon it.
asv.3:5: Let darkness and the shadow of death claim it for their own; Let a cloud dwell upon it; Let all that maketh black the day terrify it.
asv.3:6: As for that night, let thick darkness seize upon it: Let it not rejoice among the days of the year; Let it not come into the number of the months.
asv.3:7: Lo, let that night be barren; Let no joyful voice come therein.
asv.3:8: Let them curse it that curse the day, Who are ready to rouse up leviathan.
asv.3:9: Let the stars of the twilight thereof be dark: Let it look for light, but have none; Neither let it behold the eyelids of the morning:
asv.3:10: Because it shut not up the doors of my mother’s womb, Nor hid trouble from mine eyes.
asv.3:11: Why died I not from the womb? Why did I not give up the ghost when my mother bare me?
asv.3:12: Why did the knees receive me? Or why the breasts, that I should suck?
asv.3:13: For now should I have lain down and been quiet; I should have slept; then had I been at rest,
asv.3:14: With kings and counsellors of the earth, Who built up waste places for themselves;
asv.3:15: Or with princes that had gold, Who filled their houses with silver:
asv.3:16: Or as a hidden untimely birth I had not been, As infants that never saw light.
asv.3:17: There the wicked cease from troubling; And there the weary are at rest.
asv.3:18: There the prisoners are at ease together; They hear not the voice of the taskmaster.
asv.3:19: The small and the great are there: And the servant is free from his master.
asv.3:20: Wherefore is light given to him that is in misery, And life unto the bitter in soul;
asv.3:21: Who long for death, but it cometh not, And dig for it more than for hid treasures;
asv.3:22: Who rejoice exceedingly, And are glad, when they can find the grave?
asv.3:23: Why is light given to a man whose way is hid, And whom God hath hedged in?
asv.3:24: For my sighing cometh before I eat, And my groanings are poured out like water.
asv.3:25: For the thing which I fear cometh upon me, And that which I am afraid of cometh unto me.
asv.3:26: I am not at ease, neither am I quiet, neither have I rest; But trouble cometh.
asv.4:1: Then answered Eliphaz the Temanite, and said,
asv.4:2: If one assay to commune with thee, wilt thou be grieved? But who can withhold himself from speaking?
asv.4:3: Behold, thou hast instructed many, And thou hast strengthened the weak hands.
asv.4:4: Thy words have upholden him that was falling, And thou hast made firm the feeble knees.
asv.4:5: But now it is come unto thee, and thou faintest; It toucheth thee, and thou art troubled.
asv.4:6: Is not thy fear of God thy confidence, And the integrity of thy ways thy hope?
asv.4:7: Remember, I pray thee, who ever perished, being innocent? Or where were the upright cut off?
asv.4:8: According as I have seen, they that plow iniquity, And sow trouble, reap the same.
asv.4:9: By the breath of God they perish, And by the blast of his anger are they consumed.
asv.4:10: The roaring of the lion, and the voice of the fierce lion, And the teeth of the young lions, are broken.
asv.4:11: The old lion perisheth for lack of prey, And the whelps of the lioness are scattered abroad.
asv.4:12: Now a thing was secretly brought to me, And mine ear received a whisper thereof.
asv.4:13: In thoughts from the visions of the night, When deep sleep falleth on men,
asv.4:14: Fear came upon me, and trembling, Which made all my bones to shake.
asv.4:15: Then a spirit passed before my face; The hair of my flesh stood up.
asv.4:16: It stood still, but I could not discern the appearance thereof; A form was before mine eyes: There was silence, and I heard a voice, saying,
asv.4:17: Shall mortal man be more just than God? Shall a man be more pure than his Maker?
asv.4:18: Behold, he putteth no trust in his servants; And his angels he chargeth with folly:
asv.4:19: How much more them that dwell in houses of clay, Whose foundation is in the dust, Who are crushed before the moth!
asv.4:20: Betwixt morning and evening they are destroyed: They perish for ever without any regarding it.
asv.4:21: Is not their tent-cord plucked up within them? They die, and that without wisdom.
asv.5:1: Call now; is there any that will answer thee? And to which of the holy ones wilt thou turn?
asv.5:2: For vexation killeth the foolish man, And jealousy slayeth the silly one.
asv.5:3: I have seen the foolish taking root: But suddenly I cursed his habitation.
asv.5:4: His children are far from safety, And they are crushed in the gate, Neither is there any to deliver them:
asv.5:5: Whose harvest the hungry eateth up, And taketh it even out of the thorns; And the snare gapeth for their substance.
asv.5:6: For affliction cometh not forth from the dust, Neither doth trouble spring out of the ground;
asv.5:7: But man is born unto trouble, As the sparks fly upward.
asv.5:8: But as for me, I would seek unto God, And unto God would I commit my cause;
asv.5:9: Who doeth great things and unsearchable, Marvellous things without number:
asv.5:10: Who giveth rain upon the earth, And sendeth waters upon the fields;
asv.5:11: So that he setteth up on high those that are low, And those that mourn are exalted to safety.
asv.5:12: He frustrateth the devices of the crafty, So that their hands cannot perform their enterprise.
asv.5:13: He taketh the wise in their own craftiness; And the counsel of the cunning is carried headlong.
asv.5:14: They meet with darkness in the day-time, And grope at noonday as in the night.
asv.5:15: But he saveth from the sword of their mouth, Even the needy from the hand of the mighty.
asv.5:16: So the poor hath hope, And iniquity stoppeth her mouth.
asv.5:17: Behold, happy is the man whom God correcteth: Therefore despise not thou the chastening of the Almighty.
asv.5:18: For he maketh sore, and bindeth up; He woundeth, and his hands make whole.
asv.5:19: He will deliver thee in six troubles; Yea, in seven there shall no evil touch thee.
asv.5:20: In famine he will redeem thee from death; And in war from the power of the sword.
asv.5:21: Thou shalt be hid from the scourge of the tongue; Neither shalt thou be afraid of destruction when it cometh.
asv.5:22: At destruction and dearth thou shalt laugh; Neither shalt thou be afraid of the beasts of the earth.
asv.5:23: For thou shalt be in league with the stones of the field; And the beasts of the field shall be at peace with thee.
asv.5:24: And thou shalt know that thy tent is in peace; And thou shalt visit thy fold, and shalt miss nothing.
asv.5:25: Thou shalt know also that thy seed shall be great, And thine offspring as the grass of the earth.
asv.5:26: Thou shalt come to thy grave in a full age, Like as a shock of grain cometh in in its season.
asv.5:27: Lo this, we have searched it, so it is; Hear it, and know thou it for thy good.
asv.6:2: Oh that my vexation were but weighed, And all my calamity laid in the balances!
asv.6:3: For now it would be heavier than the sand of the seas: Therefore have my words been rash.
asv.6:4: For the arrows of the Almighty are within me, The poison whereof my spirit drinketh up: The terrors of God do set themselves in array against me.
asv.6:5: Doth the wild ass bray when he hath grass? Or loweth the ox over his fodder?
asv.6:6: Can that which hath no savor be eaten without salt? Or is there any taste in the white of an egg?
asv.6:7: My soul refuseth to touch them; They are as loathsome food to me.
asv.6:8: Oh that I might have my request; And that God would grant me the thing that I long for!
asv.6:9: Even that it would please God to crush me; That he would let loose his hand, and cut me off!
asv.6:10: And be it still my consolation, Yea, let me exult in pain that spareth not, That I have not denied the words of the Holy One.
asv.6:11: What is my strength, that I should wait? And what is mine end, that I should be patient?
asv.6:12: Is my strength the strength of stones? Or is my flesh of brass?
asv.6:13: Is it not that I have no help in me, And that wisdom is driven quite from me?
asv.6:14: To him that is ready to faint kindness should be showed from his friend; Even to him that forsaketh the fear of the Almighty.
asv.6:15: My brethren have dealt deceitfully as a brook, As the channel of brooks that pass away;
asv.6:16: Which are black by reason of the ice, And wherein the snow hideth itself:
asv.6:17: What time they wax warm, they vanish; When it is hot, they are consumed out of their place.
asv.6:18: The caravans that travel by the way of them turn aside; They go up into the waste, and perish.
asv.6:19: The caravans of Tema looked, The companies of Sheba waited for them.
asv.6:20: They were put to shame because they had hoped; They came thither, and were confounded.
asv.6:21: For now ye are nothing; Ye see a terror, and are afraid.
asv.6:22: Did I say, Give unto me? Or, Offer a present for me of your substance?
asv.6:23: Or, Deliver me from the adversary’s hand? Or, Redeem me from the hand of the oppressors?
asv.6:24: Teach me, and I will hold my peace; And cause me to understand wherein I have erred.
asv.6:25: How forcible are words of uprightness! But your reproof, what doth it reprove?
asv.6:26: Do ye think to reprove words, Seeing that the speeches of one that is desperate are as wind?
asv.6:27: Yea, ye would cast lots upon the fatherless, And make merchandise of your friend.
asv.6:28: Now therefore be pleased to look upon me; For surely I shall not lie to your face.
asv.6:29: Return, I pray you, let there be no injustice; Yea, return again, my cause is righteous.
asv.6:30: Is there injustice on my tongue? Cannot my taste discern mischievous things?
asv.7:1: Is there not a warfare to man upon earth? And are not his days like the days of a hireling?
asv.7:2: As a servant that earnestly desireth the shadow, And as a hireling that looketh for his wages:
asv.7:3: So am I made to possess months of misery, And wearisome nights are appointed to me.
asv.7:4: When I lie down, I say, When shall I arise, and the night be gone? And I am full of tossings to and fro unto the dawning of the day.
asv.7:5: My flesh is clothed with worms and clods of dust; My skin closeth up, and breaketh out afresh.
asv.7:6: My days are swifter than a weaver’s shuttle, And are spent without hope.
asv.7:7: Oh remember that my life is a breath: Mine eye shall no more see good.
asv.7:8: The eye of him that seeth me shall behold me no more; Thine eyes shall be upon me, but I shall not be.
asv.7:9: As the cloud is consumed and vanisheth away, So he that goeth down to Sheol shall come up no more.
asv.7:10: He shall return no more to his house, Neither shall his place know him any more.
asv.7:11: Therefore I will not refrain my mouth; I will speak in the anguish of my spirit; I will complain in the bitterness of my soul.
asv.7:12: Am I a sea, or a sea-monster, That thou settest a watch over me?
asv.7:13: When I say, My bed shall comfort me, My couch shall ease my complaint;
asv.7:14: Then thou scarest me with dreams, And terrifiest me through visions:
asv.7:15: So that my soul chooseth strangling, And death rather than these my bones.
asv.7:16: I loathe my life; I would not live alway: Let me alone; for my days are vanity.
asv.7:17: What is man, that thou shouldest magnify him, And that thou shouldest set thy mind upon him,
asv.7:18: And that thou shouldest visit him every morning, And try him every moment?
asv.7:19: How long wilt thou not look away from me, Nor let me alone till I swallow down my spittle?
asv.7:20: If I have sinned, what do I unto thee, O thou watcher of men? Why hast thou set me as a mark for thee, So that I am a burden to myself?
asv.7:21: And why dost thou not pardon my transgression, and take away mine iniquity? For now shall I lie down in the dust; And thou wilt seek me diligently, but I shall not be.
asv.8:1: Then answered Bildad the Shuhite, and said,
asv.8:2: How long wilt thou speak these things? And how long shall the words of thy mouth be like a mighty wind?
asv.8:3: Doth God pervert justice? Or doth the Almighty pervert righteousness?
asv.8:4: If thy children have sinned against him, And he hath delivered them into the hand of their transgression;
asv.8:5: If thou wouldest seek diligently unto God, And make thy supplication to the Almighty;
asv.8:6: If thou wert pure and upright: Surely now he would awake for thee, And make the habitation of thy righteousness prosperous.
asv.8:7: And though thy beginning was small, Yet thy latter end would greatly increase.
asv.8:8: For inquire, I pray thee, of the former age, And apply thyself to that which their fathers have searched out
asv.8:9: (For we are but of yesterday, and know nothing, Because our days upon earth are a shadow);
asv.8:10: Shall not they teach thee, and tell thee, And utter words out of their heart?
asv.8:11: Can the rush grow up without mire? Can the flag grow without water?
asv.8:12: Whilst it is yet in its greenness, and not cut down, It withereth before any other herb.
asv.8:13: So are the paths of all that forget God; And the hope of the godless man shall perish:
asv.8:14: Whose confidence shall break in sunder, And whose trust is a spider’s web.
asv.8:15: He shall lean upon his house, but it shall not stand: He shall hold fast thereby, but it shall not endure.
asv.8:16: He is green before the sun, And his shoots go forth over his garden.
asv.8:17: His roots are wrapped about the stone -heap, He beholdeth the place of stones.
asv.8:18: If he be destroyed from his place, Then it shall deny him, saying, I have not seen thee.
asv.8:19: Behold, this is the joy of his way; And out of the earth shall others spring.
asv.8:20: Behold, God will not cast away a perfect man, Neither will he uphold the evil-doers.
asv.8:21: He will yet fill thy mouth with laughter, And thy lips with shouting.
asv.8:22: They that hate thee shall be clothed with shame; And the tent of the wicked shall be no more.
asv.9:2: Of a truth I know that it is so: But how can man be just with God?
asv.9:3: If he be pleased to contend with him, He cannot answer him one of a thousand.
asv.9:4: He is wise in heart, and mighty in strength: Who hath hardened himself against him, and prospered?—
asv.9:5: Him that removeth the mountains, and they know it not, When he overturneth them in his anger;
asv.9:6: That shaketh the earth out of its place, And the pillars thereof tremble;
asv.9:7: That commandeth the sun, and it riseth not, And sealeth up the stars;
asv.9:8: That alone stretcheth out the heavens, And treadeth upon the waves of the sea;
asv.9:9: That maketh the Bear, Orion, and the Pleiades, And the chambers of the south;
asv.9:10: That doeth great things past finding out, Yea, marvellous things without number.
asv.9:11: Lo, he goeth by me, and I see him not: He passeth on also, but I perceive him not.
asv.9:12: Behold, he seizeth the prey, who can hinder him? Who will say unto him, What doest thou?
asv.9:13: God will not withdraw his anger; The helpers of Rahab do stoop under him.
asv.9:14: How much less shall I answer him, And choose out my words to reason with him?
asv.9:15: Whom, though I were righteous, yet would I not answer; I would make supplication to my judge.
asv.9:16: If I had called, and he had answered me, Yet would I not believe that he hearkened unto my voice.
asv.9:17: For he breaketh me with a tempest, And multiplieth my wounds without cause.
asv.9:18: He will not suffer me to take my breath, But filleth me with bitterness.
asv.9:19: If we speak of strength, lo, he is mighty! And if of justice, Who, saith he, will summon me?
asv.9:20: Though I be righteous, mine own mouth shall condemn me: Though I be perfect, it shall prove me perverse.
asv.9:21: I am perfect; I regard not myself; I despise my life.
asv.9:22: It is all one; therefore I say, He destroyeth the perfect and the wicked.
asv.9:23: If the scourge slay suddenly, He will mock at the trial of the innocent.
asv.9:24: The earth is given into the hand of the wicked; He covereth the faces of the judges thereof: If it be not he, who then is it?
asv.9:25: Now my days are swifter than a post: They flee away, they see no good.
asv.9:26: They are passed away as the swift ships; As the eagle that swoopeth on the prey.
asv.9:27: If I say, I will forget my complaint, I will put off my sad countenance, and be of good cheer;
asv.9:28: I am afraid of all my sorrows, I know that thou wilt not hold me innocent.
asv.9:29: I shall be condemned; Why then do I labor in vain?
asv.9:30: If I wash myself with snow water, And make my hands never so clean;
asv.9:31: Yet wilt thou plunge me in the ditch, And mine own clothes shall abhor me.
asv.9:32: For he is not a man, as I am, that I should answer him, That we should come together in judgment.
asv.9:33: There is no umpire betwixt us, That might lay his hand upon us both.
asv.9:34: Let him take his rod away from me, And let not his terror make me afraid:
asv.9:35: Then would I speak, and not fear him; For I am not so in myself.
asv.10:1: My soul is weary of my life; I will give free course to my complaint; I will speak in the bitterness of my soul.
asv.10:2: I will say unto God, Do not condemn me; Show me wherefore thou contendest with me.
asv.10:3: Is it good unto thee that thou shouldest oppress, That thou shouldest despise the work of thy hands, And shine upon the counsel of the wicked?
asv.10:4: Hast thou eyes of flesh? Or seest thou as man seeth?
asv.10:5: Are thy days as the days of man, Or thy years as man’s days,
asv.10:6: That thou inquirest after mine iniquity, And searchest after my sin,
asv.10:7: Although thou knowest that I am not wicked, And there is none that can deliver out of thy hand?
asv.10:8: Thy hands have framed me and fashioned me Together round about; yet thou dost destroy me.
asv.10:9: Remember, I beseech thee, that thou hast fashioned me as clay; And wilt thou bring me into dust again?
asv.10:10: Hast thou not poured me out as milk, And curdled me like cheese?
asv.10:11: Thou hast clothed me with skin and flesh, And knit me together with bones and sinews.
asv.10:12: Thou hast granted me life and lovingkindness; And thy visitation hath preserved my spirit.
asv.10:13: Yet these things thou didst hide in thy heart; I know that this is with thee:
asv.10:14: If I sin, then thou markest me, And thou wilt not acquit me from mine iniquity.
asv.10:15: If I be wicked, woe unto me; And if I be righteous, yet shall I not lift up my head; Being filled with ignominy, And looking upon mine affliction.
asv.10:16: And if my head exalt itself, thou huntest me as a lion; And again thou showest thyself marvellous upon me.
asv.10:17: Thou renewest thy witnesses against me, And increasest thine indignation upon me: Changes and warfare are with me.
asv.10:18: Wherefore then hast thou brought me forth out of the womb? I had given up the ghost, and no eye had seen me.
asv.10:19: I should have been as though I had not been; I should have been carried from the womb to the grave.
asv.10:20: Are not my days few? cease then, And let me alone, that I may take comfort a little,
asv.10:21: Before I go whence I shall not return, Even to the land of darkness and of the shadow of death;
asv.10:22: The land dark as midnight, The land of the shadow of death, without any order, And where the light is as midnight.
asv.11:1: Then answered Zophar the Naamathite, and said,
asv.11:2: Should not the multitude of words be answered? And should a man full of talk be justified?
asv.11:3: Should thy boastings make men hold their peace? And when thou mockest, shall no man make thee ashamed?
asv.11:4: For thou sayest, My doctrine is pure, And I am clean in thine eyes.
asv.11:5: But oh that God would speak, And open his lips against thee,
asv.11:6: And that he would show thee the secrets of wisdom! For he is manifold in understanding. Know therefore that God exacteth of thee less than thine iniquity deserveth.
asv.11:7: Canst thou by searching find out God? Canst thou find out the Almighty unto perfection?
asv.11:8: It is high as heaven; what canst thou do? Deeper than Sheol; what canst thou know?
asv.11:9: The measure thereof is longer than the earth, And broader than the sea.
asv.11:10: If he pass through, and shut up, And call unto judgment, then who can hinder him?
asv.11:11: For he knoweth false men: He seeth iniquity also, even though he consider it not.
asv.11:12: But vain man is void of understanding, Yea, man is born as a wild ass’s colt.
asv.11:13: If thou set thy heart aright, And stretch out thy hands toward him;
asv.11:14: If iniquity be in thy hand, put it far away, And let not unrighteousness dwell in thy tents.
asv.11:15: Surely then shalt thou lift up thy face without spot; Yea, thou shalt be stedfast, and shalt not fear:
asv.11:16: For thou shalt forget thy misery; Thou shalt remember it as waters that are passed away,
asv.11:17: And thy life shall be clearer than the noonday; Though there be darkness, it shall be as the morning.
asv.11:18: And thou shalt be secure, because there is hope; Yea, thou shalt search about thee, and shalt take thy rest in safety.
asv.11:19: Also thou shalt lie down, and none shall make thee afraid; Yea, many shall make suit unto thee.
asv.11:20: But the eyes of the wicked shall fail, And they shall have no way to flee; And their hope shall be the giving up of the ghost.
asv.12:2: No doubt but ye are the people, And wisdom shall die with you.
asv.12:3: But I have understanding as well as you; I am not inferior to you: Yea, who knoweth not such things as these?
asv.12:4: I am as one that is a laughing-stock to his neighbor, I who called upon God, and he answered: The just, the perfect man is a laughing-stock.
asv.12:5: In the thought of him that is at ease there is contempt for misfortune; It is ready for them whose foot slippeth.
asv.12:6: The tents of robbers prosper, And they that provoke God are secure; Into whose hand God bringeth abundantly.
asv.12:7: But ask now the beasts, and they shall teach thee; And the birds of the heavens, and they shall tell thee:
asv.12:8: Or speak to the earth, and it shall teach thee; And the fishes of the sea shall declare unto thee.
asv.12:9: Who knoweth not in all these, That the hand of Jehovah hath wrought this,
asv.12:10: In whose hand is the soul of every living thing, And the breath of all mankind?
asv.12:11: Doth not the ear try words, Even as the palate tasteth its food?
asv.12:12: With aged men is wisdom, And in length of days understanding.
asv.12:13: With God is wisdom and might; He hath counsel and understanding.
asv.12:14: Behold, he breaketh down, and it cannot be built again; He shutteth up a man, and there can be no opening.
asv.12:15: Behold, he withholdeth the waters, and they dry up; Again, he sendeth them out, and they overturn the earth.
asv.12:16: With him is strength and wisdom; The deceived and the deceiver are his.
asv.12:17: He leadeth counsellors away stripped, And judges maketh he fools.
asv.12:18: He looseth the bond of kings, And he bindeth their loins with a girdle.
asv.12:19: He leadeth priests away stripped, And overthroweth the mighty.
asv.12:20: He removeth the speech of the trusty, And taketh away the understanding of the elders.
asv.12:21: He poureth contempt upon princes, And looseth the belt of the strong.
asv.12:22: He uncovereth deep things out of darkness, And bringeth out to light the shadow of death.
asv.12:23: He increaseth the nations, and he destroyeth them: He enlargeth the nations, and he leadeth them captive.
asv.12:24: He taketh away understanding from the chiefs of the people of the earth, And causeth them to wander in a wilderness where there is no way.
asv.12:25: They grope in the dark without light; And he maketh them to stagger like a drunken man.
asv.13:1: Lo, mine eye hath seen all this, Mine ear hath heard and understood it.
asv.13:2: What ye know, the same do I know also: I am not inferior unto you.
asv.13:3: Surely I would speak to the Almighty, And I desire to reason with God.
asv.13:4: But ye are forgers of lies; Ye are all physicians of no value.
asv.13:5: Oh that ye would altogether hold your peace! And it would be your wisdom.
asv.13:6: Hear now my reasoning, And hearken to the pleadings of my lips.
asv.13:7: Will ye speak unrighteously for God, And talk deceitfully for him?
asv.13:8: Will ye show partiality to him? Will ye contend for God?
asv.13:9: Is it good that he should search you out? Or as one deceiveth a man, will ye deceive him?
asv.13:10: He will surely reprove you, If ye do secretly show partiality.
asv.13:11: Shall not his majesty make you afraid, And his dread fall upon you?
asv.13:12: Your memorable sayings are proverbs of ashes, Your defences are defences of clay.
asv.13:13: Hold your peace, let me alone, that I may speak; And let come on me what will.
asv.13:14: Wherefore should I take my flesh in my teeth, And put my life in my hand?
asv.13:15: Behold, he will slay me; I have no hope: Nevertheless I will maintain my ways before him.
asv.13:16: This also shall be my salvation, That a godless man shall not come before him.
asv.13:17: Hear diligently my speech, And let my declaration be in your ears.
asv.13:18: Behold now, I have set my cause in order; I know that I am righteous.
asv.13:19: Who is he that will contend with me? For then would I hold my peace and give up the ghost.
asv.13:20: Only do not two things unto me; Then will I not hide myself from thy face:
asv.13:21: Withdraw thy hand far from me; And let not thy terror make me afraid.
asv.13:22: Then call thou, and I will answer; Or let me speak, and answer thou me.
asv.13:23: How many are mine iniquities and sins? Make me to know my transgression and my sin.
asv.13:24: Wherefore hidest thou thy face, And holdest me for thine enemy?
asv.13:25: Wilt thou harass a driven leaf? And wilt thou pursue the dry stubble?
asv.13:26: For thou writest bitter things against me, And makest me to inherit the iniquities of my youth:
asv.13:27: Thou puttest my feet also in the stocks, And markest all my paths; Thou settest a bound to the soles of my feet:
asv.13:28: Though I am like a rotten thing that consumeth, Like a garment that is moth-eaten.
asv.14:1: Man, that is born of a woman, Is of few days, and full of trouble.
asv.14:2: He cometh forth like a flower, and is cut down: He fleeth also as a shadow, and continueth not.
asv.14:3: And dost thou open thine eyes upon such a one, And bringest me into judgment with thee?
asv.14:4: Who can bring a clean thing out of an unclean? not one.
asv.14:5: Seeing his days are determined, The number of his months is with thee, And thou hast appointed his bounds that he cannot pass;
asv.14:6: Look away from him, that he may rest, Till he shall accomplish, as a hireling, his day.
asv.14:7: For there is hope of a tree, If it be cut down, that it will sprout again, And that the tender branch thereof will not cease.
asv.14:8: Though the root thereof wax old in the earth, And the stock thereof die in the ground;
asv.14:9: Yet through the scent of water it will bud, And put forth boughs like a plant.
asv.14:10: But man dieth, and is laid low: Yea, man giveth up the ghost, and where is he?
asv.14:11: As the waters fail from the sea, And the river wasteth and drieth up;
asv.14:12: So man lieth down and riseth not: Till the heavens be no more, they shall not awake, Nor be roused out of their sleep.
asv.14:13: Oh that thou wouldest hide me in Sheol, That thou wouldest keep me secret, until thy wrath be past, That thou wouldest appoint me a set time, and remember me!
asv.14:14: If a man die, shall he live again? All the days of my warfare would I wait, Till my release should come.
asv.14:15: Thou wouldest call, and I would answer thee: Thou wouldest have a desire to the work of thy hands.
asv.14:16: But now thou numberest my steps: Dost thou not watch over my sin?
asv.14:17: My transgression is sealed up in a bag, And thou fastenest up mine iniquity.
asv.14:18: But the mountain falling cometh to nought; And the rock is removed out of its place;
asv.14:19: The waters wear the stones; The overflowings thereof wash away the dust of the earth: So thou destroyest the hope of man.
asv.14:20: Thou prevailest for ever against him, and he passeth; Thou changest his countenance, and sendest him away.
asv.14:21: His sons come to honor, and he knoweth it not; And they are brought low, but he perceiveth it not of them.
asv.14:22: But his flesh upon him hath pain, And his soul within him mourneth.
asv.15:1: Then answered Eliphaz the Temanite, and said,
asv.15:2: Should a wise man make answer with vain knowledge, And fill himself with the east wind?
asv.15:3: Should he reason with unprofitable talk, Or with speeches wherewith he can do no good?
asv.15:4: Yea, thou doest away with fear, And hinderest devotion before God.
asv.15:5: For thine iniquity teacheth thy mouth, And thou choosest the tongue of the crafty.
asv.15:6: Thine own mouth condemneth thee, and not I; Yea, thine own lips testify against thee.
asv.15:7: Art thou the first man that was born? Or wast thou brought forth before the hills?
asv.15:8: Hast thou heard the secret counsel of God? And dost thou limit wisdom to thyself?
asv.15:9: What knowest thou, that we know not? What understandest thou, which is not in us?
asv.15:10: With us are both the gray-headed and the very aged men, Much elder than thy father.
asv.15:11: Are the consolations of God too small for thee, Even the word that is gentle toward thee?
asv.15:12: Why doth thy heart carry thee away? And why do thine eyes flash,
asv.15:13: That against God thou turnest thy spirit, And lettest words go out of thy mouth?
asv.15:14: What is man, that he should be clean? And he that is born of a woman, that he should be righteous?
asv.15:15: Behold, he putteth no trust in his holy ones; Yea, the heavens are not clean in his sight:
asv.15:16: How much less one that is abominable and corrupt, A man that drinketh iniquity like water!
asv.15:17: I will show thee, hear thou me; And that which I have seen I will declare
asv.15:18: (Which wise men have told From their fathers, and have not hid it;
asv.15:19: Unto whom alone the land was given, And no stranger passed among them):
asv.15:20: The wicked man travaileth with pain all his days, Even the number of years that are laid up for the oppressor.
asv.15:21: A sound of terrors is in his ears; In prosperity the destroyer shall come upon him.
asv.15:22: He believeth not that he shall return out of darkness, And he is waited for of the sword.
asv.15:23: He wandereth abroad for bread, saying, Where is it? He knoweth that the day of darkness is ready at his hand.
asv.15:24: Distress and anguish make him afraid; They prevail against him, as a king ready to the battle.
