ylt.5:5: Whose harvest the hungry doth eat, And even from the thorns taketh it, And the designing swallowed their wealth.
ylt.5:6: For sorrow cometh not forth from the dust, Nor from the ground springeth up misery.
ylt.5:7: For man to misery is born, And the sparks go high to fly.
ylt.5:8: Yet I--I inquire for God, And for God I give my word,
ylt.5:9: Doing great things, and there is no searching. Wonderful, till there is no numbering.
ylt.5:10: Who is giving rain on the face of the land, And is sending waters on the out-places.
ylt.5:11: To set the low on a high place, And the mourners have been high in safety.
ylt.5:12: Making void thoughts of the subtile, And their hands do not execute wisdom.
ylt.5:13: Capturing the wise in their subtilty, And the counsel of wrestling ones was hastened,
ylt.5:14: By day they meet darkness, And as night--they grope at noon.
ylt.5:15: And He saveth the wasted from their mouth, And from a strong hand the needy,
ylt.5:16: And there is hope to the poor, And perverseness hath shut her mouth.
ylt.5:17: Lo, the happiness of mortal man, God doth reprove him: And the chastisement of the Mighty despise not,
ylt.5:18: For He doth pain, and He bindeth up, He smiteth, and His hands heal.
ylt.5:19: In six distresses He delivereth thee, And in seven evil striketh not on thee.
ylt.5:20: In famine He hath redeemed thee from death, And in battle from the hands of the sword.
ylt.5:21: When the tongue scourgeth thou art hid, And thou art not afraid of destruction, When it cometh.
ylt.5:22: At destruction and at hunger thou mockest, And of the beast of the earth, Thou art not afraid.
ylt.5:23: (For with sons of the field is thy covenant, And the beast of the field Hath been at peace with thee.)
ylt.5:24: And thou hast known that thy tent is peace, And inspected thy habitation, and errest not,
ylt.5:25: And hast known that numerous is Thy seed, And thine offspring as the herb of the earth;
ylt.5:26: Thou comest in full age unto the grave, As the going up of a stalk in its season.
ylt.5:27: Lo, this--we searched it out--it is right, hearken; And thou, know for thyself!
ylt.6:2: O that my provocation were thoroughly weighed, And my calamity in balances They would lift up together!
ylt.6:3: For now, than the sands of the sea it is heavier, Therefore my words have been rash.
ylt.6:4: For arrows of the Mighty are with me, Whose poison is drinking up my spirit. Terrors of God array themselves for me!
ylt.6:5: Brayeth a wild ass over tender grass? Loweth an ox over his provender?
ylt.6:6: Eaten is an insipid thing without salt? Is there sense in the drivel of dreams?
ylt.6:7: My soul is refusing to touch! They are as my sickening food.
ylt.6:8: O that my request may come, That God may grant my hope!
ylt.6:9: That God would please--and bruise me, Loose His hand and cut me off!
ylt.6:10: And yet it is my comfort, (And I exult in pain--He doth not spare,) That I have not hidden The sayings of the Holy One.
ylt.6:11: What is my power that I should hope? And what mine end That I should prolong my life?
ylt.6:12: Is my strength the strength of stones? Is my flesh brazen?
ylt.6:13: Is not my help with me, And substance driven from me?
ylt.6:14: To a despiser of his friends is shame, And the fear of the Mighty he forsaketh.
ylt.6:15: My brethren have deceived as a brook, As a stream of brooks they pass away.
ylt.6:16: That are black because of ice, By them doth snow hide itself.
ylt.6:17: By the time they are warm they have been cut off, By its being hot they have been Extinguished from their place.
ylt.6:18: Turn aside do the paths of their way, They ascend into emptiness, and are lost.
ylt.6:19: Passengers of Tema looked expectingly, Travellers of Sheba hoped for them.
ylt.6:20: They were ashamed that one hath trusted, They have come unto it and are confounded.
ylt.6:21: Surely now ye have become the same! Ye see a downfall, and are afraid.
ylt.6:22: Is it because I said, Give to me? And, By your power bribe for me?
ylt.6:23: And, Deliver me from the hand of an adversary? And, From the hand of terrible ones ransom me?
ylt.6:24: Shew me, and I--I keep silent, And what I have erred, let me understand.
ylt.6:25: How powerful have been upright sayings, And what doth reproof from you reprove?
ylt.6:26: For reproof--do you reckon words? And for wind--sayings of the desperate.
ylt.6:27: Anger on the fatherless ye cause to fall, And are strange to your friend.
ylt.6:28: And, now, please, look upon me, Even to your face do I lie?
ylt.6:29: Turn back, I pray you, let it not be perverseness, Yea, turn back again--my righteousness is in it.
ylt.6:30: Is there in my tongue perverseness? Discerneth not my palate desirable things?
ylt.7:1: Is there not a warfare to man on earth? And as the days of an hireling his days?
ylt.7:2: As a servant desireth the shadow, And as a hireling expecteth his wage,
ylt.7:3: So I have been caused to inherit months of vanity, And nights of misery they numbered to me.
ylt.7:4: If I lay down then I said, `When do I rise!' And evening hath been measured, And I have been full of tossings till dawn.
ylt.7:5: Clothed hath been my flesh with worms, And a clod of dust, My skin hath been shrivelled and is loathsome,
ylt.7:6: My days swifter than a weaving machine, And they are consumed without hope.
ylt.7:7: Remember Thou that my life is a breath, Mine eye turneth not back to see good.
ylt.7:8: The eye of my beholder beholdeth me not. Thine eyes are upon me--and I am not.
ylt.7:9: Consumed hath been a cloud, and it goeth, So he who is going down to Sheol cometh not up.
ylt.7:10: He turneth not again to his house, Nor doth his place discern him again.
ylt.7:11: Also I--I withhold not my mouth--I speak in the distress of my spirit, I talk in the bitterness of my soul.
ylt.7:12: A sea- monster am I, or a dragon, That thou settest over me a guard?
ylt.7:13: When I said, `My bed doth comfort me,' He taketh away in my talking my couch.
ylt.7:14: And thou hast affrighted me with dreams, And from visions thou terrifiest me,
ylt.7:15: And my soul chooseth strangling, Death rather than my bones.
ylt.7:16: I have wasted away--not to the age do I live. Cease from me, for my days are vanity.
ylt.7:17: What is man that Thou dost magnify him? And that Thou settest unto him Thy heart?
ylt.7:18: And inspectest him in the mornings, In the evenings dost try him?
ylt.7:19: How long dost Thou not look from me? Thou dost not desist till I swallow my spittle.
ylt.7:20: I have sinned, what do I to Thee, O watcher of man? Why hast Thou set me for a mark to Thee, And I am for a burden to myself--and what?
ylt.7:21: Thou dost not take away my transgression, And cause to pass away mine iniquity, Because now, for dust I lie down: And Thou hast sought me--and I am not!
ylt.8:1: And Bildad the Shuhite answereth and saith: --
ylt.8:2: Till when dost thou speak these things? And a strong wind--sayings of thy mouth?
ylt.8:3: Doth God pervert judgment? And doth the Mighty One pervert justice?
ylt.8:4: If thy sons have sinned before Him, And He doth send them away, By the hand of their transgression,
ylt.8:5: If thou dost seek early unto God, And unto the Mighty makest supplication,
ylt.8:6: If pure and upright thou art, Surely now He waketh for thee, And hath completed The habitation of thy righteousness.
ylt.8:7: And thy beginning hath been small, And thy latter end is very great.
ylt.8:8: For, ask I pray thee of a former generation, And prepare to a search of their fathers,
ylt.8:9: (For of yesterday we are, and we know not, For a shadow are our days on earth.)
ylt.8:10: Do they not shew thee--speak to thee, And from their heart bring forth words?
ylt.8:11: `Doth a rush wise without mire? A reed increase without water?
ylt.8:12: While it is in its budding--uncropped, Even before any herb it withereth.
ylt.8:13: So are the paths of all forgetting God, And the hope of the profane doth perish,
ylt.8:14: Whose confidence is loathsome, And the house of a spider his trust.
ylt.8:15: He leaneth on his house--and it standeth not: He taketh hold on it--and it abideth not.
ylt.8:16: Green he is before the sun, And over his garden his branch goeth out.
ylt.8:17: By a heap his roots are wrapped, A house of stones he looketh for.
ylt.8:18: If one doth destroy him from his place, Then it hath feigned concerning him, I have not seen thee!
ylt.8:19: Lo, this is the joy of his way, And from the dust others spring up.'
ylt.8:20: Lo, God doth not reject the perfect, Nor taketh hold on the hand of evil doers.
ylt.8:21: While he filleth with laughter thy mouth, And thy lips with shouting,
ylt.8:22: Those hating thee do put on shame, And the tent of the wicked is not!
ylt.9:2: Truly I have known that it is so, And what--is man righteous with God?
ylt.9:3: If he delight to strive with Him--He doth not answer him one of a thousand.
ylt.9:4: Wise in heart and strong in power--Who hath hardened toward Him and is at peace?
ylt.9:5: Who is removing mountains, And they have not known, Who hath overturned them in His anger.
ylt.9:6: Who is shaking earth from its place, And its pillars move themselves.
ylt.9:7: Who is speaking to the sun, and it riseth not, And the stars He sealeth up.
ylt.9:8: Stretching out the heavens by Himself, And treading on the heights of the sea,
ylt.9:9: Making Osh, Kesil, and Kimah, And the inner chambers of the south.
ylt.9:10: Doing great things till there is no searching, And wonderful, till there is no numbering.
ylt.9:11: Lo, He goeth over by me, and I see not, And He passeth on, and I attend not to it.
ylt.9:12: Lo, He snatches away, who bringeth it back? Who saith unto Him, `What dost Thou?'
ylt.9:13: God doth not turn back His anger, Under Him bowed have proud helpers.
ylt.9:14: How much less do I--I answer Him? Choose out my words with Him?
ylt.9:15: Whom, though I were righteous, I answer not, For my judgment I make supplication.
ylt.9:16: Though I had called and He answereth me, I do not believe that He giveth ear to my voice.
ylt.9:17: Because with a tempest He bruiseth me, And hath multiplied my wounds for nought.
ylt.9:18: He permitteth me not to refresh my spirit, But filleth me with bitter things.
ylt.9:19: If of power, lo, the Strong One; And if of judgment--who doth convene me?
ylt.9:20: If I be righteous, Mine mouth doth declare me wicked, Perfect I am! --it declareth me perverse.
ylt.9:21: Perfect I am! --I know not my soul, I despise my life.
ylt.9:22: It is the same thing, therefore I said, `The perfect and the wicked He is consuming.'
ylt.9:23: If a scourge doth put to death suddenly, At the trial of the innocent He laugheth.
ylt.9:24: Earth hath been given Into the hand of the wicked one. The face of its judges he covereth, If not--where, who is he?
ylt.9:25: My days have been swifter than a runner, They have fled, they have not seen good,
ylt.9:26: They have passed on with ships of reed, As an eagle darteth on food.
ylt.9:27: Though I say, `I forget my talking, I forsake my corner, and I brighten up!'
ylt.9:28: I have been afraid of all my griefs, I have known that Thou dost not acquit me.
ylt.9:29: I--I am become wicked; why is this? In vain I labour.
ylt.9:30: If I have washed myself with snow-water, And purified with soap my hands,
ylt.9:31: Then in corruption Thou dost dip me, And my garments have abominated me.
ylt.9:32: But if a man like myself--I answer him, We come together into judgment.
ylt.9:33: If there were between us an umpire, He doth place his hand on us both.
ylt.9:34: He doth turn aside from off me his rod, And His terror doth not make me afraid,
ylt.9:35: I speak, and do not fear Him, But I am not right with myself.
ylt.10:1: My soul hath been weary of my life, I leave off my talking to myself, I speak in the bitterness of my soul.
ylt.10:2: I say unto God, `Do not condemn me, Let me know why Thou dost strive with me.
ylt.10:3: Is it good for Thee that Thou dost oppress? That Thou despisest the labour of Thy hands, And on the counsel of the wicked hast shone?
ylt.10:4: Eyes of flesh hast Thou? As man seeth--seest Thou?
ylt.10:5: As the days of man are Thy days? Thy years as the days of a man?
ylt.10:6: That Thou inquirest for mine iniquity, And for my sin seekest?
ylt.10:7: For Thou knowest that I am not wicked, And there is no deliverer from Thy hand.
ylt.10:8: Thy hands have taken pains about me, And they make me together round about, And Thou swallowest me up!
ylt.10:9: Remember, I pray Thee, That as clay Thou hast made me, And unto dust Thou dost bring me back.
ylt.10:10: Dost Thou not as milk pour me out? And as cheese curdle me?
ylt.10:11: Skin and flesh Thou dost put on me, And with bones and sinews dost fence me.
ylt.10:12: Life and kindness Thou hast done with me. And Thy inspection hath preserved my spirit.
ylt.10:13: And these Thou hast laid up in Thy heart, I have known that this is with Thee.
ylt.10:14: If I sinned, then Thou hast observed me, And from mine iniquity dost not acquit me,
ylt.10:15: If I have done wickedly--woe to me, And righteously--I lift not up my head, Full of shame--then see my affliction,
ylt.10:16: And it riseth--as a lion Thou huntest me. And Thou turnest back--Thou shewest Thyself wonderful in me.
ylt.10:17: Thou renewest Thy witnesses against me, And dost multiply Thine anger with me, Changes and warfare are with me.
ylt.10:18: And why from the womb Hast Thou brought me forth? I expire, and the eye doth not see me.
ylt.10:19: As I had not been, I am, From the belly to the grave I am brought,
ylt.10:20: Are not my days few? Cease then, and put from me, And I brighten up a little,
ylt.10:21: Before I go, and return not, Unto a land of darkness and death-shade,
ylt.10:22: A land of obscurity as thick darkness, Death-shade--and no order, And the shining is as thick darkness.'
ylt.11:1: And Zophar the Naamathite answereth and saith: --
ylt.11:2: Is a multitude of words not answered? And is a man of lips justified?
ylt.11:3: Thy devices make men keep silent, Thou scornest, and none is causing blushing!
ylt.11:4: And thou sayest, `Pure is my discourse, And clean I have been in Thine eyes.'
ylt.11:5: And yet, O that God had spoken! And doth open His lips with thee.
ylt.11:6: And declare to thee secrets of wisdom, For counsel hath foldings. And know thou that God forgetteth for thee, Some of thine iniquity.
ylt.11:7: By searching dost thou find out God? Unto perfection find out the Mighty One?
ylt.11:8: Heights of the heavens! --what dost thou? Deeper than Sheol! --what knowest thou?
ylt.11:9: Longer than earth is its measure, And broader than the sea.
ylt.11:10: If He pass on, and shut up, and assemble, Who then dost reverse it?
ylt.11:11: For he hath known men of vanity, And He seeth iniquity, And one doth not consider it!
ylt.11:12: And empty man is bold, And the colt of a wild ass man is born.
ylt.11:13: If thou--thou hast prepared thy heart, And hast spread out unto Him thy hands,
ylt.11:14: If iniquity is in thy hand, put it far off, And let not perverseness dwell in thy tents.
ylt.11:15: For then thou liftest up thy face from blemish, And thou hast been firm, and fearest not.
ylt.11:16: For thou dost forget misery, As waters passed away thou rememberest.
ylt.11:17: And above the noon doth age rise, Thou fliest--as the morning thou art.
ylt.11:18: And thou hast trusted because their is hope, And searched--in confidence thou liest down,
ylt.11:19: And thou hast rested, And none is causing trembling, And many have entreated thy face;
ylt.11:20: And the eyes of the wicked are consumed, And refuge hath perished from them, And their hope is a breathing out of soul!
ylt.12:2: Truly--ye are the people, And with you doth wisdom die.
ylt.12:3: I also have a heart like you, I am not fallen more than you, And with whom is there not like these?
ylt.12:4: A laughter to his friend I am: `He calleth to God, and He answereth him,' A laughter is the perfect righteous one.
ylt.12:5: A torch--despised in the thoughts of the secure Is prepared for those sliding with the feet.
ylt.12:6: At peace are the tents of spoilers, And those provoking God have confidence, He into whose hand God hath brought.
ylt.12:7: And yet, ask, I pray thee, One of the beasts, and it doth shew thee, And a fowl of the heavens, And it doth declare to thee.
ylt.12:8: Or talk to the earth, and it sheweth thee, And fishes of the sea recount to thee:
ylt.12:9: `Who hath not known in all these, That the hand of Jehovah hath done this?
ylt.12:10: In whose hand is the breath of every living thing, And the spirit of all flesh of man.'
ylt.12:11: Doth not the ear try words? And the palate taste food for itself?
ylt.12:12: With the very aged is wisdom, And with length of days understanding.
ylt.12:13: With Him are wisdom and might, To him are counsel and understanding.
ylt.12:14: Lo, He breaketh down, and it is not built up, He shutteth against a man, And it is not opened.
ylt.12:15: Lo, He keepeth in the waters, and they are dried up, And he sendeth them forth, And they overturn the land.
ylt.12:16: With Him are strength and wisdom, His the deceived and deceiver.
ylt.12:17: Causing counsellors to go away a spoil, And judges He maketh foolish.
ylt.12:18: The bands of kings He hath opened, And He bindeth a girdle on their loins.
ylt.12:19: Causing ministers to go away a spoil And strong ones He overthroweth.
ylt.12:20: Turning aside the lip of the stedfast, And the reason of the aged He taketh away.
ylt.12:21: Pouring contempt upon princes, And the girdle of the mighty He made feeble.
ylt.12:22: Removing deep things out of darkness, And He bringeth out to light death-shade.
ylt.12:23: Magnifying the nations, and He destroyeth them, Spreading out the nations, and He quieteth them.
ylt.12:24: Turning aside the heart Of the heads of the people of the land, And he causeth them to wander In vacancy--no way!
ylt.12:25: They feel darkness, and not light, He causeth them to wander as a drunkard.
ylt.13:1: Lo, all--hath mine eye seen, Heard hath mine ear, and it attendeth to it.
ylt.13:2: According to your knowledge I have known--also I. I am not fallen more than you.
ylt.13:3: Yet I for the Mighty One do speak, And to argue for God I delight.
ylt.13:4: And yet, ye are forgers of falsehood, Physicians of nought--all of you,
ylt.13:5: O that ye would keep perfectly silent, And it would be to you for wisdom.
ylt.13:6: Hear, I pray you, my argument, And to the pleadings of my lips attend,
ylt.13:7: For God do ye speak perverseness? And for Him do ye speak deceit?
ylt.13:8: His face do ye accept, if for God ye strive?
ylt.13:9: Is it good that He doth search you, If, as one mocketh at a man, ye mock at Him?
ylt.13:10: He doth surely reprove you, if in secret ye accept faces.
ylt.13:11: Doth not His excellency terrify you? And His dread fall upon you?
ylt.13:12: Your remembrances are similes of ashes, For high places of clay your heights.
ylt.13:13: Keep silent from me, and I speak, And pass over me doth what?
ylt.13:14: Wherefore do I take my flesh in my teeth? And my soul put in my hand?
ylt.13:15: Lo, He doth slay me--I wait not! Only, my ways unto His face I argue.
ylt.13:16: Also--He is to me for salvation, For the profane cometh not before Him.
ylt.13:17: Hear ye diligently my word, And my declaration with your ears.
ylt.13:18: Lo, I pray you, I have set in order the cause, I have known that I am righteous.
ylt.13:19: Who is he that doth strive with me? For now I keep silent and gasp.
ylt.13:20: Only two things, O God, do with me: Then from Thy face I am not hidden.
ylt.13:21: Thy hand put far off from me, And Thy terror let not terrify me.
ylt.13:22: And call Thou, and I--I answer, Or--I speak, and answer Thou me.
ylt.13:23: How many iniquities and sins have I? My transgression and my sin let me know.
ylt.13:24: Why dost Thou hide Thy face? And reckonest me for an enemy to Thee?
ylt.13:25: A leaf driven away dost Thou terrify? And the dry stubble dost Thou pursue?
ylt.13:26: For Thou writest against me bitter things, And causest me to possess iniquities of my youth:
ylt.13:27: And puttest in the stocks my feet, And observest all my paths, On the roots of my feet Thou settest a print,
ylt.13:28: And he, as a rotten thing, weareth away, As a garment hath a moth consumed him.
ylt.14:1: Man, born of woman! Of few days, and full of trouble!
ylt.14:2: As a flower he hath gone forth, and is cut off, And he fleeth as a shadow and standeth not.
ylt.14:3: Also--on this Thou hast opened Thine eyes, And dost bring me into judgment with Thee.
ylt.14:4: Who giveth a clean thing out of an unclean? not one.
ylt.14:5: If determined are his days, The number of his months are with Thee, His limit Thou hast made, And he passeth not over;
ylt.14:6: Look away from off him that he may cease, Till he enjoy as an hireling his day.
ylt.14:7: For there is of a tree hope, if it be cut down, That again it doth change, That its tender branch doth not cease.
ylt.14:8: If its root becometh old in the earth, And its stem doth die in the dust,
ylt.14:9: From the fragrance of water it doth flourish, And hath made a crop as a plant.
ylt.14:10: And a man dieth, and becometh weak, And man expireth, and where is he?
ylt.14:11: Waters have gone away from a sea, And a river becometh waste and dry.
ylt.14:12: And man hath lain down, and riseth not, Till the wearing out of the heavens they awake not, Nor are roused from their sleep.
ylt.14:13: O that in Sheol Thou wouldest conceal me, Hide me till the turning of Thine anger, Set for me a limit, and remember me.
ylt.14:14: If a man dieth--doth he revive? All days of my warfare I wait, till my change come.
ylt.14:15: Thou dost call, and I--I answer Thee; To the work of Thy hands Thou hast desire.
ylt.14:16: But now, my steps Thou numberest, Thou dost not watch over my sin.
ylt.14:17: Sealed up in a bag is my transgression, And Thou sewest up mine iniquity.
ylt.14:18: And yet, a falling mountain wasteth away, And a rock is removed from its place.
ylt.14:19: Stones have waters worn away, Their outpourings wash away the dust of earth, And the hope of man Thou hast destroyed.
ylt.14:20: Thou prevailest over him for ever, and he goeth, He is changing his countenance, And Thou sendest him away.
ylt.14:21: Honoured are his sons, and he knoweth not; And they are little, and he attendeth not to them.
ylt.14:22: Only--his flesh for him is pained, And his soul for him doth mourn.'
ylt.15:1: And Eliphaz the Temanite answereth and saith: --
ylt.15:2: Doth a wise man answer with vain knowledge? And fill with an east wind his belly?
ylt.15:3: To reason with a word not useful? And speeches--no profit in them?
ylt.15:4: Yea, thou dost make reverence void, And dost diminish meditation before God.
ylt.15:5: For thy mouth teacheth thine iniquity, And thou chooseth the tongue of the subtile.
ylt.15:6: Thy mouth declareth thee wicked, and not I, And thy lips testify against thee.
ylt.15:7: The first man art thou born? And before the heights wast thou formed?
ylt.15:8: Of the secret counsel of God dost thou hear? And withdrawest thou unto thee wisdom?
ylt.15:9: What hast thou known, and we know not? Understandest thou--and it is not with us?
ylt.15:10: Both the gray-headed And the very aged are among us--Greater than thy father in days.
ylt.15:11: Too few for thee are the comforts of God? And a gentle word is with thee,
ylt.15:12: What--doth thine heart take thee away? And what--are thine eyes high?
ylt.15:13: For thou turnest against God thy spirit? And hast brought out words from thy mouth:
ylt.15:14: What is man that he is pure, And that he is righteous, one born of woman?
ylt.15:15: Lo, in His holy ones He putteth no credence, And the heavens have not been pure in His eyes.
ylt.15:16: Also--surely abominable and filthy Is man drinking as water perverseness.
ylt.15:17: I shew thee--hearken to me--And this I have seen and declare:
ylt.15:18: Which the wise declare--And have not hid--from their fathers.
ylt.15:19: To them alone was the land given, And a stranger passed not over into their midst:
ylt.15:20: `All days of the wicked he is paining himself, And few years have been laid up for the terrible one.
ylt.15:21: A fearful voice is in his ears, In peace doth a destroyer come to him.
ylt.15:22: He believeth not to return from darkness, And watched is he for the sword.
ylt.15:23: He is wandering for bread--`Where is it?' He hath known that ready at his hand Is a day of darkness.
ylt.15:24: Terrify him do adversity and distress, They prevail over him As a king ready for a boaster.
ylt.15:25: For he stretched out against God his hand, And against the Mighty he maketh himself mighty.
ylt.15:26: He runneth unto Him with a neck, With thick bosses of his shields.
ylt.15:27: For he hath covered his face with his fat, And maketh vigour over his confidence.
ylt.15:28: And he inhabiteth cities cut off, houses not dwelt in, That have been ready to become heaps.
ylt.15:29: He is not rich, nor doth his wealth rise, Nor doth he stretch out on earth their continuance.
ylt.15:30: He turneth not aside from darkness, His tender branch doth a flame dry up, And he turneth aside at the breath of His mouth!
ylt.15:31: Let him not put credence in vanity, He hath been deceived, For vanity is his recompence.
ylt.15:32: Not in his day is it completed, And his bending branch is not green.
ylt.15:33: He shaketh off as a vine his unripe fruit, And casteth off as an olive his blossom.
ylt.15:34: For the company of the profane is gloomy, And fire hath consumed tents of bribery.
ylt.15:35: To conceive misery, and to bear iniquity, Even their heart doth prepare deceit.
ylt.16:2: I have heard many such things, Miserable comforters are ye all.
ylt.16:3: Is there an end to words of wind? Or what doth embolden thee that thou answerest?
ylt.16:4: I also, like you, might speak, If your soul were in my soul's stead. I might join against you with words, And nod at you with my head.
ylt.16:5: I might harden you with my mouth, And the moving of my lips might be sparing.
ylt.16:6: If I speak, my pain is not restrained, And I cease--what goeth from me?
ylt.16:7: Only, now, it hath wearied me; Thou hast desolated all my company,
ylt.16:8: And Thou dost loathe me, For a witness it hath been, And rise up against me doth my failure, In my face it testifieth.
ylt.16:9: His anger hath torn, and he hateth me, He hath gnashed at me with his teeth, My adversary sharpeneth his eyes for me.
ylt.16:10: They have gaped on me with their mouth, In reproach they have smitten my cheeks, Together against me they set themselves.
ylt.16:11: God shutteth me up unto the perverse, And to the hands of the wicked turneth me over.
ylt.16:12: At ease I have been, and he breaketh me, And he hath laid hold on my neck, And he breaketh me in pieces, And he raiseth me to him for a mark.
ylt.16:13: Go round against me do his archers. He splitteth my reins, and spareth not, He poureth out to the earth my gall.
ylt.16:14: He breaketh me--breach upon breach, He runneth upon me as a mighty one.
ylt.16:15: Sackcloth I have sewed on my skin, And have rolled in the dust my horn.
ylt.16:16: My face is foul with weeping, And on mine eyelids is death-shade.
ylt.16:17: Not for violence in my hands, And my prayer is pure.
ylt.16:18: O earth, do not thou cover my blood! And let there not be a place for my cry.
ylt.16:19: Also, now, lo, in the heavens is my witness, And my testifier in the high places.
ylt.16:20: My interpreter is my friend, Unto God hath mine eye dropped:
ylt.16:21: And he reasoneth for a man with God, And a son of man for his friend.
ylt.16:22: When a few years do come, Then a path I return not do I go.
ylt.17:1: My spirit hath been destroyed, My days extinguished--graves are for me.
ylt.17:2: If not--mockeries are with me. And in their provocations mine eye lodgeth.
ylt.17:3: Place, I pray Thee, my pledge with Thee; Who is he that striketh hand with me?
ylt.17:4: For their heart Thou hast hidden From understanding, Therefore Thou dost not exalt them.
ylt.17:5: For a portion he sheweth friendship, And the eyes of his sons are consumed.
ylt.17:6: And he set me up for a proverb of the peoples, And a wonder before them I am.
ylt.17:7: And dim from sorrow is mine eye, And my members as a shadow all of them.
ylt.17:8: Astonished are the upright at this, And the innocent against the profane Stirreth himself up.
ylt.17:9: And the righteous layeth hold on his way, And the clean of hands addeth strength, And--dumb are they all.
ylt.17:10: Return, and come in, I pray you, And I find not among you a wise man.
ylt.17:11: My days have passed by, My devices have been broken off, The possessions of my heart!
ylt.17:12: Night for day they appoint, Light is near because of darkness.
ylt.17:13: If I wait--Sheol is my house, In darkness I have spread out my couch.
ylt.17:14: To corruption I have called: --`Thou art my father.' `My mother' and `my sister' --to the worm.
ylt.17:15: And where is now my hope? Yea, my hope, who doth behold it?
ylt.17:16: To the parts of Sheol ye go down, If together on the dust we may rest.
ylt.18:1: And Bildad the Shuhite answereth and saith: --
ylt.18:2: When do ye set an end to words? Consider ye, and afterwards do we speak.
ylt.18:3: Wherefore have we been reckoned as cattle? We have been defiled in your eyes!
ylt.18:4: (He is tearing himself in his anger.) For thy sake is earth forsaken? And removed is a rock from its place?
ylt.18:5: Also, the light of the wicked is extinguished. And there doth not shine a spark of his fire.
ylt.18:6: The light hath been dark in his tent, And his lamp over him is extinguished.
ylt.18:7: Straitened are the steps of his strength, And cast him down doth his own counsel.
ylt.18:8: For he is sent into a net by his own feet, And on a snare he doth walk habitually.
ylt.18:9: Seize on the heel doth a gin, Prevail over him do the designing.
ylt.18:10: Hidden in the earth is his cord, And his trap on the path.
ylt.18:11: Round about terrified him have terrors, And they have scattered him--at his feet.
ylt.18:12: Hungry is his sorrow, And calamity is ready at his side.
ylt.18:13: It consumeth the parts of his skin, Consume his parts doth death's first-born.
ylt.18:14: Drawn from his tent is his confidence, And it causeth him to step to the king of terrors.
ylt.18:15: It dwelleth in his tent--out of his provender, Scattered over his habitation is sulphur.
ylt.18:16: From beneath his roots are dried up, And from above cut off is his crop.
ylt.18:17: His memorial hath perished from the land, And he hath no name on the street.
ylt.18:18: They thrust him from light unto darkness, And from the habitable earth cast him out.
ylt.18:19: He hath no continuator, Nor successor among his people, And none is remaining in his dwellings.
ylt.18:20: At this day westerns have been astonished And easterns have taken fright.
ylt.18:21: Only these are tabernacles of the perverse, And this the place God hath not known.
ylt.19:2: Till when do ye afflict my soul, And bruise me with words?
ylt.19:3: These ten times ye put me to shame, ye blush not. Ye make yourselves strange to me--
ylt.19:4: And also--truly, I have erred, With me doth my error remain.
ylt.19:5: If, truly, over me ye magnify yourselves, And decide against me my reproach;
ylt.19:6: Know now, that God turned me upside down, And His net against me hath set round,
ylt.19:7: Lo, I cry out--violence, and am not answered, I cry aloud, and there is no judgment.
ylt.19:8: My way He hedged up, and I pass not over, And on my paths darkness He placeth.
ylt.19:9: Mine honour from off me He hath stripped, And He turneth the crown from my head.
ylt.19:10: He breaketh me down round about, and I go, And removeth like a tree my hope.
ylt.19:11: And He kindleth against me His anger, And reckoneth me to Him as His adversaries.
ylt.19:12: Come in do His troops together, And they raise up against me their way, And encamp round about my tent.
ylt.19:13: My brethren from me He hath put far off, And mine acquaintances surely Have been estranged from me.
ylt.19:14: Ceased have my neighbours And my familiar friends have forgotten me,
ylt.19:15: Sojourners of my house and my maids, For a stranger reckon me: An alien I have been in their eyes.
ylt.19:16: To my servant I have called, And he doth not answer, With my mouth I make supplication to him.
ylt.19:17: My spirit is strange to my wife, And my favours to the sons of my mother's womb.
ylt.19:18: Also sucklings have despised me, I rise, and they speak against me.
ylt.19:19: Abominate me do all the men of my counsel, And those I have loved, Have been turned against me.
ylt.19:20: To my skin and to my flesh Cleaved hath my bone, And I deliver myself with the skin of my teeth.
ylt.19:21: Pity me, pity me, ye my friends, For the hand of God hath stricken against me.
ylt.19:22: Why do you pursue me as God? And with my flesh are not satisfied?
ylt.19:23: Who doth grant now, That my words may be written? Who doth grant that in a book they may be graven?
ylt.19:24: With a pen of iron and lead--For ever in a rock they may be hewn.
ylt.19:25: That--I have known my Redeemer, The Living and the Last, For the dust he doth rise.
ylt.19:26: And after my skin hath compassed this body, Then from my flesh I see God:
ylt.19:27: Whom I--I see on my side, And mine eyes have beheld, and not a stranger, Consumed have been my reins in my bosom.
ylt.19:28: But ye say, `Why do we pursue after him?' And the root of the matter hath been found in me.
ylt.19:29: Be ye afraid because of the sword, For furious are the punishments of the sword, That ye may know that there is a judgment.
ylt.20:1: And Zophar the Naamathite answereth and saith: --
ylt.20:2: Therefore my thoughts cause me to answer, And because of my sensations in me.
ylt.20:3: The chastisement of my shame I hear, And the spirit of mine understanding Doth cause me to answer:
ylt.20:4: This hast thou known from antiquity? Since the placing of man on earth?
ylt.20:5: That the singing of the wicked is short, And the joy of the profane for a moment,
ylt.20:6: Though his excellency go up to the heavens, And his head against a cloud he strike--
ylt.20:7: As his own dung for ever he doth perish, His beholders say: `Where is he?'
ylt.20:8: As a dream he fleeth, and they find him not, And he is driven away as a vision of the night,
ylt.20:9: The eye hath not seen him, and addeth not. And not again doth his place behold him.
ylt.20:10: His sons do the poor oppress, And his hands give back his wealth.
ylt.20:11: His bones have been full of his youth, And with him on the dust it lieth down.
ylt.20:12: Though he doth sweeten evil in his mouth, Doth hide it under his tongue,
ylt.20:13: Hath pity on it, and doth not forsake it, And keep it back in the midst of his palate,
ylt.20:14: His food in his bowels is turned, The bitterness of asps is in his heart.
ylt.20:15: Wealth he hath swallowed, and doth vomit it. From his belly God driveth it out.
ylt.20:16: Gall of asps he sucketh, Slay him doth the tongue of a viper.
ylt.20:17: He looketh not on rivulets, Flowing of brooks of honey and butter.
ylt.20:18: He is giving back what he laboured for, And doth not consume it; As a bulwark is his exchange, and he exults not.
ylt.20:19: For he oppressed--he forsook the poor, A house he hath taken violently away, And he doth not build it.
ylt.20:20: For he hath not known ease in his belly. With his desirable thing he delivereth not himself.
ylt.20:21: There is not a remnant to his food, Therefore his good doth not stay.
ylt.20:22: In the fulness of his sufficiency he is straitened. Every perverse hand doth meet him.
ylt.20:23: It cometh to pass, at the filling of his belly, He sendeth forth against him The fierceness of His anger, Yea, He raineth on him in his eating.
ylt.20:24: He fleeth from an iron weapon, Pass through him doth a bow of brass.
ylt.20:25: One hath drawn, And it cometh out from the body, And a glittering weapon from his gall proceedeth. On him are terrors.
ylt.20:26: All darkness is hid for his treasures, Consume him doth a fire not blown, Broken is the remnant in his tent.
ylt.20:27: Reveal do the heavens his iniquity, And earth is raising itself against him.
ylt.20:28: Remove doth the increase of his house, Poured forth in a day of His anger.
ylt.20:29: This is the portion of a wicked man from God. And an inheritance appointed him by God.
ylt.21:2: Hear ye diligently my word, And this is your consolation.
ylt.21:3: Bear with me, and I speak, And after my speaking--ye may deride.
ylt.21:4: I--to man is my complaint? and if so, wherefore May not my temper become short?
ylt.21:5: Turn unto me, and be astonished, And put hand to mouth.
ylt.21:6: Yea, if I have remembered, then I have been troubled. And my flesh hath taken fright.
ylt.21:7: Wherefore do the wicked live? They have become old, Yea, they have been mighty in wealth.
ylt.21:8: Their seed is established, Before their face with them, And their offspring before their eyes.
ylt.21:9: Their houses are peace without fear, Nor is a rod of God upon them.
ylt.21:10: His bullock hath eaten corn, and doth not loath. His cow bringeth forth safely, And doth not miscarry.
ylt.21:11: They send forth as a flock their sucklings, And their children skip,
ylt.21:12: They lift themselves up at timbrel and harp, And rejoice at the sound of an organ.
ylt.21:13: They wear out in good their days, And in a moment to Sheol go down.
ylt.21:14: And they say to God, `Turn aside from us, And the knowledge of Thy ways We have not desired.
ylt.21:15: What is the Mighty One that we serve Him? And what do we profit when we meet with Him?'
ylt.21:16: Lo, not in their hand is their good, (The counsel of the wicked Hath been far from me.)
ylt.21:17: How oft is the lamp of the wicked extinguished, And come on them doth their calamity? Pangs He apportioneth in His anger.
ylt.21:18: They are as straw before wind, And as chaff a hurricane hath stolen away,
ylt.21:19: God layeth up for his sons his sorrow, He giveth recompense unto him--and he knoweth.
ylt.21:20: His own eyes see his destruction, And of the wrath of the Mighty he drinketh.
ylt.21:21: For what is his delight in his house after him, And the number of his months cut off?
ylt.21:22: To God doth one teach knowledge, And He the high doth judge?
ylt.21:23: This one dieth in his perfect strength, Wholly at ease and quiet.
ylt.21:24: His breasts have been full of milk, And marrow his bones doth moisten.
ylt.21:25: And this one dieth with a bitter soul, And have not eaten with gladness.
ylt.21:26: Together--on the dust they lie down, And the worm doth cover them over.
ylt.21:27: Lo, I have known your thoughts, And the devices against me ye do wrongfully.
ylt.21:28: For ye say, `Where is the house of the noble? And where the tent--The tabernacles of the wicked?'
ylt.21:29: Have ye not asked those passing by the way? And their signs do ye not know?
ylt.21:30: That to a day of calamity is the wicked spared. To a day of wrath they are brought.
ylt.21:31: Who doth declare to his face his way? And for that which he hath done, Who doth give recompence to him?
ylt.21:32: And he--to the graves he is brought. And over the heap a watch is kept.
ylt.21:33: Sweet to him have been the clods of the valley, And after him every man he draweth, And before him there is no numbering.
ylt.21:34: And how do ye comfort me with vanity, And in your answers hath been left trespass?
ylt.22:1: And Eliphaz the Temanite answereth and saith: --
ylt.22:2: To God is a man profitable, Because a wise man to himself is profitable?
ylt.22:3: Is it a delight to the Mighty One That thou art righteous? is it gain, That thou makest perfect thy ways?
ylt.22:4: Because of thy reverence Doth He reason with thee? He entereth with thee into judgment:
ylt.22:5: Is not thy wickedness abundant? And there is no end to thine iniquities.
ylt.22:6: For thou takest a pledge of thy brother for nought, And the garments of the naked Thou dost strip off.
ylt.22:7: Thou causest not the weary to drink water, And from the hungry thou withholdest bread.
ylt.22:8: As to the man of arm--he hath the earth, And the accepted of face--he dwelleth in it.
ylt.22:9: Widows thou hast sent away empty, And the arms of the fatherless are bruised.
ylt.22:10: Therefore round about thee are snares, And trouble thee doth fear suddenly.
ylt.22:11: Or darkness--thou dost not see, And abundance of waters doth cover thee.
ylt.22:12: Is not God high in heaven? And see the summit of the stars, That they are high.
ylt.22:13: And thou hast said, `What--hath God known? Through thickness doth He judge?
ylt.22:14: Thick clouds are a secret place to Him, And He doth not see;' And the circle of the heavens He walketh habitually,
ylt.22:15: The path of the age dost thou observe, That men of iniquity have trodden?
ylt.22:16: Who have been cut down unexpectedly, A flood is poured out on their foundation.
ylt.22:17: Those saying to God, `Turn aside from us,' And what doth the Mighty One to them?
ylt.22:18: And he hath filled their houses with good: (And the counsel of the wicked Hath been far from me.)
ylt.22:19: See do the righteous and they rejoice, And the innocent mocketh at them,
ylt.22:20: `Surely our substance hath not been cut off, And their excellency hath fire consumed.'
ylt.22:21: Acquaint thyself, I pray thee, with Him, And be at peace, Thereby thine increase is good.
ylt.22:22: Receive, I pray thee, from His mouth a law, And set His sayings in thy heart.
ylt.22:23: If thou dost return unto the Mighty Thou art built up, Thou puttest iniquity far from thy tents.
ylt.22:24: So as to set on the dust a defence, And on a rock of the valleys a covering.
ylt.22:25: And the Mighty hath been thy defence, And silver is strength to thee.
ylt.22:26: For then on the Mighty thou delightest thyself, And dost lift up unto God thy face,
ylt.22:27: Thou dost make supplication unto Him, And He doth hear thee, And thy vows thou completest.
ylt.22:28: And thou decreest a saying, And it is established to thee, And on thy ways hath light shone.
ylt.22:29: For they have made low, And thou sayest, `Lift up.' And the bowed down of eyes he saveth.
ylt.22:30: He delivereth the not innocent, Yea, he hath been delivered By the cleanness of thy hands.
ylt.23:2: Also--to-day is my complaint bitter, My hand hath been heavy because of my sighing.
ylt.23:3: O that I had known--and I find Him, I come in unto His seat,
ylt.23:4: I arrange before Him the cause, And my mouth fill with arguments.
ylt.23:5: I know the words He doth answer me, And understand what He saith to me.
ylt.23:6: In the abundance of power doth He strive with me? No! surely He putteth it in me.
ylt.23:7: There the upright doth reason with Him, And I escape for ever from my judge.
ylt.23:8: Lo, forward I go--and He is not, And backward--and I perceive him not.
ylt.23:9: To the left in His working--and I see not, He is covered on the right, and I behold not.
ylt.23:10: For He hath known the way with me, He hath tried me--as gold I go forth.
ylt.23:11: On His step hath my foot laid hold, His way I have kept, and turn not aside,
ylt.23:12: The command of His lips, and I depart not. Above my allotted portion I have laid up The sayings of His mouth.
ylt.23:13: And He is in one mind, And who doth turn Him back? And His soul hath desired--and He doth it.
ylt.23:14: For He doth complete my portion, And many such things are with Him.
ylt.23:15: Therefore, from His presence I am troubled, I consider, and am afraid of Him.
ylt.23:16: And God hath made my heart soft, And the Mighty hath troubled me.
ylt.23:17: For I have not been cut off before darkness, And before me He covered thick darkness.
ylt.24:1: Wherefore from the Mighty One Times have not been hidden, And those knowing Him have not seen His days.
ylt.24:2: The borders they reach, A drove they have taken violently away, Yea, they do evil.
ylt.24:3: The ass of the fatherless they lead away, They take in pledge the ox of the widow,
ylt.24:4: They turn aside the needy from the way, Together have hid the poor of the earth.
ylt.24:5: Lo, wild asses in a wilderness, They have gone out about their work, Seeking early for prey, A mixture for himself--food for young ones.
ylt.24:6: In a field his provender they reap, And the vineyard of the wicked they glean.
ylt.24:7: The naked they cause to lodge Without clothing. And there is no covering in the cold.
ylt.24:8: From the inundation of hills they are wet, And without a refuge--have embraced a rock.
ylt.24:9: They take violently away From the breast the orphan, And on the poor they lay a pledge.
ylt.24:10: Naked, they have gone without clothing, And hungry--have taken away a sheaf.
ylt.24:11: Between their walls they make oil, Wine-presses they have trodden, and thirst.
ylt.24:12: Because of enmity men do groan, And the soul of pierced ones doth cry, And God doth not give praise.
ylt.24:13: They have been among rebellious ones of light, They have not discerned His ways, Nor abode in His paths.
ylt.24:14: At the light doth the murderer rise, He doth slay the poor and needy, And in the night he is as a thief.
ylt.24:15: And the eye of an adulterer Hath observed the twilight, Saying, `No eye doth behold me.' And he putteth the face in secret.
ylt.24:16: He hath dug in the darkness--houses; By day they shut themselves up, They have not known light.
ylt.24:17: When together, morning is to them death shade, When he discerneth the terrors of death shade.
ylt.24:18: Light he is on the face of the waters, Vilified is their portion in the earth, He turneth not the way of vineyards.
ylt.24:19: Drought--also heat--consume snow-waters, Sheol those who have sinned.
ylt.24:20: Forget him doth the womb, Sweeten on him doth the worm, No more is he remembered, And broken as a tree is wickedness.
ylt.24:21: Treating evil the barren who beareth not, And to the widow he doth no good,
ylt.24:22: And hath drawn the mighty by his power, He riseth, and none believeth in life.
ylt.24:23: He giveth to him confidence, and he is supported, And his eyes are on their ways.
ylt.24:24: High they were for a little, and they are not, And they have been brought low. As all others they are shut up, And as the head of an ear of corn cut off.
ylt.24:25: And if not now, who doth prove me a liar, And doth make of nothing my word?
ylt.25:1: And Bildad the Shuhite answereth and saith: --
ylt.25:2: The rule and fear are with Him, Making peace in His high places.
ylt.25:3: Is their any number to His troops? And on whom ariseth not His light?
ylt.25:4: And what? is man righteous with God? And what? is he pure--born of a woman?
ylt.25:5: Lo--unto the moon, and it shineth not, And stars have not been pure in His eyes.
ylt.25:6: How much less man--a grub, And the son of man--a worm!
ylt.26:2: What--thou hast helped the powerless, Saved an arm not strong!
ylt.26:3: What--thou hast given counsel to the unwise, And wise plans in abundance made known.
ylt.26:4: With whom hast thou declared words? And whose breath came forth from thee?
ylt.26:5: The Rephaim are formed, Beneath the waters, also their inhabitants.
ylt.26:6: Naked is Sheol over-against Him, And there is no covering to destruction.
ylt.26:7: Stretching out the north over desolation, Hanging the earth upon nothing,
ylt.26:8: Binding up the waters in His thick clouds, And the cloud is not rent under them.
ylt.26:9: Taking hold of the face of the throne, Spreading over it His cloud.
ylt.26:10: A limit He hath placed on the waters, Unto the boundary of light with darkness.
ylt.26:11: Pillars of the heavens do tremble, And they wonder because of His rebuke.
ylt.26:12: By His power He hath quieted the sea, And by His understanding smitten the proud.
ylt.26:13: By His Spirit the heavens He beautified, Formed hath His hand the fleeing serpent.
ylt.26:14: Lo, these are the borders of His way, And how little a matter is heard of Him, And the thunder of His might Who doth understand?
ylt.27:1: And Job addeth to lift up his simile, and saith: --
ylt.27:2: God liveth! He turned aside my judgment, And the Mighty--He made my soul bitter.
ylt.27:3: For all the while my breath is in me, And the spirit of God in my nostrils.
ylt.27:4: My lips do not speak perverseness, And my tongue doth not utter deceit.
ylt.27:5: Pollution to me--if I justify you, Till I expire I turn not aside mine integrity from me.
ylt.27:6: On my righteousness I have laid hold, And I do not let it go, My heart doth not reproach me while I live.
ylt.27:7: As the wicked is my enemy, And my withstander as the perverse.
ylt.27:8: For what is the hope of the profane, When He doth cut off? When God doth cast off his soul?
ylt.27:9: His cry doth God hear, When distress cometh on him?
ylt.27:10: On the Mighty doth he delight himself? Call God at all times?
ylt.27:11: I shew you by the hand of God, That which is with the Mighty I hide not.
ylt.27:12: Lo, ye--all of you--have seen, And why is this--ye are altogether vain?
ylt.27:13: This is the portion of wicked man with God, And the inheritance of terrible ones From the Mighty they receive.
ylt.27:14: If his sons multiply--for them is a sword. And his offspring are not satisfied with bread.
ylt.27:15: His remnant in death are buried, And his widows do not weep.
ylt.27:16: If he heap up as dust silver, And as clay prepare clothing,
ylt.27:17: He prepareth--and the righteous putteth it on, And the silver the innocent doth apportion.
ylt.27:18: He hath built as a moth his house, And as a booth a watchman hath made.
ylt.27:19: Rich he lieth down, and he is not gathered, His eyes he hath opened, and he is not.
ylt.27:20: Overtake him as waters do terrors, By night stolen him away hath a whirlwind.
ylt.27:21: Take him up doth an east wind, and he goeth, And it frighteneth him from his place,
ylt.27:22: And it casteth at him, and doth not spare, From its hand he diligently fleeth.
ylt.27:23: It clappeth at him its hands, And it hisseth at him from his place.
ylt.28:1: Surely there is for silver a source, And a place for the gold they refine;
ylt.28:2: Iron from the dust is taken, And from the firm stone brass.
ylt.28:3: An end hath he set to darkness, And to all perfection he is searching, A stone of darkness and death-shade.
ylt.28:4: A stream hath broken out from a sojourner, Those forgotten of the foot, They were low, from man they wandered.
ylt.28:5: The earth! from it cometh forth bread, And its under-part is turned like fire.
ylt.28:6: A place of the sapphire are its stones, And it hath dust of gold.
ylt.28:7: A path--not known it hath a ravenous fowl, Nor scorched it hath an eye of the kite,
ylt.28:8: Nor trodden it have the sons of pride, Not passed over it hath the fierce lion.
ylt.28:9: Against the flint he sent forth his hand, He overturned from the root mountains.
ylt.28:10: Among rocks, brooks he hath cleaved, And every precious thing hath his eye seen.
ylt.28:11: From overflowing floods he hath bound, And the hidden thing bringeth out to light.
ylt.28:12: And the wisdom--whence is it found? And where is this, the place of understanding?
ylt.28:13: Man hath not known its arrangement, Nor is it found in the land of the living.
ylt.28:14: The deep hath said, `It is not in me,' And the sea hath said, `It is not with me.'
ylt.28:15: Gold is not given for it, Nor is silver weighed--its price.
ylt.28:16: It is not valued with pure gold of Ophir, With precious onyx and sapphire,
ylt.28:17: Not equal it do gold and crystal, Nor is its exchange a vessel of fine gold.
ylt.28:18: Corals and pearl are not remembered, The acquisition of wisdom is above rubies.
ylt.28:19: Not equal it doth the topaz of Cush, With pure gold it is not valued.
ylt.28:20: And the wisdom--whence doth it come? And where is this, the place of understanding?
ylt.28:21: It hath been hid from the eyes of all living. And from the fowl of the heavens It hath been hidden.
ylt.28:22: Destruction and death have said: `With our ears we have heard its fame.'
ylt.28:23: God hath understood its way, And He hath known its place.
ylt.28:24: For He to the ends of the earth doth look, Under the whole heavens He doth see,
ylt.28:25: To make for the wind a weight, And the waters He meted out in measure.
ylt.28:26: In His making for the rain a limit, And a way for the brightness of the voices,
ylt.28:27: Then He hath seen and declareth it, He hath prepared it, and also searched it out,
ylt.28:28: And He saith to man: --`Lo, fear of the Lord, that is wisdom, And to turn from evil is understanding.'
ylt.29:1: And Job addeth to lift up his simile, and saith: --
ylt.29:2: Who doth make me as in months past, As in the days of God's preserving me?
ylt.29:3: In His causing His lamp to shine on my head, By His light I walk through darkness.
ylt.29:4: As I have been in days of my maturity, And the counsel of God upon my tent.
ylt.29:5: When yet the Mighty One is with me. Round about me--my young ones,
ylt.29:6: When washing my goings with butter, And the firm rock is with me rivulets of oil.
ylt.29:7: When I go out to the gate by the city, In a broad place I prepare my seat.
ylt.29:8: Seen me have youths, and they, been hidden, And the aged have risen--they stood up.
ylt.29:9: Princes have kept in words, And a hand they place on their mouth.
ylt.29:10: The voice of leaders hath been hidden, And their tongue to the palate hath cleaved.
ylt.29:11: For the ear heard, and declareth me happy, And the eye hath seen, and testifieth to me.
ylt.29:12: For I deliver the afflicted who is crying, And the fatherless who hath no helper.
ylt.29:13: The blessing of the perishing cometh on me, And the heart of the widow I cause to sing.
ylt.29:14: Righteousness I have put on, and it clotheth me, As a robe and a diadem my justice.
ylt.29:15: Eyes I have been to the blind, And feet to the lame am I.
ylt.29:16: A father I am to the needy, And the cause I have not known I search out.
ylt.29:17: And I break the jaw-teeth of the perverse, And from his teeth I cast away prey.
ylt.29:18: And I say, `With my nest I expire, And as the sand I multiply days.'
ylt.29:19: My root is open unto the waters, And dew doth lodge on my branch.
ylt.29:20: My honour is fresh with me, And my bow in my hand is renewed.
ylt.29:21: To me they have hearkened, Yea, they wait, and are silent for my counsel.
ylt.29:22: After my word they change not, And on them doth my speech drop,
ylt.29:23: And they wait as for rain for me, And their mouth they have opened wide As for the latter rain.
ylt.29:24: I laugh unto them--they give no credence, And the light of my face cause not to fall.
ylt.29:25: I choose their way, and sit head, And I dwell as a king in a troop, When mourners he doth comfort.
ylt.30:1: And now, laughed at me, Have the younger in days than I, Whose fathers I have loathed to set With the dogs of my flock.
ylt.30:2: Also--the power of their hands, why is it to me? On them hath old age perished.
ylt.30:3: With want and with famine gloomy, Those fleeing to a dry place, Formerly a desolation and waste,
ylt.30:4: Those cropping mallows near a shrub, And broom-roots is their food.
ylt.30:5: From the midst they are cast out, (They shout against them as a thief),
ylt.30:6: In a frightful place of valleys to dwell, Holes of earth and clefts.
ylt.30:7: Among shrubs they do groan, Under nettles they are gathered together.
ylt.30:8: Sons of folly--even sons without name, They have been smitten from the land.
ylt.30:9: And now, their song I have been, And I am to them for a byword.
ylt.30:10: They have abominated me, They have kept far from me, And from before me have not spared to spit.
ylt.30:11: Because His cord He loosed and afflicteth me, And the bridle from before me, They have cast away.
ylt.30:12: On the right hand doth a brood arise, My feet they have cast away, And they raise up against me, Their paths of calamity.
ylt.30:13: They have broken down my path, By my calamity they profit, `He hath no helper.'
ylt.30:14: As a wide breach they come, Under the desolation have rolled themselves.
ylt.30:15: He hath turned against me terrors, It pursueth as the wind mine abundance, And as a thick cloud, Hath my safety passed away.
ylt.30:16: And now, in me my soul poureth itself out, Seize me do days of affliction.
ylt.30:17: At night my bone hath been pierced in me, And mine eyelids do not lie down.
ylt.30:18: By the abundance of power, Is my clothing changed, As the mouth of my coat it doth gird me.
ylt.30:19: Casting me into mire, And I am become like dust and ashes.
ylt.30:20: I cry unto Thee, And Thou dost not answer me, I have stood, and Thou dost consider me.
ylt.30:21: Thou art turned to be fierce to me, With the strength of Thy hand, Thou oppressest me.
ylt.30:22: Thou dost lift me up, On the wind Thou dost cause me to ride, And Thou meltest--Thou levellest me.
ylt.30:23: For I have known To death Thou dost bring me back, And to the house appointed for all living.
ylt.30:24: Surely not against the heap Doth He send forth the hand, Though in its ruin they have safety.
ylt.30:25: Did not I weep for him whose day is hard? Grieved hath my soul for the needy.
ylt.30:26: When good I expected, then cometh evil, And I wait for light, and darkness cometh.
ylt.30:27: My bowels have boiled, and have not ceased, Gone before me have days of affliction.
ylt.30:28: Mourning I have gone without the sun, I have risen, in an assembly I cry.
ylt.30:29: A brother I have been to dragons, And a companion to daughters of the ostrich.
ylt.30:30: My skin hath been black upon me, And my bone hath burned from heat,
ylt.30:31: And my harp doth become mourning, And my organ the sound of weeping.
ylt.31:1: A covenant I made for mine eyes, And what--do I attend to a virgin?
ylt.31:2: And what is the portion of God from above? And the inheritance of the Mighty from the heights?
ylt.31:3: Is not calamity to the perverse? And strangeness to workers of iniquity?
ylt.31:4: Doth not He see my ways, And all my steps number?
ylt.31:5: If I have walked with vanity, And my foot doth hasten to deceit,
ylt.31:6: He doth weigh me in righteous balances, And God doth know my integrity.
ylt.31:7: If my step doth turn aside from the way, And after mine eyes hath my heart gone, And to my hands cleaved hath blemish,
ylt.31:8: Let me sow--and another eat, And my products let be rooted out.
ylt.31:9: If my heart hath been enticed by woman, And by the opening of my neighbour I laid wait,
ylt.31:10: Grind to another let my wife, And over her let others bend.
ylt.31:11: For it is a wicked thing, and a judicial iniquity;
ylt.31:12: For a fire it is, to destruction it consumeth, And among all mine increase doth take root,
ylt.31:13: If I despise the cause of my man-servant, And of my handmaid, In their contending with me,
ylt.31:14: Then what do I do when God ariseth? And when He doth inspect, What do I answer Him?
ylt.31:15: Did not He that made me in the womb make him? Yea, prepare us in the womb doth One.
ylt.31:16: If I withhold from pleasure the poor, And the eyes of the widow do consume,
ylt.31:17: And I do eat my morsel by myself, And the orphan hath not eat of it,
ylt.31:18: (But from my youth He grew up with me as with a father, And from the belly of my mother I am led.)
ylt.31:19: If I see any perishing without clothing, And there is no covering to the needy,
ylt.31:20: If his loins have not blessed me, And from the fleece of my sheep He doth not warm himself,
ylt.31:21: If I have waved at the fatherless my hand, When I see in him the gate of my court,
ylt.31:22: My shoulder from its blade let fall, And mine arm from the bone be broken.
ylt.31:23: For a dread unto me is calamity from God, And because of His excellency I am not able.
ylt.31:24: If I have made gold my confidence, And to the pure gold have said, `My trust,'
ylt.31:25: If I rejoice because great is my wealth, And because abundance hath my hand found,
ylt.31:26: If I see the light when it shineth, And the precious moon walking,
ylt.31:27: And my heart is enticed in secret, And my hand doth kiss my mouth,
ylt.31:28: It also is a judicial iniquity, For I had lied to God above.
ylt.31:29: If I rejoice at the ruin of my hater, And stirred up myself when evil found him,
ylt.31:30: Yea, I have not suffered my mouth to sin, To ask with an oath his life.
ylt.31:31: If not--say ye, O men of my tent, `O that we had of his flesh, we are not satisfied.'
ylt.31:32: In the street doth not lodge a stranger, My doors to the traveller I open.
ylt.31:33: If I have covered as Adam my transgressions, To hide in my bosom mine iniquity,
ylt.31:34: Because I fear a great multitude, And the contempt of families doth affright me, Then I am silent, I go not out of the opening.
ylt.31:35: Who giveth to me a hearing? lo, my mark. The Mighty One doth answer me, And a bill hath mine adversary written.
ylt.31:36: If not--on my shoulder I take it up, I bind it a crown on myself.
ylt.31:37: The number of my steps I tell Him, As a leader I approach Him.
ylt.31:38: If against me my land doth cry out, And together its furrows weep,
ylt.31:39: If its strength I consumed without money, And the life of its possessors, I have caused to breathe out,
ylt.31:40: Instead of wheat let a thorn go forth, And instead of barley a useless weed! The words of Job are finished.
ylt.32:1: And these three men cease from answering Job, for he is righteous in his own eyes,
ylt.32:2: and burn doth the anger of Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite, of the family of Ram; against Job hath his anger burned, because of his justifying himself more than God;
ylt.32:3: and against his three friends hath his anger burned, because that they have not found an answer, and condemn Job.
ylt.32:4: And Elihu hath waited earnestly beside Job with words, for they are older than he in days.
ylt.32:5: And Elihu seeth that there is no answer in the mouth of the three men, and his anger burneth.
ylt.32:6: And Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite answereth and saith: --Young I am in days, and ye are age Therefore I have feared, And am afraid of shewing you my opinion.
ylt.32:7: I said: Days do speak, And multitude of years teach wisdom.
ylt.32:8: Surely a spirit is in man, And the breath of the Mighty One Doth cause them to understand.
ylt.32:9: The multitude are not wise, Nor do the aged understand judgment.
ylt.32:10: Therefore I have said: Hearken to me, I do shew my opinion--even I.
ylt.32:11: Lo, I have waited for your words, I give ear unto your reasons, Till ye search out sayings.
ylt.32:12: And unto you I attend, And lo, there is no reasoner for Job, Or answerer of his sayings among you.
ylt.32:13: Lest ye say, We have found wisdom, God doth thrust him away, not man.
ylt.32:14: And he hath not set in array words for me, And with your sayings I do not answer him.
ylt.32:15: (They have broken down, They have not answered again, They removed from themselves words.
ylt.32:16: And I have waited, but they do not speak, For they have stood still, They have not answered any more.)
ylt.32:17: I answer, even I--my share, I shew my opinion--even I.
ylt.32:18: For I have been full of words, Distressed me hath the spirit of my breast,
ylt.32:19: Lo, my breast is as wine not opened, Like new bottles it is broken up.
ylt.32:20: I speak, and there is refreshment to me, I open my lips and answer.
ylt.32:21: Let me not, I pray you, accept the face of any, Nor unto man give flattering titles,
ylt.32:22: For I have not known to give flattering titles, In a little doth my Maker take me away.
ylt.33:1: And yet, I pray thee, O Job, Hear my speech and to all my words give ear.
ylt.33:2: Lo, I pray thee, I have opened my mouth, My tongue hath spoken in the palate.
ylt.33:3: Of the uprightness of my heart are my sayings, And knowledge have my lips clearly spoken.
ylt.33:4: The Spirit of God hath made me, And the breath of the Mighty doth quicken me.
ylt.33:5: If thou art able--answer me, Set in array before me--station thyself.
ylt.33:6: Lo, I am, according to thy word, for God, From the clay I--I also, have been formed.
ylt.33:7: Lo, my terror doth not frighten thee, And my burden on thee is not heavy.
ylt.33:8: Surely--thou hast said in mine ears, And the sounds of words I hear:
ylt.33:9: `Pure am I, without transgression, Innocent am I, and I have no iniquity.
ylt.33:10: Lo, occasions against me He doth find, He doth reckon me for an enemy to Him,
ylt.33:11: He doth put in the stocks my feet, He doth watch all my paths.'
ylt.33:12: Lo, in this thou hast not been righteous, I answer thee, that greater is God than man.
ylt.33:13: Wherefore against Him hast thou striven, When for all His matters He answereth not?
ylt.33:14: For once doth God speak, and twice, (He doth not behold it.)
ylt.33:15: In a dream--a vision of night, In the falling of deep sleep on men, In slumberings on a bed.
ylt.33:16: Then He uncovereth the ear of men, And for their instruction sealeth:
ylt.33:17: To turn aside man from doing, And pride from man He concealeth.
ylt.33:18: He keepeth back his soul from corruption, And his life from passing away by a dart.
ylt.33:19: And he hath been reproved With pain on his bed, And the strife of his bones is enduring.
ylt.33:20: And his life hath nauseated bread, And his soul desirable food.
ylt.33:21: His flesh is consumed from being seen, And high are his bones, they were not seen!
ylt.33:22: And draw near to the pit doth his soul, And his life to those causing death.
ylt.33:23: If there is by him a messenger, An interpreter--one of a thousand, To declare for man his uprightness:
ylt.33:24: Then He doth favour him and saith, `Ransom him from going down to the pit, I have found an atonement.'
ylt.33:25: Fresher is his flesh than a child's, He returneth to the days of his youth.
ylt.33:26: He maketh supplication unto God, And He accepteth him. And he seeth His face with shouting, And He returneth to man His righteousness.
ylt.33:27: He looketh on men, and saith, `I sinned, And uprightness I have perverted, And it hath not been profitable to me.
ylt.33:28: He hath ransomed my soul From going over into the pit, And my life on the light looketh.'
ylt.33:29: Lo, all these doth God work, Twice--thrice with man,
ylt.33:30: To bring back his soul from the pit, To be enlightened with the light of the living.
ylt.33:31: Attend, O Job, hearken to me, Keep silent, and I--I do speak.
ylt.33:32: If there are words--answer me, Speak, for I have a desire to justify thee.
ylt.33:33: If there are not--hearken thou to me, Keep silent, and I teach thee wisdom.
ylt.34:2: Hear, O wise men, my words, And, O knowing ones, give ear to me.
ylt.34:3: For the ear doth try words, And the palate tasteth to eat.
ylt.34:4: Judgment let us choose for ourselves, Let us know among ourselves what is good.
ylt.34:5: For Job hath said, `I have been righteous, And God hath turned aside my right,
ylt.34:6: Against my right do I lie? Mortal is mine arrow--without transgression.'
ylt.34:7: Who is a man like Job? He drinketh scoffing like water,
ylt.34:8: And he hath travelled for company With workers of iniquity, So as to go with men of wickedness.
ylt.34:9: For he hath said, `It doth not profit a man, When he delighteth himself with God.'
ylt.34:10: Therefore, O men of heart, hearken to me; Far be it from God to do wickedness, And from the Mighty to do perverseness:
ylt.34:11: For the work of man he repayeth to him, And according to the path of each He doth cause him to find.
ylt.34:12: Yea, truly, God doth not do wickedly, And the Mighty doth not pervert judgment.
ylt.34:13: Who hath inspected for Himself the earth? And who hath placed all the habitable world?
ylt.34:14: If He doth set on him His heart, His spirit and his breath unto Him He gathereth.
ylt.34:15: Expire doth all flesh together, And man to dust returneth.
ylt.34:16: And if there is understanding, hear this, Give ear to the voice of my words.
ylt.34:17: Yea, doth one hating justice govern? Or the Most Just dost thou condemn?
ylt.34:18: Who hath said to a king--`Worthless,' Unto princes--`Wicked?'
ylt.34:19: That hath not accepted the person of princes, Nor hath known the rich before the poor, For a work of His hands are all of them.
ylt.34:20: In a moment they die, and at midnight Shake do people, and they pass away, And they remove the mighty without hand.
ylt.34:21: For His eyes are on the ways of each, And all his steps He doth see.
ylt.34:22: There is no darkness nor death-shade, For workers of iniquity to be hidden there;
ylt.34:23: For He doth not suffer man any more, To go unto God in judgment,
ylt.34:24: He breaketh the mighty--no searching! And He appointeth others in their stead.
ylt.34:25: Therefore He knoweth their works, And He hath overturned by night, And they are bruised.
ylt.34:26: As wicked He hath stricken them, In the place of beholders.
ylt.34:27: Because that against right They have turned aside from after Him, And none of His ways have considered wisely,
ylt.34:28: To cause to come in unto Him The cry of the poor, And the cry of the afflicted He heareth.
ylt.34:29: And He giveth rest, and who maketh wrong? And hideth the face, and who beholdeth it? And in reference to a nation and to a man, It is the same.
ylt.34:30: From the reigning of a profane man, From the snares of a people;
ylt.34:31: For unto God hath any said: `I have taken away, I do not corruptly,
ylt.34:32: Besides that which I see, shew Thou me, If iniquity I have done--I do not add?'
ylt.34:33: By thee doth He recompense, That thou hast refused--That thou dost choose, and not I? And what thou hast known, speak.
ylt.34:34: Let men of heart say to me, And a wise man is hearkening to me.
ylt.34:35: Job--not with knowledge doth he speak, And his words are not with wisdom.
ylt.34:36: My Father! let Job be tried--unto victory, Because of answers for men of iniquity,
ylt.34:37: For he doth add to his sin, Transgression among us he vomiteth, And multiplieth his sayings to God.
ylt.35:2: This hast thou reckoned for judgment: Thou hast said--`My righteousness is more than God's?'
ylt.35:3: For thou sayest, `What doth it profit Thee! What do I profit from my sin?'
ylt.35:4: I return thee words, and thy friends with thee,
ylt.35:5: Behold attentively the heavens--and see, And behold the clouds, They have been higher than thou.
ylt.35:6: If thou hast sinned, what dost thou against Him? And thy transgressions have been multiplied, What dost thou to Him?
ylt.35:7: If thou hast been righteous, What dost thou give to Him? Or what from thy hand doth He receive?
ylt.35:8: For a man like thyself is thy wickedness, And for a son of man thy righteousness.
ylt.35:9: Because of the multitude of oppressions They cause to cry out, They cry because of the arm of the mighty.
ylt.35:10: And none said, `Where is God my maker? Giving songs in the night,
ylt.35:11: Teaching us more than the beasts of the earth, Yea, than the fowl of the heavens He maketh us wiser.'
ylt.35:12: There they cry, and He doth not answer, Because of the pride of evil doers.
ylt.35:13: Surely vanity God doth not hear, And the Mighty doth not behold it.
ylt.35:14: Yea, though thou sayest thou dost not behold Him, Judgment is before Him, and stay for Him.
ylt.35:15: And, now, because there is not, He hath appointed His anger, And He hath not known in great extremity.
ylt.35:16: And Job with vanity doth open his mouth, Without knowledge words he multiplieth.
ylt.36:2: Honour me a little, and I shew thee, That yet for God are words.
ylt.36:3: I lift up my knowledge from afar, And to my Maker I ascribe righteousness.
ylt.36:4: For, truly, my words are not false, The perfect in knowledge is with thee.
ylt.36:5: Lo, God is mighty, and despiseth not, Mighty in power and heart.
ylt.36:6: He reviveth not the wicked, And the judgment of the poor appointeth;
ylt.36:7: He withdraweth not from the righteous His eyes, And from kings on the throne, And causeth them to sit for ever, and they are high,
ylt.36:8: And if prisoners in fetters They are captured with cords of affliction,
ylt.36:9: Then He declareth to them their work, And their transgressions, Because they have become mighty,
ylt.36:10: And He uncovereth their ear for instruction, And saith that they turn back from iniquity.
ylt.36:11: If they do hear and serve, They complete their days in good, And their years in pleasantness.
ylt.36:12: And if they do not hearken, By the dart they pass away, And expire without knowledge.
ylt.36:13: And the profane in heart set the face, They cry not when He hath bound them.
ylt.36:14: Their soul dieth in youth, And their life among the defiled.
ylt.36:15: He draweth out the afflicted in his affliction, And uncovereth in oppression their ear.
ylt.36:16: And also He moved thee from a strait place, To a broad place--no straitness under it, And the sitting beyond of thy table Hath been full of fatness.
ylt.36:17: And the judgment of the wicked thou hast fulfilled, Judgment and justice are upheld--because of fury,
ylt.36:18: Lest He move thee with a stroke, And the abundance of an atonement turn thee not aside.
ylt.36:19: Doth He value thy riches? He hath gold, and all the forces of power.
ylt.36:20: Desire not the night, For the going up of peoples in their stead.
ylt.36:21: Take heed--do not turn unto iniquity, For on this thou hast fixed Rather than on affliction.
ylt.36:22: Lo, God doth sit on high by His power, Who is like Him--a teacher?
ylt.36:23: Who hath appointed unto Him his way? And who said, `Thou hast done iniquity?'
ylt.36:24: Remember that thou magnify His work That men have beheld.
ylt.36:25: All men have looked on it, Man looketh attentively from afar.
ylt.36:26: Lo, God is high, And we know not the number of His years, Yea, there is no searching.
ylt.36:27: When He doth diminish droppings of the waters, They refine rain according to its vapour,
ylt.36:28: Which clouds do drop, They distil on man abundantly.
ylt.36:29: Yea, doth any understand The spreadings out of a cloud? The noises of His tabernacle?
ylt.36:30: Lo, He hath spread over it His light, And the roots of the sea He hath covered,
ylt.36:31: For by them He doth judge peoples, He giveth food in abundance.
ylt.36:32: By two palms He hath covered the light, And layeth a charge over it in meeting,
ylt.36:33: He sheweth by it to his friend substance, Anger against perversity.
ylt.37:1: Also, at this my heart trembleth, And it moveth from its place.
ylt.37:2: Hearken diligently to the trembling of His voice, Yea, the sound from His mouth goeth forth.
ylt.37:3: Under the whole heavens He directeth it, And its light is over the skirts of the earth.
ylt.37:4: After it roar doth a voice--He thundereth with the voice of His excellency, And He doth not hold them back, When His voice is heard.
ylt.37:5: God thundereth with His voice wonderfully, Doing great things and we know not.
ylt.37:6: For to snow He saith, `Be on the earth.' And the small rain and great rain of His power.
ylt.37:7: Into the hand of every man he sealeth, For the knowledge by all men of His work.
ylt.37:8: And enter doth the beast into covert, And in its habitations it doth continue.
ylt.37:9: From the inner chamber cometh a hurricane, And from scatterings winds--cold,
ylt.37:10: From the breath of God is frost given, And the breadth of waters is straitened,
ylt.37:11: Yea, by filling He doth press out a cloud, Scatter a cloud doth His light.
ylt.37:12: And it is turning itself round by His counsels, For their doing all He commandeth them, On the face of the habitable earth.
ylt.37:13: Whether for a rod, or for His land, Or for kindness--He doth cause it to come.
ylt.37:14: Hear this, O Job, Stand and consider the wonders of God.
ylt.37:15: Dost thou know when God doth place them, And caused to shine the light of His cloud?
ylt.37:16: Dost thou know the balancings of a cloud? The wonders of the Perfect in knowledge?
ylt.37:17: How thy garments are warm, In the quieting of the earth from the south?
ylt.37:18: Thou hast made an expanse with Him For the clouds--strong as a hard mirror!
ylt.37:19: Let us know what we say to Him, We set not in array because of darkness.
ylt.37:20: Is it declared to Him that I speak? If a man hath spoken, surely he is swallowed up.
ylt.37:21: And now, they have not seen the light, Bright it is in the clouds, And the wind hath passed by and cleanseth them.
ylt.37:22: From the golden north it cometh, Beside God is fearful honour.
ylt.37:23: The Mighty! we have not found Him out, High in power and judgment, He doth not answer! And abundant in righteousness,
ylt.37:24: Therefore do men fear Him, He seeth not any of the wise of heart.
ylt.38:1: And Jehovah answereth Job out of the whirlwind, and saith: --
ylt.38:2: Who is this--darkening counsel, By words without knowledge?
ylt.38:3: Gird, I pray thee, as a man, thy loins, And I ask thee, and cause thou Me to know.
ylt.38:4: Where wast thou when I founded earth? Declare, if thou hast known understanding.
ylt.38:5: Who placed its measures--if thou knowest? Or who hath stretched out upon it a line?
ylt.38:6: On what have its sockets been sunk? Or who hath cast its corner-stone?
ylt.38:7: In the singing together of stars of morning, And all sons of God shout for joy,
ylt.38:8: And He shutteth up with doors the sea, In its coming forth, from the womb it goeth out.
ylt.38:9: In My making a cloud its clothing, And thick darkness its swaddling band,
ylt.38:10: And I measure over it My statute, And place bar and doors,
ylt.38:11: And say, `Hitherto come thou, and add not, And a command is placed On the pride of thy billows.'
ylt.38:12: Hast thou commanded morning since thy days? Causest thou the dawn to know its place?
ylt.38:13: To take hold on the skirts of the earth, And the wicked are shaken out of it,
ylt.38:14: It turneth itself as clay of a seal And they station themselves as clothed.
ylt.38:15: And withheld from the wicked is their light, And the arm lifted up is broken.
ylt.38:16: Hast thou come in to springs of the sea? And in searching the deep Hast thou walked up and down?
ylt.38:17: Revealed to thee were the gates of death? And the gates of death-shade dost thou see?
ylt.38:18: Thou hast understanding, Even unto the broad places of earth! Declare--if thou hast known it all.
ylt.38:19: Where is this--the way light dwelleth? And darkness, where is this--its place?
ylt.38:20: That thou dost take it unto its boundary, And that thou dost understand The paths of its house.
ylt.38:21: Thou hast known--for then thou art born And the number of thy days are many!
ylt.38:22: Hast thou come in unto the treasure of snow? Yea, the treasures of hail dost thou see?
ylt.38:23: That I have kept back for a time of distress, For a day of conflict and battle.
ylt.38:24: Where is this, the way light is apportioned? It scattereth an east wind over the earth.
ylt.38:25: Who hath divided for the flood a conduit? And a way for the lightning of the voices?
ylt.38:26: To cause it to rain on a land--no man, A wilderness--no man in it.
ylt.38:27: To satisfy a desolate and waste place, And to cause to shoot up The produce of the tender grass?
ylt.38:28: Hath the rain a father? Or who hath begotten the drops of dew?
ylt.38:29: From whose belly came forth the ice? And the hoar-frost of the heavens, Who hath begotten it?
ylt.38:30: As a stone waters are hidden, And the face of the deep is captured.
ylt.38:31: Dost thou bind sweet influences of Kimah? Or the attractions of Kesil dost thou open?
ylt.38:32: Dost thou bring out Mazzaroth in its season? And Aysh for her sons dost thou comfort?
ylt.38:33: Hast thou known the statutes of heaven? Or dost thou appoint Its dominion in the earth?
ylt.38:34: Dost thou lift up to the cloud thy voice, And abundance of water doth cover thee?
ylt.38:35: Dost thou send out lightnings, and they go And say unto thee, `Behold us?'
ylt.38:36: Who hath put in the inward parts wisdom? Or who hath given To the covered part understanding?
