ylt.38:37: Who doth number the clouds by wisdom? And the bottles of the heavens, Who doth cause to lie down,
ylt.38:38: In the hardening of dust into hardness, And clods cleave together?
ylt.38:39: Dost thou hunt for a lion prey? And the desire of young lions fulfil?
ylt.38:40: When they bow down in dens--Abide in a thicket for a covert?
ylt.38:41: Who doth prepare for a raven his provision, When his young ones cry unto God? They wander without food.
ylt.39:1: Hast thou known the time of The bearing of the wild goats of the rock? The bringing forth of hinds thou dost mark!
ylt.39:2: Thou dost number the months they fulfil? And thou hast known the time of their bringing forth!
ylt.39:3: They bow down, Their young ones they bring forth safely, Their pangs they cast forth.
ylt.39:4: Safe are their young ones, They grow up in the field, they have gone out, And have not returned to them.
ylt.39:5: Who hath sent forth the wild ass free? Yea, the bands of the wild ass who opened?
ylt.39:6: Whose house I have made the wilderness, And his dwellings the barren land,
ylt.39:7: He doth laugh at the multitude of a city, The cries of an exactor he heareth not.
ylt.39:8: The range of mountains is his pasture, And after every green thing he seeketh.
ylt.39:9: Is a Reem willing to serve thee? Doth he lodge by thy crib?
ylt.39:10: Dost thou bind a Reem in a furrow with his thick band? Doth he harrow valleys after thee?
ylt.39:11: Dost thou trust in him because great is his power? And dost thou leave unto him thy labour?
ylt.39:12: Dost thou trust in him That he doth bring back thy seed? And to thy threshing-floor doth gather it?
ylt.39:13: The wing of the rattling ones exulteth, Whether the pinion of the ostrich or hawk.
ylt.39:14: For she leaveth on the earth her eggs, And on the dust she doth warm them,
ylt.39:15: And she forgetteth that a foot may press it, And a beast of the field tread it down.
ylt.39:16: Her young ones it hath hardened without her, In vain is her labour without fear.
ylt.39:17: For God hath caused her to forget wisdom, And He hath not given a portion To her in understanding:
ylt.39:18: At the time on high she lifteth herself up, She laugheth at the horse and at his rider.
ylt.39:19: Dost thou give to the horse might? Dost thou clothe his neck with a mane?
ylt.39:20: Dost thou cause him to rush as a locust? The majesty of his snorting is terrible.
ylt.39:21: They dig in a valley, and he rejoiceth in power, He goeth forth to meet the armour.
ylt.39:22: He laugheth at fear, and is not affrighted, And he turneth not back from the face of the sword.
ylt.39:23: Against him rattle doth quiver, The flame of a spear, and a halbert.
ylt.39:24: With trembling and rage he swalloweth the ground, And remaineth not stedfast Because of the sound of a trumpet.
ylt.39:25: Among the trumpets he saith, Aha, And from afar he doth smell battle, Roaring of princes and shouting.
ylt.39:26: By thine understanding flieth a hawk? Spreadeth he his wings to the south?
ylt.39:27: At thy command goeth an eagle up high? Or lifteth he up his nest?
ylt.39:28: A rock he doth inhabit, Yea, he lodgeth on the tooth of a rock, and fortress.
ylt.39:29: From thence he hath sought food, To a far off place his eyes look attentively,
ylt.39:30: And his brood gulp up blood, And where the pierced are --there is he!
ylt.40:1: And Jehovah doth answer Job, and saith: --
ylt.40:2: Is the striver with the Mighty instructed? The reprover of God, let him answer it.
ylt.40:3: And Job answereth Jehovah, and saith: --
ylt.40:4: Lo, I have been vile, What do I return to Thee? My hand I have placed on my mouth.
ylt.40:5: Once I have spoken, and I answer not, And twice, and I add not.
ylt.40:6: And Jehovah answereth Job out of the whirlwind, and saith: --
ylt.40:7: Gird, I pray thee, as a man, thy loins, I ask thee, and cause thou Me to know.
ylt.40:8: Dost thou also make void My judgment? Dost thou condemn Me, That thou mayest be righteous?
ylt.40:9: And an arm like God hast thou? And with a voice like Him dost thou thunder?
ylt.40:10: Put on, I pray thee, excellency and loftiness, Yea, honour and beauty put on.
ylt.40:11: Scatter abroad the wrath of thine anger, And see every proud one, and make him low.
ylt.40:12: See every proud one--humble him, And tread down the wicked in their place.
ylt.40:13: Hide them in the dust together, Their faces bind in secret.
ylt.40:14: And even I--I do praise thee, For thy right hand giveth salvation to thee.
ylt.40:15: Lo, I pray thee, Behemoth, that I made with thee: Grass as an ox he eateth.
ylt.40:16: Lo, I pray thee, his power is in his loins, And his strength in the muscles of his belly.
ylt.40:17: He doth bend his tail as a cedar, The sinews of his thighs are wrapped together,
ylt.40:18: His bones are tubes of brass, His bones are as a bar of iron.
ylt.40:19: He is a beginning of the ways of God, His Maker bringeth nigh his sword;
ylt.40:20: For food do mountains bear for him, And all the beasts of the field play there.
ylt.40:21: Under shades he lieth down, In a secret place of reed and mire.
ylt.40:22: Cover him do shades, with their shadow, Cover him do willows of the brook.
ylt.40:23: Lo, a flood oppresseth--he doth not haste, He is confident though Jordan Doth come forth unto his mouth.
ylt.40:24: Before his eyes doth one take him, With snares doth one pierce the nose?
ylt.41:1: Dost thou draw leviathan with an angle? And with a rope thou lettest down--his tongue?
ylt.41:2: Dost thou put a reed in his nose? And with a thorn pierce his jaw?
ylt.41:3: Doth he multiply unto thee supplications? Doth he speak unto thee tender things?
ylt.41:4: Doth he make a covenant with thee? Dost thou take him for a servant age-during?
ylt.41:5: Dost thou play with him as a bird? And dost thou bind him for thy damsels?
ylt.41:6: (Feast upon him do companions, They divide him among the merchants!)
ylt.41:7: Dost thou fill with barbed irons his skin? And with fish-spears his head?
ylt.41:8: Place on him thy hand, Remember the battle--do not add!
ylt.41:9: Lo, the hope of him is found a liar, Also at his appearance is not one cast down?
ylt.41:10: None so fierce that he doth awake him, And who is he before Me stationeth himself?
ylt.41:11: Who hath brought before Me and I repay? Under the whole heavens it is mine.
ylt.41:12: I do not keep silent concerning his parts, And the matter of might, And the grace of his arrangement.
ylt.41:13: Who hath uncovered the face of his clothing? Within his double bridle who doth enter?
ylt.41:14: The doors of his face who hath opened? Round about his teeth are terrible.
ylt.41:15: A pride--strong ones of shields, Shut up--a close seal.
ylt.41:16: One unto another they draw nigh, And air doth not enter between them.
ylt.41:17: One unto another they adhere, They stick together and are not separated.
ylt.41:18: His sneezings cause light to shine, And his eyes are as the eyelids of the dawn.
ylt.41:19: Out of his mouth do flames go, sparks of fire escape.
ylt.41:20: Out of his nostrils goeth forth smoke, As a blown pot and reeds.
ylt.41:21: His breath setteth coals on fire, And a flame from his mouth goeth forth.
ylt.41:22: In his neck lodge doth strength, And before him doth grief exult.
ylt.41:23: The flakes of his flesh have adhered--Firm upon him--it is not moved.
ylt.41:24: His heart is firm as a stone, Yea, firm as the lower piece.
ylt.41:25: From his rising are the mighty afraid, From breakings they keep themselves free.
ylt.41:26: The sword of his overtaker standeth not, Spear--dart--and lance.
ylt.41:27: He reckoneth iron as straw, brass as rotten wood.
ylt.41:28: The son of the bow doth not cause him to flee, Turned by him into stubble are stones of the sling.
ylt.41:29: As stubble have darts been reckoned, And he laugheth at the shaking of a javelin.
ylt.41:30: Under him are sharp points of clay, He spreadeth gold on the mire.
ylt.41:31: He causeth to boil as a pot the deep, The sea he maketh as a pot of ointment.
ylt.41:32: After him he causeth a path to shine, One thinketh the deep to be hoary.
ylt.41:33: There is not on the earth his like, That is made without terror.
ylt.41:34: Every high thing he doth see, He is king over all sons of pride.
ylt.42:1: And Job answereth Jehovah and saith: --
ylt.42:2: Thou hast known that for all things Thou art able, And not withheld from Thee is any device:
ylt.42:3: `Who is this, hiding counsel without knowledge?' Therefore, I have declared, and understand not, Too wonderful for me, and I know not.
ylt.42:4: `Hear, I pray thee, and I--I do speak, I ask thee, and cause thou me to know.'
ylt.42:5: By the hearing of the ear I heard Thee, And now mine eye hath seen Thee.
ylt.42:6: Therefore do I loathe it, And I have repented on dust and ashes.
ylt.42:7: And it cometh to pass after Jehovah's speaking these words unto Job, that Jehovah saith unto Eliphaz the Temanite, `Burned hath Mine anger against thee, and against thy two friends, because ye have not spoken concerning Me rightly, like My servant Job.
ylt.42:8: And now, take to you seven bullocks and seven rams, and go ye unto My servant Job, and ye have caused a burnt-offering to ascend for you; and Job My servant doth pray for you, for surely his face I accept, so as not to do with you folly, because ye have not spoken concerning Me rightly, like My servant Job.
ylt.42:9: And they go--Eliphaz the Temanite, and Bildad the Shuhite, Zophar the Naamathite--and do as Jehovah hath spoken unto them; and Jehovah doth accept the face of Job.
ylt.42:10: And Jehovah hath turned to the captivity of Job in his praying for his friends, and Jehovah doth add to all that Job hath--to double.
ylt.42:11: And come unto him do all his brethren, and all his sisters, and all his former acquaintances, and they eat bread with him in his house, and bemoan him, and comfort him concerning all the evil that Jehovah had brought upon him, and they gave to him each one kesitah, and each one ring of gold.
ylt.42:12: And Jehovah hath blessed the latter end of Job more than his beginning, and he hath fourteen thousand of a flock, and six thousand camels, and a thousand pairs of oxen, and a thousand she-asses.
ylt.42:13: And he hath seven sons and three daughters;
ylt.42:14: and he calleth the name of the one Jemima, and the name of the second Kezia, and the name of the third Keren-Happuch.
ylt.42:15: And there have not been found women fair as the daughters of Job in all the land, and their father doth give to them an inheritance in the midst of their brethren.
ylt.42:16: And Job liveth after this a hundred and forty years, and seeth his sons, and his sons' sons, four generations;
ylt.42:17: and Job dieth, aged and satisfied with days.

web.1:1: There was a man in the land of Uz, whose name was Job. That man was blameless and upright, and one who feared God, and turned away from evil.
web.1:2: There were born to him seven sons and three daughters.
web.1:3: His possessions also were seven thousand sheep, three thousand camels, five hundred yoke of oxen, five hundred female donkeys, and a very great household; so that this man was the greatest of all the children of the east.
web.1:4: His sons went and held a feast in the house of each one on his birthday; and they sent and called for their three sisters to eat and to drink with them.
web.1:5: It was so, when the days of their feasting had run their course, that Job sent and sanctified them, and rose up early in the morning, and offered burnt offerings according to the number of them all. For Job said, “It may be that my sons have sinned, and renounced God in their hearts.” Job did so continually.
web.1:6: Now on the day when God’s sons came to present themselves before Yahweh, Satan also came among them.
web.1:7: Yahweh said to Satan, “Where have you come from?” Then Satan answered Yahweh, and said, “From going back and forth in the earth, and from walking up and down in it.”
web.1:8: Yahweh said to Satan, “Have you considered my servant, Job? For there is no one like him in the earth, a blameless and an upright man, one who fears God, and turns away from evil.”
web.1:9: Then Satan answered Yahweh, and said, “Does Job fear God for nothing?
web.1:10: Haven’t you made a hedge around him, and around his house, and around all that he has, on every side? You have blessed the work of his hands, and his substance is increased in the land.
web.1:11: But stretch out your hand now, and touch all that he has, and he will renounce you to your face.”
web.1:12: Yahweh said to Satan, “Behold, all that he has is in your power. Only on himself don’t stretch out your hand.” So Satan went out from the presence of Yahweh.
web.1:13: It fell on a day when his sons and his daughters were eating and drinking wine in their oldest brother’s house,
web.1:14: that there came a messenger to Job, and said, “The oxen were plowing, and the donkeys feeding beside them,
web.1:15: and the Sabeans attacked, and took them away. Yes, they have killed the servants with the edge of the sword, and I alone have escaped to tell you.”
web.1:16: While he was still speaking, there also came another, and said, “The fire of God has fallen from the sky, and has burned up the sheep and the servants, and consumed them, and I alone have escaped to tell you.”
web.1:17: While he was still speaking, there came also another, and said, “The Chaldeans made three bands, and swept down on the camels, and have taken them away, yes, and killed the servants with the edge of the sword; and I alone have escaped to tell you.”
web.1:18: While he was still speaking, there came also another, and said, “Your sons and your daughters were eating and drinking wine in their oldest brother’s house,
web.1:19: and behold, there came a great wind from the wilderness, and struck the four corners of the house, and it fell on the young men, and they are dead. I alone have escaped to tell you.”
web.1:20: Then Job arose, and tore his robe, and shaved his head, and fell down on the ground, and worshiped.
web.1:21: He said, “Naked I came out of my mother’s womb, and naked will I return there. Yahweh gave, and Yahweh has taken away. Blessed be Yahweh’s name.”
web.1:22: In all this, Job didn’t sin, nor charge God with wrongdoing.
web.2:1: Again, on the day when the God’s sons came to present themselves before Yahweh, Satan came also among them to present himself before Yahweh.
web.2:2: Yahweh said to Satan, “Where have you come from?” Satan answered Yahweh, and said, “From going back and forth in the earth, and from walking up and down in it.”
web.2:3: Yahweh said to Satan, “Have you considered my servant Job? For there is no one like him in the earth, a blameless and an upright man, one who fears God, and turns away from evil. He still maintains his integrity, although you incited me against him, to ruin him without cause.”
web.2:4: Satan answered Yahweh, and said, “Skin for skin. Yes, all that a man has he will give for his life.
web.2:5: But stretch out your hand now, and touch his bone and his flesh, and he will renounce you to your face.”
web.2:6: Yahweh said to Satan, “Behold, he is in your hand. Only spare his life.”
web.2:7: So Satan went out from the presence of Yahweh, and struck Job with painful sores from the sole of his foot to his head.
web.2:8: He took for himself a potsherd to scrape himself with, and he sat among the ashes.
web.2:9: Then his wife said to him, “Do you still maintain your integrity? Renounce God, and die.”
web.2:10: But he said to her, “You speak as one of the foolish women would speak. What? Shall we receive good at the hand of God, and shall we not receive evil?” In all this Job didn’t sin with his lips.
web.2:11: Now when Job’s three friends heard of all this evil that had come on him, they each came from his own place: Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite; and they made an appointment together to come to sympathize with him and to comfort him.
web.2:12: When they lifted up their eyes from a distance, and didn’t recognize him, they raised their voices, and wept; and they each tore his robe, and sprinkled dust on their heads toward the sky.
web.2:13: So they sat down with him on the ground seven days and seven nights, and no one spoke a word to him, for they saw that his grief was very great.
web.3:1: After this Job opened his mouth, and cursed the day of his birth.
web.3:3: “Let the day perish in which I was born, the night which said, ‘There is a boy conceived.’
web.3:4: Let that day be darkness. Don’t let God from above seek for it, neither let the light shine on it.
web.3:5: Let darkness and the shadow of death claim it for their own. Let a cloud dwell on it. Let all that makes black the day terrify it.
web.3:6: As for that night, let thick darkness seize on it. Let it not rejoice among the days of the year. Let it not come into the number of the months.
web.3:7: Behold, let that night be barren. Let no joyful voice come therein.
web.3:8: Let them curse it who curse the day, who are ready to rouse up leviathan.
web.3:9: Let the stars of its twilight be dark. Let it look for light, but have none, neither let it see the eyelids of the morning,
web.3:10: because it didn’t shut up the doors of my mother’s womb, nor did it hide trouble from my eyes.
web.3:11: “Why didn’t I die from the womb? Why didn’t I give up the spirit when my mother bore me?
web.3:12: Why did the knees receive me? Or why the breast, that I should nurse?
web.3:13: For now should I have lain down and been quiet. I should have slept, then I would have been at rest,
web.3:14: with kings and counselors of the earth, who built up waste places for themselves;
web.3:15: or with princes who had gold, who filled their houses with silver:
web.3:16: or as a hidden untimely birth I had not been, as infants who never saw light.
web.3:17: There the wicked cease from troubling. There the weary are at rest.
web.3:18: There the prisoners are at ease together. They don’t hear the voice of the taskmaster.
web.3:19: The small and the great are there. The servant is free from his master.
web.3:20: “Why is light given to him who is in misery, life to the bitter in soul,
web.3:21: Who long for death, but it doesn’t come; and dig for it more than for hidden treasures,
web.3:22: who rejoice exceedingly, and are glad, when they can find the grave?
web.3:23: Why is light given to a man whose way is hidden, whom God has hedged in?
web.3:24: For my sighing comes before I eat. My groanings are poured out like water.
web.3:25: For the thing which I fear comes on me, That which I am afraid of comes to me.
web.3:26: I am not at ease, neither am I quiet, neither have I rest; but trouble comes.”
web.4:2: “If someone ventures to talk with you, will you be grieved? But who can withhold himself from speaking?
web.4:3: Behold, you have instructed many, you have strengthened the weak hands.
web.4:4: Your words have supported him who was falling, You have made firm the feeble knees.
web.4:5: But now it has come to you, and you faint. It touches you, and you are troubled.
web.4:6: Isn’t your piety your confidence? Isn’t the integrity of your ways your hope?
web.4:7: “Remember, now, whoever perished, being innocent? Or where were the upright cut off?
web.4:8: According to what I have seen, those who plow iniquity, and sow trouble, reap the same.
web.4:9: By the breath of God they perish. By the blast of his anger are they consumed.
web.4:10: The roaring of the lion, and the voice of the fierce lion, the teeth of the young lions, are broken.
web.4:11: The old lion perishes for lack of prey. The cubs of the lioness are scattered abroad.
web.4:12: “Now a thing was secretly brought to me. My ear received a whisper of it.
web.4:13: In thoughts from the visions of the night, when deep sleep falls on men,
web.4:14: fear came on me, and trembling, which made all my bones shake.
web.4:15: Then a spirit passed before my face. The hair of my flesh stood up.
web.4:16: It stood still, but I couldn’t discern its appearance. A form was before my eyes. Silence, then I heard a voice, saying,
web.4:17: ‘Shall mortal man be more just than God? Shall a man be more pure than his Maker?
web.4:18: Behold, he puts no trust in his servants. He charges his angels with error.
web.4:19: How much more, those who dwell in houses of clay, whose foundation is in the dust, who are crushed before the moth!
web.4:20: Between morning and evening they are destroyed. They perish forever without any regarding it.
web.4:21: Isn’t their tent cord plucked up within them? They die, and that without wisdom.’
web.5:1: “Call now; is there any who will answer you? To which of the holy ones will you turn?
web.5:2: For resentment kills the foolish man, and jealousy kills the simple.
web.5:3: I have seen the foolish taking root, but suddenly I cursed his habitation.
web.5:4: His children are far from safety. They are crushed in the gate. Neither is there any to deliver them,
web.5:5: whose harvest the hungry eats up, and take it even out of the thorns. The snare gapes for their substance.
web.5:6: For affliction doesn’t come out of the dust, neither does trouble spring out of the ground;
web.5:7: but man is born to trouble, as the sparks fly upward.
web.5:8: “But as for me, I would seek God. I would commit my cause to God,
web.5:9: who does great things that can’t be fathomed, marvelous things without number;
web.5:10: who gives rain on the earth, and sends waters on the fields;
web.5:11: so that he sets up on high those who are low, those who mourn are exalted to safety.
web.5:12: He frustrates the plans of the crafty, So that their hands can’t perform their enterprise.
web.5:13: He takes the wise in their own craftiness; the counsel of the cunning is carried headlong.
web.5:14: They meet with darkness in the day time, and grope at noonday as in the night.
web.5:15: But he saves from the sword of their mouth, even the needy from the hand of the mighty.
web.5:16: So the poor has hope, and injustice shuts her mouth.
web.5:17: “Behold, happy is the man whom God corrects. Therefore do not despise the chastening of the Almighty.
web.5:18: For he wounds and binds up. He injures and his hands make whole.
web.5:19: He will deliver you in six troubles; yes, in seven no evil will touch you.
web.5:20: In famine he will redeem you from death; in war, from the power of the sword.
web.5:21: You will be hidden from the scourge of the tongue, neither will you be afraid of destruction when it comes.
web.5:22: You will laugh at destruction and famine, neither will you be afraid of the animals of the earth.
web.5:23: For you will be allied with the stones of the field. The animals of the field will be at peace with you.
web.5:24: You will know that your tent is in peace. You will visit your fold, and will miss nothing.
web.5:25: You will know also that your offspring will be great, Your offspring as the grass of the earth.
web.5:26: You will come to your grave in a full age, like a shock of grain comes in its season.
web.5:27: Look at this. We have searched it. It is so. Hear it, and know it for your good.”
web.6:2: “Oh that my anguish were weighed, and all my calamity laid in the balances!
web.6:3: For now it would be heavier than the sand of the seas, therefore have my words been rash.
web.6:4: For the arrows of the Almighty are within me. My spirit drinks up their poison. The terrors of God set themselves in array against me.
web.6:5: Does the wild donkey bray when he has grass? Or does the ox low over his fodder?
web.6:6: Can that which has no flavor be eaten without salt? Or is there any taste in the white of an egg?
web.6:7: My soul refuses to touch them. They are as loathsome food to me.
web.6:8: “Oh that I might have my request, that God would grant the thing that I long for,
web.6:9: even that it would please God to crush me; that he would let loose his hand, and cut me off!
web.6:10: Let still be my consolation, yes, let me exult in pain that doesn’t spare, that I have not denied the words of the Holy One.
web.6:11: What is my strength, that I should wait? What is my end, that I should be patient?
web.6:12: Is my strength the strength of stones? Or is my flesh of bronze?
web.6:13: Isn’t it that I have no help in me, That wisdom is driven quite from me?
web.6:14: “To him who is ready to faint, kindness should be shown from his friend; even to him who forsakes the fear of the Almighty.
web.6:15: My brothers have dealt deceitfully as a brook, as the channel of brooks that pass away;
web.6:16: Which are black by reason of the ice, in which the snow hides itself.
web.6:17: In the dry season, they vanish. When it is hot, they are consumed out of their place.
web.6:18: The caravans that travel beside them turn away. They go up into the waste, and perish.
web.6:19: The caravans of Tema looked. The companies of Sheba waited for them.
web.6:20: They were distressed because they were confident. They came there, and were confounded.
web.6:21: For now you are nothing. You see a terror, and are afraid.
web.6:22: Did I say, ‘Give to me?’ or, ‘Offer a present for me from your substance?’
web.6:23: or, ‘Deliver me from the adversary’s hand?’ or, ‘Redeem me from the hand of the oppressors?’
web.6:24: “Teach me, and I will hold my peace. Cause me to understand my error.
web.6:25: How forcible are words of uprightness! But your reproof, what does it reprove?
web.6:26: Do you intend to reprove words, since the speeches of one who is desperate are as wind?
web.6:27: Yes, you would even cast lots for the fatherless, and make merchandise of your friend.
web.6:28: Now therefore be pleased to look at me, for surely I will not lie to your face.
web.6:29: Please return. Let there be no injustice. Yes, return again. My cause is righteous.
web.6:30: Is there injustice on my tongue? Can’t my taste discern mischievous things?
web.7:1: “Isn’t a man forced to labor on earth? Aren’t his days like the days of a hired hand?
web.7:2: As a servant who earnestly desires the shadow, as a hireling who looks for his wages,
web.7:3: so am I made to possess months of misery, wearisome nights are appointed to me.
web.7:4: When I lie down, I say, ‘When will I arise, and the night be gone?’ I toss and turn until the dawning of the day.
web.7:5: My flesh is clothed with worms and clods of dust. My skin closes up, and breaks out afresh.
web.7:6: My days are swifter than a weaver’s shuttle, and are spent without hope.
web.7:7: Oh remember that my life is a breath. My eye will no more see good.
web.7:8: The eye of him who sees me will see me no more. Your eyes will be on me, but I will not be.
web.7:9: As the cloud is consumed and vanishes away, so he who goes down to Sheol will come up no more.
web.7:10: He will return no more to his house, neither will his place know him any more.
web.7:11: “Therefore I will not keep silent. I will speak in the anguish of my spirit. I will complain in the bitterness of my soul.
web.7:12: Am I a sea, or a sea monster, that you put a guard over me?
web.7:13: When I say, ‘My bed will comfort me. My couch will ease my complaint;’
web.7:14: then you scare me with dreams, and terrify me through visions:
web.7:15: so that my soul chooses strangling, death rather than my bones.
web.7:16: I loathe my life. I don’t want to live forever. Leave me alone, for my days are but a breath.
web.7:17: What is man, that you should magnify him, that you should set your mind on him,
web.7:18: that you should visit him every morning, and test him every moment?
web.7:19: How long will you not look away from me, nor leave me alone until I swallow down my spittle?
web.7:20: If I have sinned, what do I do to you, you watcher of men? Why have you set me as a mark for you, so that I am a burden to myself?
web.7:21: Why do you not pardon my disobedience, and take away my iniquity? For now will I lie down in the dust. You will seek me diligently, but I will not be.”
web.8:2: “How long will you speak these things? Shall the words of your mouth be a mighty wind?
web.8:3: Does God pervert justice? Or does the Almighty pervert righteousness?
web.8:4: If your children have sinned against him, he has delivered them into the hand of their disobedience.
web.8:5: If you want to seek God diligently, make your supplication to the Almighty.
web.8:6: If you were pure and upright, surely now he would awaken for you, and make the habitation of your righteousness prosperous.
web.8:7: Though your beginning was small, yet your latter end would greatly increase.
web.8:8: “Please inquire of past generations. Find out about the learning of their fathers.
web.8:9: (For we are but of yesterday, and know nothing, because our days on earth are a shadow.)
web.8:10: Shall they not teach you, tell you, and utter words out of their heart?
web.8:11: “Can the papyrus grow up without mire? Can the rushes grow without water?
web.8:12: While it is yet in its greenness, not cut down, it withers before any other reed.
web.8:13: So are the paths of all who forget God. The hope of the godless man will perish,
web.8:14: Whose confidence will break apart, Whose trust is a spider’s web.
web.8:15: He will lean on his house, but it will not stand. He will cling to it, but it will not endure.
web.8:16: He is green before the sun. His shoots go out along his garden.
web.8:17: His roots are wrapped around the rock pile. He sees the place of stones.
web.8:18: If he is destroyed from his place, then it will deny him, saying, ‘I have not seen you.’
web.8:19: Behold, this is the joy of his way: out of the earth, others will spring.
web.8:20: “Behold, God will not cast away a blameless man, neither will he uphold the evildoers.
web.8:21: He will still fill your mouth with laughter, your lips with shouting.
web.8:22: Those who hate you will be clothed with shame. The tent of the wicked will be no more.”
web.9:2: “Truly I know that it is so, but how can man be just with God?
web.9:3: If he is pleased to contend with him, he can’t answer him one time in a thousand.
web.9:4: God who is wise in heart, and mighty in strength: who has hardened himself against him and prospered?
web.9:5: He removes the mountains, and they don’t know it, when he overturns them in his anger.
web.9:6: He shakes the earth out of its place. Its pillars tremble.
web.9:7: He commands the sun and it doesn’t rise, and seals up the stars.
web.9:8: He alone stretches out the heavens, and treads on the waves of the sea.
web.9:9: He makes the Bear, Orion, and the Pleiades, and the rooms of the south.
web.9:10: He does great things past finding out; yes, marvelous things without number.
web.9:11: Behold, he goes by me, and I don’t see him. He passes on also, but I don’t perceive him.
web.9:12: Behold, he snatches away. Who can hinder him? Who will ask him, ‘What are you doing?’
web.9:13: “God will not withdraw his anger. The helpers of Rahab stoop under him.
web.9:14: How much less will I answer him, And choose my words to argue with him?
web.9:15: Though I were righteous, yet I wouldn’t answer him. I would make supplication to my judge.
web.9:16: If I had called, and he had answered me, yet I wouldn’t believe that he listened to my voice.
web.9:17: For he breaks me with a storm, and multiplies my wounds without cause.
web.9:18: He will not allow me to catch my breath, but fills me with bitterness.
web.9:19: If it is a matter of strength, behold, he is mighty! If of justice, ‘Who,’ says he, ‘will summon me?’
web.9:20: Though I am righteous, my own mouth will condemn me. Though I am blameless, it will prove me perverse.
web.9:21: I am blameless. I don’t respect myself. I despise my life.
web.9:22: “It is all the same. Therefore I say he destroys the blameless and the wicked.
web.9:23: If the scourge kills suddenly, he will mock at the trial of the innocent.
web.9:24: The earth is given into the hand of the wicked. He covers the faces of its judges. If not he, then who is it?
web.9:25: “Now my days are swifter than a runner. They flee away. They see no good.
web.9:26: They have passed away as the swift ships, as the eagle that swoops on the prey.
web.9:27: If I say, ‘I will forget my complaint, I will put off my sad face, and cheer up;’
web.9:28: I am afraid of all my sorrows, I know that you will not hold me innocent.
web.9:29: I will be condemned. Why then do I labor in vain?
web.9:30: If I wash myself with snow, and cleanse my hands with lye,
web.9:31: yet you will plunge me in the ditch. My own clothes will abhor me.
web.9:32: For he is not a man, as I am, that I should answer him, that we should come together in judgment.
web.9:33: There is no umpire between us, that might lay his hand on us both.
web.9:34: Let him take his rod away from me. Let his terror not make me afraid;
web.9:35: then I would speak, and not fear him, for I am not so in myself.
web.10:1: “My soul is weary of my life. I will give free course to my complaint. I will speak in the bitterness of my soul.
web.10:2: I will tell God, ‘Do not condemn me. Show me why you contend with me.
web.10:3: Is it good to you that you should oppress, that you should despise the work of your hands, and smile on the counsel of the wicked?
web.10:4: Do you have eyes of flesh? Or do you see as man sees?
web.10:5: Are your days as the days of mortals, or your years as man’s years,
web.10:6: that you inquire after my iniquity, and search after my sin?
web.10:7: Although you know that I am not wicked, there is no one who can deliver out of your hand.
web.10:8: “ ‘Your hands have framed me and fashioned me altogether, yet you destroy me.
web.10:9: Remember, I beg you, that you have fashioned me as clay. Will you bring me into dust again?
web.10:10: Haven’t you poured me out like milk, and curdled me like cheese?
web.10:11: You have clothed me with skin and flesh, and knit me together with bones and sinews.
web.10:12: You have granted me life and loving kindness. Your visitation has preserved my spirit.
web.10:13: Yet you hid these things in your heart. I know that this is with you:
web.10:14: if I sin, then you mark me. You will not acquit me from my iniquity.
web.10:15: If I am wicked, woe to me. If I am righteous, I still will not lift up my head, being filled with disgrace, and conscious of my affliction.
web.10:16: If my head is held high, you hunt me like a lion. Again you show yourself powerful to me.
web.10:17: You renew your witnesses against me, and increase your indignation on me. Changes and warfare are with me.
web.10:18: “ ‘Why, then, have you brought me out of the womb? I wish I had given up the spirit, and no eye had seen me.
web.10:19: I should have been as though I had not been. I should have been carried from the womb to the grave.
web.10:20: Aren’t my days few? Stop! Leave me alone, that I may find a little comfort,
web.10:21: before I go where I will not return from, to the land of darkness and of the shadow of death;
web.10:22: the land dark as midnight, of the shadow of death, without any order, where the light is as midnight.’ ”
web.11:2: “Shouldn’t the multitude of words be answered? Should a man full of talk be justified?
web.11:3: Should your boastings make men hold their peace? When you mock, will no man make you ashamed?
web.11:4: For you say, ‘My doctrine is pure. I am clean in your eyes.’
web.11:5: But oh that God would speak, and open his lips against you,
web.11:6: that he would show you the secrets of wisdom! For true wisdom has two sides. Know therefore that God exacts of you less than your iniquity deserves.
web.11:7: “Can you fathom the mystery of God? Or can you probe the limits of the Almighty?
web.11:8: They are high as heaven. What can you do? They are deeper than Sheol. What can you know?
web.11:9: Its measure is longer than the earth, and broader than the sea.
web.11:10: If he passes by, or confines, or convenes a court, then who can oppose him?
web.11:11: For he knows false men. He sees iniquity also, even though he doesn’t consider it.
web.11:12: An empty-headed man becomes wise when a man is born as a wild donkey’s colt.
web.11:13: “If you set your heart aright, stretch out your hands toward him.
web.11:14: If iniquity is in your hand, put it far away. Don’t let unrighteousness dwell in your tents.
web.11:15: Surely then you will lift up your face without spot; Yes, you will be steadfast, and will not fear:
web.11:16: for you will forget your misery. You will remember it like waters that have passed away.
web.11:17: Life will be clearer than the noonday. Though there is darkness, it will be as the morning.
web.11:18: You will be secure, because there is hope. Yes, you will search, and will take your rest in safety.
web.11:19: Also you will lie down, and no one will make you afraid. Yes, many will court your favor.
web.11:20: But the eyes of the wicked will fail. They will have no way to flee. Their hope will be the giving up of the spirit.”
web.12:2: “No doubt, but you are the people, and wisdom will die with you.
web.12:3: But I have understanding as well as you; I am not inferior to you. Yes, who doesn’t know such things as these?
web.12:4: I am like one who is a joke to his neighbor, I, who called on God, and he answered. The just, the blameless man is a joke.
web.12:5: In the thought of him who is at ease there is contempt for misfortune. It is ready for them whose foot slips.
web.12:6: The tents of robbers prosper. Those who provoke God are secure, who carry their god in their hands.
web.12:7: “But ask the animals, now, and they will teach you; the birds of the sky, and they will tell you.
web.12:8: Or speak to the earth, and it will teach you. The fish of the sea will declare to you.
web.12:9: Who doesn’t know that in all these, Yahweh’s hand has done this,
web.12:10: in whose hand is the life of every living thing, and the breath of all mankind?
web.12:11: Doesn’t the ear try words, even as the palate tastes its food?
web.12:12: With aged men is wisdom, in length of days understanding.
web.12:13: “With God is wisdom and might. He has counsel and understanding.
web.12:14: Behold, he breaks down, and it can’t be built again. He imprisons a man, and there can be no release.
web.12:15: Behold, he withholds the waters, and they dry up. Again, he sends them out, and they overturn the earth.
web.12:16: With him is strength and wisdom. The deceived and the deceiver are his.
web.12:17: He leads counselors away stripped. He makes judges fools.
web.12:18: He loosens the bond of kings. He binds their waist with a belt.
web.12:19: He leads priests away stripped, and overthrows the mighty.
web.12:20: He removes the speech of those who are trusted, and takes away the understanding of the elders.
web.12:21: He pours contempt on princes, and loosens the belt of the strong.
web.12:22: He uncovers deep things out of darkness, and brings out to light the shadow of death.
web.12:23: He increases the nations, and he destroys them. He enlarges the nations, and he leads them captive.
web.12:24: He takes away understanding from the chiefs of the people of the earth, and causes them to wander in a wilderness where there is no way.
web.12:25: They grope in the dark without light. He makes them stagger like a drunken man.
web.13:1: “Behold, my eye has seen all this. My ear has heard and understood it.
web.13:2: What you know, I know also. I am not inferior to you.
web.13:3: “Surely I would speak to the Almighty. I desire to reason with God.
web.13:4: But you are forgers of lies. You are all physicians of no value.
web.13:5: Oh that you would be completely silent! Then you would be wise.
web.13:6: Hear now my reasoning. Listen to the pleadings of my lips.
web.13:7: Will you speak unrighteously for God, and talk deceitfully for him?
web.13:8: Will you show partiality to him? Will you contend for God?
web.13:9: Is it good that he should search you out? Or as one deceives a man, will you deceive him?
web.13:10: He will surely reprove you if you secretly show partiality.
web.13:11: Shall not his majesty make you afraid, and his dread fall on you?
web.13:12: Your memorable sayings are proverbs of ashes. Your defenses are defenses of clay.
web.13:13: “Be silent! Leave me alone, that I may speak. Let come on me what will.
web.13:14: Why should I take my flesh in my teeth, and put my life in my hand?
web.13:15: Behold, he will kill me. I have no hope. Nevertheless, I will maintain my ways before him.
web.13:16: This also will be my salvation, that a godless man will not come before him.
web.13:17: Listen carefully to my speech. Let my declaration be in your ears.
web.13:18: See now, I have set my cause in order. I know that I am righteous.
web.13:19: Who is he who will contend with me? For then would I hold my peace and give up the spirit.
web.13:20: “Only don’t do two things to me, then I will not hide myself from your face:
web.13:21: withdraw your hand far from me, and don’t let your terror make me afraid.
web.13:22: Then call, and I will answer, or let me speak, and you answer me.
web.13:23: How many are my iniquities and sins? Make me know my disobedience and my sin.
web.13:24: Why do you hide your face, and consider me your enemy?
web.13:25: Will you harass a driven leaf? Will you pursue the dry stubble?
web.13:26: For you write bitter things against me, and make me inherit the iniquities of my youth:
web.13:27: You also put my feet in the stocks, and mark all my paths. You set a bound to the soles of my feet,
web.13:28: though I am decaying like a rotten thing, like a garment that is moth-eaten.
web.14:1: “Man, who is born of a woman, is of few days, and full of trouble.
web.14:2: He grows up like a flower, and is cut down. He also flees like a shadow, and doesn’t continue.
web.14:3: Do you open your eyes on such a one, and bring me into judgment with you?
web.14:4: Who can bring a clean thing out of an unclean? Not one.
web.14:5: Seeing his days are determined, the number of his months is with you, and you have appointed his bounds that he can’t pass;
web.14:6: Look away from him, that he may rest, until he accomplishes, as a hireling, his day.
web.14:7: “For there is hope for a tree if it is cut down, that it will sprout again, that the tender branch of it will not cease.
web.14:8: Though its root grows old in the earth, and its stock dies in the ground,
web.14:9: yet through the scent of water it will bud, and sprout boughs like a plant.
web.14:10: But man dies, and is laid low. Yes, man gives up the spirit, and where is he?
web.14:11: As the waters fail from the sea, and the river wastes and dries up,
web.14:12: so man lies down and doesn’t rise. Until the heavens are no more, they will not awake, nor be roused out of their sleep.
web.14:13: “Oh that you would hide me in Sheol, that you would keep me secret until your wrath is past, that you would appoint me a set time and remember me!
web.14:14: If a man dies, will he live again? I would wait all the days of my warfare, until my release should come.
web.14:15: You would call, and I would answer you. You would have a desire for the work of your hands.
web.14:16: But now you count my steps. Don’t you watch over my sin?
web.14:17: My disobedience is sealed up in a bag. You fasten up my iniquity.
web.14:18: “But the mountain falling comes to nothing. The rock is removed out of its place;
web.14:19: The waters wear the stones. The torrents of it wash away the dust of the earth. So you destroy the hope of man.
web.14:20: You forever prevail against him, and he departs. You change his face, and send him away.
web.14:21: His sons come to honor, and he doesn’t know it. They are brought low, but he doesn’t perceive it of them.
web.14:22: But his flesh on him has pain, and his soul within him mourns.”
web.15:2: “Should a wise man answer with vain knowledge, and fill himself with the east wind?
web.15:3: Should he reason with unprofitable talk, or with speeches with which he can do no good?
web.15:4: Yes, you do away with fear, and hinder devotion before God.
web.15:5: For your iniquity teaches your mouth, and you choose the language of the crafty.
web.15:6: Your own mouth condemns you, and not I. Yes, your own lips testify against you.
web.15:7: “Are you the first man who was born? Or were you brought out before the hills?
web.15:8: Have you heard the secret counsel of God? Do you limit wisdom to yourself?
web.15:9: What do you know that we don’t know? What do you understand which is not in us?
web.15:10: With us are both the gray-headed and the very aged men, much elder than your father.
web.15:11: Are the consolations of God too small for you, even the word that is gentle toward you?
web.15:12: Why does your heart carry you away? Why do your eyes flash,
web.15:13: That you turn your spirit against God, and let such words go out of your mouth?
web.15:14: What is man, that he should be clean? What is he who is born of a woman, that he should be righteous?
web.15:15: Behold, he puts no trust in his holy ones. Yes, the heavens are not clean in his sight;
web.15:16: how much less one who is abominable and corrupt, a man who drinks iniquity like water!
web.15:17: “I will show you, listen to me; that which I have seen I will declare
web.15:18: (which wise men have told by their fathers, and have not hidden it;
web.15:19: to whom alone the land was given, and no stranger passed among them):
web.15:20: the wicked man writhes in pain all his days, even the number of years that are laid up for the oppressor.
web.15:21: A sound of terrors is in his ears. In prosperity the destroyer will come on him.
web.15:22: He doesn’t believe that he will return out of darkness. He is waited for by the sword.
web.15:23: He wanders abroad for bread, saying, ‘Where is it?’ He knows that the day of darkness is ready at his hand.
web.15:24: Distress and anguish make him afraid. They prevail against him, as a king ready to the battle.
web.15:25: Because he has stretched out his hand against God, and behaves himself proudly against the Almighty,
web.15:26: he runs at him with a stiff neck, with the thick shields of his bucklers,
web.15:27: because he has covered his face with his fatness, and gathered fat on his thighs.
web.15:28: He has lived in desolate cities, in houses which no one inhabited, which were ready to become heaps.
web.15:29: He will not be rich, neither will his substance continue, neither will their possessions be extended on the earth.
web.15:30: He will not depart out of darkness. The flame will dry up his branches. He will go away by the breath of God’s mouth.
web.15:31: Let him not trust in emptiness, deceiving himself; for emptiness will be his reward.
web.15:32: It will be accomplished before his time. His branch will not be green.
web.15:33: He will shake off his unripe grape as the vine, and will cast off his flower as the olive tree.
web.15:34: For the company of the godless will be barren, and fire will consume the tents of bribery.
web.15:35: They conceive mischief, and produce iniquity. Their heart prepares deceit.”
web.16:2: “I have heard many such things. You are all miserable comforters!
web.16:3: Shall vain words have an end? Or what provokes you that you answer?
web.16:4: I also could speak as you do. If your soul were in my soul’s place, I could join words together against you, and shake my head at you,
web.16:5: but I would strengthen you with my mouth. The solace of my lips would relieve you.
web.16:6: “Though I speak, my grief is not subsided. Though I forbear, what am I eased?
web.16:7: But now, God, you have surely worn me out. You have made all my company desolate.
web.16:8: You have shriveled me up. This is a witness against me. My leanness rises up against me. It testifies to my face.
web.16:9: He has torn me in his wrath and persecuted me. He has gnashed on me with his teeth. My adversary sharpens his eyes on me.
web.16:10: They have gaped on me with their mouth. They have struck me on the cheek reproachfully. They gather themselves together against me.
web.16:11: God delivers me to the ungodly, and casts me into the hands of the wicked.
web.16:12: I was at ease, and he broke me apart. Yes, he has taken me by the neck, and dashed me to pieces. He has also set me up for his target.
web.16:13: His archers surround me. He splits my kidneys apart, and does not spare. He pours out my bile on the ground.
web.16:14: He breaks me with breach on breach. He runs at me like a giant.
web.16:15: I have sewed sackcloth on my skin, and have thrust my horn in the dust.
web.16:16: My face is red with weeping. Deep darkness is on my eyelids.
web.16:17: Although there is no violence in my hands, and my prayer is pure.
web.16:18: “Earth, don’t cover my blood. Let my cry have no place to rest.
web.16:19: Even now, behold, my witness is in heaven. He who vouches for me is on high.
web.16:20: My friends scoff at me. My eyes pour out tears to God,
web.16:21: that he would maintain the right of a man with God, of a son of man with his neighbor!
web.16:22: For when a few years have come, I will go the way of no return.
web.17:1: “My spirit is consumed. My days are extinct, and the grave is ready for me.
web.17:2: Surely there are mockers with me. My eye dwells on their provocation.
web.17:3: “Now give a pledge. Be collateral for me with yourself. Who is there who will strike hands with me?
web.17:4: For you have hidden their heart from understanding, Therefore you will not exalt them.
web.17:5: He who denounces his friends for plunder, Even the eyes of his children will fail.
web.17:6: “But he has made me a byword of the people. They spit in my face.
web.17:7: My eye also is dim by reason of sorrow. All my members are as a shadow.
web.17:8: Upright men will be astonished at this. The innocent will stir himself up against the godless.
web.17:9: Yet the righteous will hold to his way. He who has clean hands will grow stronger and stronger.
web.17:10: But as for you all, come back. I will not find a wise man among you.
web.17:11: My days are past. My plans are broken off, as are the thoughts of my heart.
web.17:12: They change the night into day, saying ‘The light is near’ in the presence of darkness.
web.17:13: If I look for Sheol as my house, if I have spread my couch in the darkness,
web.17:14: if I have said to corruption, ‘You are my father;’ to the worm, ‘My mother,’ and ‘My sister,’
web.17:15: where then is my hope? as for my hope, who will see it?
web.17:16: Shall it go down with me to the gates of Sheol, or descend together into the dust?”
web.18:2: “How long will you hunt for words? Consider, and afterwards we will speak.
web.18:3: Why are we counted as animals, which have become unclean in your sight?
web.18:4: You who tear yourself in your anger, will the earth be forsaken for you? Or will the rock be removed out of its place?
web.18:5: “Yes, the light of the wicked will be put out. The spark of his fire won’t shine.
web.18:6: The light will be dark in his tent. His lamp above him will be put out.
web.18:7: The steps of his strength will be shortened. His own counsel will cast him down.
web.18:8: For he is cast into a net by his own feet, and he wanders into its mesh.
web.18:9: A snare will take him by the heel. A trap will catch him.
web.18:10: A noose is hidden for him in the ground, a trap for him on the path.
web.18:11: Terrors will make him afraid on every side, and will chase him at his heels.
web.18:12: His strength will be famished. Calamity will be ready at his side.
web.18:13: The members of his body will be devoured. The firstborn of death will devour his members.
web.18:14: He will be rooted out of the security of his tent. He will be brought to the king of terrors.
web.18:15: There will dwell in his tent that which is none of his. Sulfur will be scattered on his habitation.
web.18:16: His roots will be dried up beneath. His branch will be cut off above.
web.18:17: His memory will perish from the earth. He will have no name in the street.
web.18:18: He will be driven from light into darkness, and chased out of the world.
web.18:19: He will have neither son nor grandson among his people, nor any remaining where he lived.
web.18:20: Those who come after will be astonished at his day, as those who went before were frightened.
web.18:21: Surely such are the dwellings of the unrighteous. This is the place of him who doesn’t know God.”
web.19:2: “How long will you torment me, and crush me with words?
web.19:3: You have reproached me ten times. You aren’t ashamed that you attack me.
web.19:4: If it is true that I have erred, my error remains with myself.
web.19:5: If indeed you will magnify yourselves against me, and plead against me my reproach,
web.19:6: know now that God has subverted me, and has surrounded me with his net.
web.19:7: “Behold, I cry out of wrong, but I am not heard. I cry for help, but there is no justice.
web.19:8: He has walled up my way so that I can’t pass, and has set darkness in my paths.
web.19:9: He has stripped me of my glory, and taken the crown from my head.
web.19:10: He has broken me down on every side, and I am gone. He has plucked my hope up like a tree.
web.19:11: He has also kindled his wrath against me. He counts me among his adversaries.
web.19:12: His troops come on together, build a siege ramp against me, and encamp around my tent.
web.19:13: “He has put my brothers far from me. My acquaintances are wholly estranged from me.
web.19:14: My relatives have gone away. My familiar friends have forgotten me.
web.19:15: Those who dwell in my house and my maids consider me a stranger. I am an alien in their sight.
web.19:16: I call to my servant, and he gives me no answer. I beg him with my mouth.
web.19:17: My breath is offensive to my wife. I am loathsome to the children of my own mother.
web.19:18: Even young children despise me. If I arise, they speak against me.
web.19:19: All my familiar friends abhor me. They whom I loved have turned against me.
web.19:20: My bones stick to my skin and to my flesh. I have escaped by the skin of my teeth.
web.19:21: “Have pity on me. Have pity on me, you my friends; for the hand of God has touched me.
web.19:22: Why do you persecute me as God, and are not satisfied with my flesh?
web.19:23: “Oh that my words were now written! Oh that they were inscribed in a book!
web.19:24: That with an iron pen and lead they were engraved in the rock forever!
web.19:25: But as for me, I know that my Redeemer lives. In the end, he will stand upon the earth.
web.19:26: After my skin is destroyed, then I will see God in my flesh,
web.19:27: whom I, even I, will see on my side. My eyes will see, and not as a stranger. “My heart is consumed within me.
web.19:28: If you say, ‘How we will persecute him!’ because the root of the matter is found in me,
web.19:29: be afraid of the sword, for wrath brings the punishments of the sword, that you may know there is a judgment.”
web.20:2: “Therefore my thoughts answer me, even by reason of my haste that is in me.
web.20:3: I have heard the reproof which puts me to shame. The spirit of my understanding answers me.
web.20:4: Don’t you know this from old time, since man was placed on earth,
web.20:5: that the triumphing of the wicked is short, the joy of the godless but for a moment?
web.20:6: Though his height mount up to the heavens, and his head reach to the clouds,
web.20:7: yet he will perish forever like his own dung. Those who have seen him will say, ‘Where is he?’
web.20:8: He will fly away as a dream, and will not be found. Yes, he will be chased away like a vision of the night.
web.20:9: The eye which saw him will see him no more, neither will his place see him any more.
web.20:10: His children will seek the favor of the poor. His hands will give back his wealth.
web.20:11: His bones are full of his youth, but youth will lie down with him in the dust.
web.20:12: “Though wickedness is sweet in his mouth, though he hide it under his tongue,
web.20:13: though he spare it, and will not let it go, but keep it still within his mouth;
web.20:14: yet his food in his bowels is turned. It is cobra venom within him.
web.20:15: He has swallowed down riches, and he will vomit them up again. God will cast them out of his belly.
web.20:16: He will suck cobra venom. The viper’s tongue will kill him.
web.20:17: He will not look at the rivers, the flowing streams of honey and butter.
web.20:18: He will restore that for which he labored, and will not swallow it down. He will not rejoice according to the substance that he has gotten.
web.20:19: For he has oppressed and forsaken the poor. He has violently taken away a house, and he will not build it up.
web.20:20: “Because he knew no quietness within him, he will not save anything of that in which he delights.
web.20:21: There was nothing left that he didn’t devour, therefore his prosperity will not endure.
web.20:22: In the fullness of his sufficiency, distress will overtake him. The hand of everyone who is in misery will come on him.
web.20:23: When he is about to fill his belly, God will cast the fierceness of his wrath on him. It will rain on him while he is eating.
web.20:24: He will flee from the iron weapon. The bronze arrow will strike him through.
web.20:25: He draws it out, and it comes out of his body. Yes, the glittering point comes out of his liver. Terrors are on him.
web.20:26: All darkness is laid up for his treasures. An unfanned fire will devour him. It will consume that which is left in his tent.
web.20:27: The heavens will reveal his iniquity. The earth will rise up against him.
web.20:28: The increase of his house will depart. They will rush away in the day of his wrath.
web.20:29: This is the portion of a wicked man from God, the heritage appointed to him by God.”
web.21:2: “Listen diligently to my speech. Let this be your consolation.
web.21:3: Allow me, and I also will speak; After I have spoken, mock on.
web.21:4: As for me, is my complaint to man? Why shouldn’t I be impatient?
web.21:5: Look at me, and be astonished. Lay your hand on your mouth.
web.21:6: When I remember, I am troubled. Horror takes hold of my flesh.
web.21:7: “Why do the wicked live, become old, yes, and grow mighty in power?
web.21:8: Their child is established with them in their sight, their offspring before their eyes.
web.21:9: Their houses are safe from fear, neither is the rod of God upon them.
web.21:10: Their bulls breed without fail. Their cows calve, and don’t miscarry.
web.21:11: They send out their little ones like a flock. Their children dance.
web.21:12: They sing to the tambourine and harp, and rejoice at the sound of the pipe.
web.21:13: They spend their days in prosperity. In an instant they go down to Sheol.
web.21:14: They tell God, ‘Depart from us, for we don’t want to know about your ways.
web.21:15: What is the Almighty, that we should serve him? What profit should we have, if we pray to him?’
web.21:16: Behold, their prosperity is not in their hand. The counsel of the wicked is far from me.
web.21:17: “How often is it that the lamp of the wicked is put out, that their calamity comes on them, that God distributes sorrows in his anger?
web.21:18: How often is it that they are as stubble before the wind, as chaff that the storm carries away?
web.21:19: You say, ‘God lays up his iniquity for his children.’ Let him recompense it to himself, that he may know it.
web.21:20: Let his own eyes see his destruction. Let him drink of the wrath of the Almighty.
web.21:21: For what does he care for his house after him, when the number of his months is cut off?
web.21:22: “Shall any teach God knowledge, since he judges those who are high?
web.21:23: One dies in his full strength, being wholly at ease and quiet.
web.21:24: His pails are full of milk. The marrow of his bones is moistened.
web.21:25: Another dies in bitterness of soul, and never tastes of good.
web.21:26: They lie down alike in the dust. The worm covers them.
web.21:27: “Behold, I know your thoughts, the plans with which you would wrong me.
web.21:28: For you say, ‘Where is the house of the prince? Where is the tent in which the wicked lived?’
web.21:29: Haven’t you asked wayfaring men? Don’t you know their evidences,
web.21:30: that the evil man is reserved to the day of calamity, That they are led out to the day of wrath?
web.21:31: Who will declare his way to his face? Who will repay him what he has done?
web.21:32: Yet he will be borne to the grave. Men will keep watch over the tomb.
web.21:33: The clods of the valley will be sweet to him. All men will draw after him, as there were innumerable before him.
web.21:34: So how can you comfort me with nonsense, because in your answers there remains only falsehood?”
web.22:2: “Can a man be profitable to God? Surely he who is wise is profitable to himself.
web.22:3: Is it any pleasure to the Almighty that you are righteous? Or does it benefit him that you make your ways perfect?
web.22:4: Is it for your piety that he reproves you, that he enters with you into judgment?
web.22:5: Isn’t your wickedness great? Neither is there any end to your iniquities.
web.22:6: For you have taken pledges from your brother for nothing, and stripped the naked of their clothing.
web.22:7: You haven’t given water to the weary to drink, and you have withheld bread from the hungry.
web.22:8: But as for the mighty man, he had the earth. The honorable man, he lived in it.
web.22:9: You have sent widows away empty, and the arms of the fatherless have been broken.
web.22:10: Therefore snares are around you. Sudden fear troubles you,
web.22:11: or darkness, so that you can not see, and floods of waters cover you.
web.22:12: “Isn’t God in the heights of heaven? See the height of the stars, how high they are!
web.22:13: You say, ‘What does God know? Can he judge through the thick darkness?
web.22:14: Thick clouds are a covering to him, so that he doesn’t see. He walks on the vault of the sky.’
web.22:15: Will you keep the old way, which wicked men have trodden,
web.22:16: who were snatched away before their time, whose foundation was poured out as a stream,
web.22:17: who said to God, ‘Depart from us;’ and, ‘What can the Almighty do for us?’
web.22:18: Yet he filled their houses with good things, but the counsel of the wicked is far from me.
web.22:19: The righteous see it, and are glad. The innocent ridicule them,
web.22:20: saying, ‘Surely those who rose up against us are cut off. The fire has consumed their remnant.’
web.22:21: “Acquaint yourself with him, now, and be at peace. By it, good will come to you.
web.22:22: Please receive instruction from his mouth, and lay up his words in your heart.
web.22:23: If you return to the Almighty, you will be built up, if you put away unrighteousness far from your tents.
web.22:24: Lay your treasure in the dust, the gold of Ophir among the stones of the brooks.
web.22:25: The Almighty will be your treasure, and precious silver to you.
web.22:26: For then you will delight yourself in the Almighty, and will lift up your face to God.
web.22:27: You will make your prayer to him, and he will hear you. You will pay your vows.
web.22:28: You will also decree a thing, and it will be established to you. Light will shine on your ways.
web.22:29: When they cast down, you will say, ‘be lifted up.’ He will save the humble person.
web.22:30: He will even deliver him who is not innocent. Yes, he will be delivered through the cleanness of your hands.”
web.23:2: “Even today my complaint is rebellious. His hand is heavy in spite of my groaning.
web.23:3: Oh that I knew where I might find him! That I might come even to his seat!
web.23:4: I would set my cause in order before him, and fill my mouth with arguments.
web.23:5: I would know the words which he would answer me, and understand what he would tell me.
web.23:6: Would he contend with me in the greatness of his power? No, but he would listen to me.
web.23:7: There the upright might reason with him, so I should be delivered forever from my judge.
web.23:8: “If I go east, he is not there; if west, I can’t find him;
web.23:9: He works to the north, but I can’t see him. He turns south, but I can’t catch a glimpse of him.
web.23:10: But he knows the way that I take. When he has tried me, I will come out like gold.
web.23:11: My foot has held fast to his steps. I have kept his way, and not turned away.
web.23:12: I haven’t gone back from the commandment of his lips. I have treasured up the words of his mouth more than my necessary food.
web.23:13: But he stands alone, and who can oppose him? What his soul desires, even that he does.
web.23:14: For he performs that which is appointed for me. Many such things are with him.
web.23:15: Therefore I am terrified at his presence. When I consider, I am afraid of him.
web.23:16: For God has made my heart faint. The Almighty has terrified me.
web.23:17: Because I was not cut off before the darkness, neither did he cover the thick darkness from my face.
web.24:1: “Why aren’t times laid up by the Almighty? Why don’t those who know him see his days?
web.24:2: There are people who remove the landmarks. They violently take away flocks, and feed them.
web.24:3: They drive away the donkey of the fatherless, and they take the widow’s ox for a pledge.
web.24:4: They turn the needy out of the way. The poor of the earth all hide themselves.
web.24:5: Behold, as wild donkeys in the desert, they go out to their work, seeking diligently for food. The wilderness yields them bread for their children.
web.24:6: They cut their food in the field. They glean the vineyard of the wicked.
web.24:7: They lie all night naked without clothing, and have no covering in the cold.
web.24:8: They are wet with the showers of the mountains, and embrace the rock for lack of a shelter.
web.24:9: There are those who pluck the fatherless from the breast, and take a pledge of the poor,
web.24:10: So that they go around naked without clothing. Being hungry, they carry the sheaves.
web.24:11: They make oil within the walls of these men. They tread wine presses, and suffer thirst.
web.24:12: From out of the populous city, men groan. The soul of the wounded cries out, yet God doesn’t regard the folly.
web.24:13: “These are of those who rebel against the light. They don’t know its ways, nor stay in its paths.
web.24:14: The murderer rises with the light. He kills the poor and needy. In the night he is like a thief.
web.24:15: The eye also of the adulterer waits for the twilight, saying, ‘No eye will see me.’ He disguises his face.
web.24:16: In the dark they dig through houses. They shut themselves up in the daytime. They don’t know the light.
web.24:17: For the morning is to all of them like thick darkness, for they know the terrors of the thick darkness.
web.24:18: “They are foam on the surface of the waters. Their portion is cursed in the earth. They don’t turn into the way of the vineyards.
web.24:19: Drought and heat consume the snow waters, so does Sheol those who have sinned.
web.24:20: The womb will forget him. The worm will feed sweetly on him. He will be no more remembered. Unrighteousness will be broken as a tree.
web.24:21: He devours the barren who don’t bear. He shows no kindness to the widow.
web.24:22: Yet God preserves the mighty by his power. He rises up who has no assurance of life.
web.24:23: God gives them security, and they rest in it. His eyes are on their ways.
web.24:24: They are exalted; yet a little while, and they are gone. Yes, they are brought low, they are taken out of the way as all others, and are cut off as the tops of the ears of grain.
web.24:25: If it isn’t so now, who will prove me a liar, and make my speech worth nothing?”
web.25:2: “Dominion and fear are with him. He makes peace in his high places.
web.25:3: Can his armies be counted? On whom does his light not arise?
web.25:4: How then can man be just with God? Or how can he who is born of a woman be clean?
web.25:5: Behold, even the moon has no brightness, and the stars are not pure in his sight;
web.25:6: How much less man, who is a worm, the son of man, who is a worm!”
web.26:2: “How have you helped him who is without power! How have you saved the arm that has no strength!
web.26:3: How have you counseled him who has no wisdom, and plentifully declared sound knowledge!
web.26:4: To whom have you uttered words? Whose spirit came out of you?
web.26:5: “The departed spirits tremble, those beneath the waters and all that live in them.
web.26:6: Sheol is naked before God, and Abaddon has no covering.
web.26:7: He stretches out the north over empty space, and hangs the earth on nothing.
web.26:8: He binds up the waters in his thick clouds, and the cloud is not burst under them.
web.26:9: He encloses the face of his throne, and spreads his cloud on it.
web.26:10: He has described a boundary on the surface of the waters, and to the confines of light and darkness.
web.26:11: The pillars of heaven tremble and are astonished at his rebuke.
web.26:12: He stirs up the sea with his power, and by his understanding he strikes through Rahab.
web.26:13: By his Spirit the heavens are garnished. His hand has pierced the swift serpent.
web.26:14: Behold, these are but the outskirts of his ways. How small a whisper do we hear of him! But the thunder of his power who can understand?”
web.27:1: Job again took up his parable, and said,
web.27:2: “As God lives, who has taken away my right, the Almighty, who has made my soul bitter
web.27:3: (for the length of my life is still in me, and the spirit of God is in my nostrils);
web.27:4: surely my lips will not speak unrighteousness, neither will my tongue utter deceit.
web.27:5: Far be it from me that I should justify you. Until I die I will not put away my integrity from me.
web.27:6: I hold fast to my righteousness, and will not let it go. My heart will not reproach me so long as I live.
web.27:7: “Let my enemy be as the wicked. Let him who rises up against me be as the unrighteous.
web.27:8: For what is the hope of the godless, when he is cut off, when God takes away his life?
web.27:9: Will God hear his cry when trouble comes on him?
web.27:10: Will he delight himself in the Almighty, and call on God at all times?
web.27:11: I will teach you about the hand of God. I will not conceal that which is with the Almighty.
web.27:12: Behold, all of you have seen it yourselves; why then have you become altogether vain?
web.27:13: “This is the portion of a wicked man with God, the heritage of oppressors, which they receive from the Almighty.
web.27:14: If his children are multiplied, it is for the sword. His offspring will not be satisfied with bread.
web.27:15: Those who remain of him will be buried in death. His widows will make no lamentation.
web.27:16: Though he heap up silver as the dust, and prepare clothing as the clay;
web.27:17: he may prepare it, but the just will put it on, and the innocent will divide the silver.
web.27:18: He builds his house as the moth, as a booth which the watchman makes.
web.27:19: He lies down rich, but he will not do so again. He opens his eyes, and he is not.
web.27:20: Terrors overtake him like waters. A storm steals him away in the night.
web.27:21: The east wind carries him away, and he departs. It sweeps him out of his place.
web.27:22: For it hurls at him, and does not spare, as he flees away from his hand.
web.27:23: Men will clap their hands at him, and will hiss him out of his place.
web.28:1: “Surely there is a mine for silver, and a place for gold which they refine.
web.28:2: Iron is taken out of the earth, and copper is smelted out of the ore.
web.28:3: Man sets an end to darkness, and searches out, to the furthest bound, the stones of obscurity and of thick darkness.
web.28:4: He breaks open a shaft away from where people live. They are forgotten by the foot. They hang far from men, they swing back and forth.
web.28:5: As for the earth, out of it comes bread; Underneath it is turned up as it were by fire.
web.28:6: Sapphires come from its rocks. It has dust of gold.
web.28:7: That path no bird of prey knows, neither has the falcon’s eye seen it.
web.28:8: The proud animals have not trodden it, nor has the fierce lion passed by there.
web.28:9: He puts his hand on the flinty rock, and he overturns the mountains by the roots.
web.28:10: He cuts out channels among the rocks. His eye sees every precious thing.
web.28:11: He binds the streams that they don’t trickle. The thing that is hidden he brings out to light.
web.28:12: “But where will wisdom be found? Where is the place of understanding?
web.28:13: Man doesn’t know its price; Neither is it found in the land of the living.
web.28:14: The deep says, ‘It isn’t in me.’ The sea says, ‘It isn’t with me.’
web.28:15: It can’t be gotten for gold, neither will silver be weighed for its price.
web.28:16: It can’t be valued with the gold of Ophir, with the precious onyx, or the sapphire.
web.28:17: Gold and glass can’t equal it, neither will it be exchanged for jewels of fine gold.
web.28:18: No mention will be made of coral or of crystal. Yes, the price of wisdom is above rubies.
web.28:19: The topaz of Ethiopia will not equal it, nor will it be valued with pure gold.
web.28:20: Where then does wisdom come from? Where is the place of understanding?
web.28:21: Seeing it is hidden from the eyes of all living, and kept close from the birds of the sky.
web.28:22: Destruction and Death say, ‘We have heard a rumor of it with our ears.’
web.28:23: “God understands its way, and he knows its place.
web.28:24: For he looks to the ends of the earth, and sees under the whole sky.
web.28:25: He establishes the force of the wind. Yes, he measures out the waters by measure.
web.28:26: When he made a decree for the rain, and a way for the lightning of the thunder,
web.28:27: then he saw it, and declared it. He established it, yes, and searched it out.
web.28:28: To man he said, ‘Behold, the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom. To depart from evil is understanding.’ ”
web.29:1: Job again took up his parable, and said,
web.29:2: “Oh that I were as in the months of old, as in the days when God watched over me;
web.29:3: when his lamp shone on my head, and by his light I walked through darkness,
web.29:4: as I was in my prime, when the friendship of God was in my tent,
web.29:5: when the Almighty was yet with me, and my children were around me,
web.29:6: when my steps were washed with butter, and the rock poured out streams of oil for me,
web.29:7: when I went out to the city gate, when I prepared my seat in the street.
web.29:8: The young men saw me and hid themselves. The aged rose up and stood.
web.29:9: The princes refrained from talking, and laid their hand on their mouth.
web.29:10: The voice of the nobles was hushed, and their tongue stuck to the roof of their mouth.
web.29:11: For when the ear heard me, then it blessed me; and when the eye saw me, it commended me:
web.29:12: Because I delivered the poor who cried, and the fatherless also, who had no one to help him,
web.29:13: the blessing of him who was ready to perish came on me, and I caused the widow’s heart to sing for joy.
web.29:14: I put on righteousness, and it clothed me. My justice was as a robe and a diadem.
web.29:15: I was eyes to the blind, and feet to the lame.
web.29:16: I was a father to the needy. I researched the cause of him who I didn’t know.
web.29:17: I broke the jaws of the unrighteous and plucked the prey out of his teeth.
web.29:18: Then I said, ‘I will die in my own house, I will count my days as the sand.
web.29:19: My root is spread out to the waters. The dew lies all night on my branch.
web.29:20: My glory is fresh in me. My bow is renewed in my hand.’
web.29:21: “Men listened to me, waited, and kept silence for my counsel.
web.29:22: After my words they didn’t speak again. My speech fell on them.
web.29:23: They waited for me as for the rain. Their mouths drank as with the spring rain.
web.29:24: I smiled on them when they had no confidence. They didn’t reject the light of my face.
web.29:25: I chose out their way, and sat as chief. I lived as a king in the army, as one who comforts the mourners.
web.30:1: “But now those who are younger than I have me in derision, whose fathers I considered unworthy to put with my sheep dogs.
web.30:2: Of what use is the strength of their hands to me, men in whom ripe age has perished?
web.30:3: They are gaunt from lack and famine. They gnaw the dry ground, in the gloom of waste and desolation.
web.30:4: They pluck salt herbs by the bushes. The roots of the broom tree are their food.
web.30:5: They are driven out from among men. They cry after them as after a thief;
web.30:6: So that they dwell in frightful valleys, and in holes of the earth and of the rocks.
web.30:7: They bray among the bushes. They are gathered together under the nettles .
web.30:8: They are children of fools, yes, children of wicked men. They were flogged out of the land.
web.30:9: “Now I have become their song. Yes, I am a byword to them.
web.30:10: They abhor me, they stand aloof from me, and don’t hesitate to spit in my face.
web.30:11: For he has untied his cord, and afflicted me; and they have thrown off restraint before me.
web.30:12: On my right hand rise the rabble. They thrust aside my feet, They cast up against me their ways of destruction.
web.30:13: They mar my path. They promote my destruction without anyone’s help.
web.30:14: As through a wide breach they come. They roll themselves in amid the ruin.
web.30:15: Terrors have turned on me. They chase my honor as the wind. My welfare has passed away as a cloud.
web.30:16: “Now my soul is poured out within me. Days of affliction have taken hold of me.
web.30:17: In the night season my bones are pierced in me, and the pains that gnaw me take no rest.
web.30:18: My garment is disfigured by great force. It binds me about as the collar of my tunic.
web.30:19: He has cast me into the mire. I have become like dust and ashes.
web.30:20: I cry to you, and you do not answer me. I stand up, and you gaze at me.
web.30:21: You have turned to be cruel to me. With the might of your hand you persecute me.
web.30:22: You lift me up to the wind, and drive me with it. You dissolve me in the storm.
web.30:23: For I know that you will bring me to death, To the house appointed for all living.
web.30:24: “However doesn’t one stretch out a hand in his fall? Or in his calamity therefore cry for help?
web.30:25: Didn’t I weep for him who was in trouble? Wasn’t my soul grieved for the needy?
web.30:26: When I looked for good, then evil came. When I waited for light, darkness came.
web.30:27: My heart is troubled, and doesn’t rest. Days of affliction have come on me.
web.30:28: I go mourning without the sun. I stand up in the assembly, and cry for help.
web.30:29: I am a brother to jackals, and a companion to ostriches.
web.30:30: My skin grows black and peels from me. My bones are burned with heat.
web.30:31: Therefore my harp has turned to mourning, and my pipe into the voice of those who weep.
web.31:1: “I made a covenant with my eyes, how then should I look lustfully at a young woman?
web.31:2: For what is the portion from God above, and the heritage from the Almighty on high?
web.31:3: Is it not calamity to the unrighteous, and disaster to the workers of iniquity?
web.31:4: Doesn’t he see my ways, and count all my steps?
web.31:5: “If I have walked with falsehood, and my foot has hurried to deceit
web.31:6: (let me be weighed in an even balance, that God may know my integrity);
web.31:7: if my step has turned out of the way, if my heart walked after my eyes, if any defilement has stuck to my hands,
web.31:8: then let me sow, and let another eat. Yes, let the produce of my field be rooted out.
web.31:9: “If my heart has been enticed to a woman, and I have laid wait at my neighbor’s door,
web.31:10: then let my wife grind for another, and let others sleep with her.
web.31:11: For that would be a heinous crime. Yes, it would be an iniquity to be punished by the judges;
