web.31:12: for it is a fire that consumes to destruction, and would root out all my increase.
web.31:13: “If I have despised the cause of my male servant or of my female servant, when they contended with me,
web.31:14: what then will I do when God rises up? When he visits, what will I answer him?
web.31:15: Didn’t he who made me in the womb make him? Didn’t one fashion us in the womb?
web.31:16: “If I have withheld the poor from their desire, or have caused the eyes of the widow to fail,
web.31:17: or have eaten my morsel alone, and the fatherless has not eaten of it
web.31:18: (no, from my youth he grew up with me as with a father, I have guided her from my mother’s womb);
web.31:19: if I have seen any perish for want of clothing, or that the needy had no covering;
web.31:20: if his heart hasn’t blessed me, if he hasn’t been warmed with my sheep’s fleece;
web.31:21: if I have lifted up my hand against the fatherless, because I saw my help in the gate,
web.31:22: then let my shoulder fall from the shoulder blade, and my arm be broken from the bone.
web.31:23: For calamity from God is a terror to me. Because of his majesty, I can do nothing.
web.31:24: “If I have made gold my hope, and have said to the fine gold, ‘You are my confidence;’
web.31:25: If I have rejoiced because my wealth was great, and because my hand had gotten much;
web.31:26: if I have seen the sun when it shined, or the moon moving in splendor,
web.31:27: and my heart has been secretly enticed, and my hand threw a kiss from my mouth,
web.31:28: this also would be an iniquity to be punished by the judges; for I should have denied the God who is above.
web.31:29: “If I have rejoiced at the destruction of him who hated me, or lifted up myself when evil found him
web.31:30: (yes, I have not allowed my mouth to sin by asking his life with a curse);
web.31:31: if the men of my tent have not said, ‘Who can find one who has not been filled with his meat?’
web.31:32: (the foreigner has not camped in the street, but I have opened my doors to the traveler);
web.31:33: if like Adam I have covered my transgressions, by hiding my iniquity in my heart,
web.31:34: because I feared the great multitude, and the contempt of families terrified me, so that I kept silence, and didn’t go out of the door—
web.31:35: oh that I had one to hear me! Behold, here is my signature! Let the Almighty answer me! Let the accuser write my indictment!
web.31:36: Surely I would carry it on my shoulder; and I would bind it to me as a crown.
web.31:37: I would declare to him the number of my steps. as a prince would I go near to him.
web.31:38: If my land cries out against me, and its furrows weep together;
web.31:39: if I have eaten its fruits without money, or have caused its owners to lose their life,
web.31:40: let briers grow instead of wheat, and stinkweed instead of barley.” The words of Job are ended.
web.32:1: So these three men ceased to answer Job, because he was righteous in his own eyes.
web.32:2: Then the wrath of Elihu the son of Barachel, the Buzite, of the family of Ram, was kindled against Job. His wrath was kindled because he justified himself rather than God.
web.32:3: Also his wrath was kindled against his three friends, because they had found no answer, and yet had condemned Job.
web.32:4: Now Elihu had waited to speak to Job, because they were elder than he.
web.32:5: When Elihu saw that there was no answer in the mouth of these three men, his wrath was kindled.
web.32:6: Elihu the son of Barachel the Buzite answered, “I am young, and you are very old; Therefore I held back, and didn’t dare show you my opinion.
web.32:7: I said, ‘Days should speak, and multitude of years should teach wisdom.’
web.32:8: But there is a spirit in man, and the Spirit of the Almighty gives them understanding.
web.32:9: It is not the great who are wise, nor the aged who understand justice.
web.32:10: Therefore I said, ‘Listen to me; I also will show my opinion.’
web.32:11: “Behold, I waited for your words, and I listened for your reasoning, while you searched out what to say.
web.32:12: Yes, I gave you my full attention, but there was no one who convinced Job, or who answered his words, among you.
web.32:13: Beware lest you say, ‘We have found wisdom. God may refute him, not man;’
web.32:14: for he has not directed his words against me; neither will I answer him with your speeches.
web.32:15: “They are amazed. They answer no more. They don’t have a word to say.
web.32:16: Shall I wait, because they don’t speak, because they stand still, and answer no more?
web.32:17: I also will answer my part, and I also will show my opinion.
web.32:18: For I am full of words. The spirit within me constrains me.
web.32:19: Behold, my breast is as wine which has no vent; like new wineskins it is ready to burst.
web.32:20: I will speak, that I may be refreshed. I will open my lips and answer.
web.32:21: Please don’t let me respect any man’s person, neither will I give flattering titles to any man.
web.32:22: For I don’t know how to give flattering titles, or else my Maker would soon take me away.
web.33:1: “However, Job, please hear my speech, and listen to all my words.
web.33:2: See now, I have opened my mouth. My tongue has spoken in my mouth.
web.33:3: My words will utter the uprightness of my heart. That which my lips know they will speak sincerely.
web.33:4: The Spirit of God has made me, and the breath of the Almighty gives me life.
web.33:5: If you can, answer me. Set your words in order before me, and stand up.
web.33:6: Behold, I am toward God even as you are. I am also formed out of the clay.
web.33:7: Behold, my terror will not make you afraid, neither will my pressure be heavy on you.
web.33:8: “Surely you have spoken in my hearing, I have heard the voice of your words, saying,
web.33:9: ‘I am clean, without disobedience. I am innocent, neither is there iniquity in me.
web.33:10: Behold, he finds occasions against me. He counts me for his enemy.
web.33:11: He puts my feet in the stocks. He marks all my paths.’
web.33:12: “Behold, I will answer you. In this you are not just, for God is greater than man.
web.33:13: Why do you strive against him, because he doesn’t give account of any of his matters?
web.33:14: For God speaks once, yes twice, though man pays no attention.
web.33:15: In a dream, in a vision of the night, when deep sleep falls on men, in slumbering on the bed;
web.33:16: Then he opens the ears of men, and seals their instruction,
web.33:17: that he may withdraw man from his purpose, and hide pride from man.
web.33:18: He keeps back his soul from the pit, and his life from perishing by the sword.
web.33:19: He is chastened also with pain on his bed, with continual strife in his bones,
web.33:20: so that his life abhors bread, and his soul dainty food.
web.33:21: His flesh is so consumed away that it can’t be seen. His bones that were not seen stick out.
web.33:22: Yes, his soul draws near to the pit, and his life to the destroyers.
web.33:23: “If there is beside him an angel, an interpreter, one among a thousand, to show to man what is right for him;
web.33:24: then God is gracious to him, and says, ‘Deliver him from going down to the pit, I have found a ransom.’
web.33:25: His flesh will be fresher than a child’s. He returns to the days of his youth.
web.33:26: He prays to God, and he is favorable to him, so that he sees his face with joy. He restores to man his righteousness.
web.33:27: He sings before men, and says, ‘I have sinned, and perverted that which was right, and it didn’t profit me.
web.33:28: He has redeemed my soul from going into the pit. My life will see the light.’
web.33:29: “Behold, God does all these things, twice, yes three times, with a man,
web.33:30: to bring back his soul from the pit, that he may be enlightened with the light of the living.
web.33:31: Mark well, Job, and listen to me. Hold your peace, and I will speak.
web.33:32: If you have anything to say, answer me. Speak, for I desire to justify you.
web.33:33: If not, listen to me. Hold your peace, and I will teach you wisdom.”
web.34:2: “Hear my words, you wise men. Give ear to me, you who have knowledge.
web.34:3: For the ear tries words, as the palate tastes food.
web.34:4: Let us choose for us that which is right. Let us know among ourselves what is good.
web.34:5: For Job has said, ‘I am righteous, God has taken away my right:
web.34:6: Notwithstanding my right I am considered a liar. My wound is incurable, though I am without disobedience.’
web.34:7: What man is like Job, who drinks scorn like water,
web.34:8: Who goes in company with the workers of iniquity, and walks with wicked men?
web.34:9: For he has said, ‘It profits a man nothing that he should delight himself with God.’
web.34:10: “Therefore listen to me, you men of understanding: far be it from God, that he should do wickedness, from the Almighty, that he should commit iniquity.
web.34:11: For the work of a man he will render to him, and cause every man to find according to his ways.
web.34:12: Yes surely, God will not do wickedly, neither will the Almighty pervert justice.
web.34:13: Who put him in charge of the earth? Or who has appointed him over the whole world?
web.34:14: If he set his heart on himself, if he gathered to himself his spirit and his breath,
web.34:15: all flesh would perish together, and man would turn again to dust.
web.34:16: “If now you have understanding, hear this. Listen to the voice of my words.
web.34:17: Should even one who hates justice govern? Will you condemn him who is righteous and mighty?—
web.34:18: Who says to a king, ‘Vile!’ or to nobles, ‘Wicked!’?
web.34:19: He doesn’t respect the persons of princes, nor respect the rich more than the poor; for they all are the work of his hands.
web.34:20: In a moment they die, even at midnight. The people are shaken and pass away. The mighty are taken away without a hand.
web.34:21: “For his eyes are on the ways of a man. He sees all his goings.
web.34:22: There is no darkness, nor thick gloom, where the workers of iniquity may hide themselves.
web.34:23: For he doesn’t need to consider a man further, that he should go before God in judgment.
web.34:24: He breaks mighty men in pieces in ways past finding out, and sets others in their place.
web.34:25: Therefore he takes knowledge of their works. He overturns them in the night, so that they are destroyed.
web.34:26: He strikes them as wicked men in the open sight of others;
web.34:27: because they turned away from following him, and wouldn’t pay attention to any of his ways,
web.34:28: so that they caused the cry of the poor to come to him. He heard the cry of the afflicted.
web.34:29: When he gives quietness, who then can condemn? When he hides his face, who then can see him? He is over a nation or a man alike,
web.34:30: that the godless man may not reign, that there be no one to ensnare the people.
web.34:31: “For has any said to God, ‘I am guilty, but I will not offend any more.
web.34:32: Teach me that which I don’t see. If I have done iniquity, I will do it no more’?
web.34:33: Shall his recompense be as you desire, that you refuse it? For you must choose, and not I. Therefore speak what you know.
web.34:34: Men of understanding will tell me, yes, every wise man who hears me:
web.34:35: ‘Job speaks without knowledge. His words are without wisdom.’
web.34:36: I wish that Job were tried to the end, because of his answering like wicked men.
web.34:37: For he adds rebellion to his sin. He claps his hands among us, and multiplies his words against God.”
web.35:2: “Do you think this to be your right, or do you say, ‘My righteousness is more than God’s,’
web.35:3: that you ask, ‘What advantage will it be to you? What profit will I have, more than if I had sinned?’
web.35:4: I will answer you, and your companions with you.
web.35:5: Look to the skies, and see. See the skies, which are higher than you.
web.35:6: If you have sinned, what effect do you have against him? If your transgressions are multiplied, what do you do to him?
web.35:7: If you are righteous, what do you give him? Or what does he receive from your hand?
web.35:8: Your wickedness may hurt a man as you are, and your righteousness may profit a son of man.
web.35:9: “By reason of the multitude of oppressions they cry out. They cry for help by reason of the arm of the mighty.
web.35:10: But no one says, ‘Where is God my Maker, who gives songs in the night,
web.35:11: who teaches us more than the animals of the earth, and makes us wiser than the birds of the sky?’
web.35:12: There they cry, but no one answers, because of the pride of evil men.
web.35:13: Surely God will not hear an empty cry, neither will the Almighty regard it.
web.35:14: How much less when you say you don’t see him. The cause is before him, and you wait for him!
web.35:15: But now, because he has not visited in his anger, neither does he greatly regard arrogance.
web.35:16: Therefore Job opens his mouth with empty talk, and he multiplies words without knowledge.”
web.36:2: “Bear with me a little, and I will show you; for I still have something to say on God’s behalf.
web.36:3: I will get my knowledge from afar, and will ascribe righteousness to my Maker.
web.36:4: For truly my words are not false. One who is perfect in knowledge is with you.
web.36:5: “Behold, God is mighty, and doesn’t despise anyone. He is mighty in strength of understanding.
web.36:6: He doesn’t preserve the life of the wicked, but gives justice to the afflicted.
web.36:7: He doesn’t withdraw his eyes from the righteous, but with kings on the throne, he sets them forever, and they are exalted.
web.36:8: If they are bound in fetters, and are taken in the cords of afflictions,
web.36:9: then he shows them their work, and their transgressions, that they have behaved themselves proudly.
web.36:10: He also opens their ears to instruction, and commands that they return from iniquity.
web.36:11: If they listen and serve him, they will spend their days in prosperity, and their years in pleasures.
web.36:12: But if they don’t listen, they will perish by the sword; they will die without knowledge.
web.36:13: “But those who are godless in heart lay up anger. They don’t cry for help when he binds them.
web.36:14: They die in youth. Their life perishes among the unclean.
web.36:15: He delivers the afflicted by their affliction, and opens their ear in oppression.
web.36:16: Yes, he would have allured you out of distress, into a wide place, where there is no restriction. That which is set on your table would be full of fatness.
web.36:17: “But you are full of the judgment of the wicked. Judgment and justice take hold of you.
web.36:18: Don’t let riches entice you to wrath, neither let the great size of a bribe turn you aside.
web.36:19: Would your wealth sustain you in distress, or all the might of your strength?
web.36:20: Don’t desire the night, when people are cut off in their place.
web.36:21: Take heed, don’t regard iniquity; for you have chosen this rather than affliction.
web.36:22: Behold, God is exalted in his power. Who is a teacher like him?
web.36:23: Who has prescribed his way for him? Or who can say, ‘You have committed unrighteousness?’
web.36:24: “Remember that you magnify his work, about which men have sung.
web.36:25: All men have looked on it. Man sees it afar off.
web.36:26: Behold, God is great, and we don’t know him. The number of his years is unsearchable.
web.36:27: For he draws up the drops of water, which distill in rain from his vapor,
web.36:28: which the skies pour down and which drop on man abundantly.
web.36:29: Yes, can any understand the spreading of the clouds, and the thunderings of his pavilion?
web.36:30: Behold, he spreads his light around him. He covers the bottom of the sea.
web.36:31: For by these he judges the people. He gives food in abundance.
web.36:32: He covers his hands with the lightning, and commands it to strike the mark.
web.36:33: Its noise tells about him, and the livestock also concerning the storm that comes up.
web.37:1: “Yes, at this my heart trembles, and is moved out of its place.
web.37:2: Hear, oh, hear the noise of his voice, the sound that goes out of his mouth.
web.37:3: He sends it out under the whole sky, and his lightning to the ends of the earth.
web.37:4: After it a voice roars. He thunders with the voice of his majesty. He doesn’t hold back anything when his voice is heard.
web.37:5: God thunders marvelously with his voice. He does great things, which we can’t comprehend.
web.37:6: For he says to the snow, ‘Fall on the earth,’ likewise to the shower of rain, and to the showers of his mighty rain.
web.37:7: He seals up the hand of every man, that all men whom he has made may know it.
web.37:8: Then the animals take cover, and remain in their dens.
web.37:9: Out of its room comes the storm, and cold out of the north.
web.37:10: By the breath of God, ice is given, and the width of the waters is frozen.
web.37:11: Yes, he loads the thick cloud with moisture. He spreads abroad the cloud of his lightning.
web.37:12: It is turned around by his guidance, that they may do whatever he commands them on the surface of the habitable world,
web.37:13: Whether it is for correction, or for his land, or for loving kindness, that he causes it to come.
web.37:14: “Listen to this, Job. Stand still, and consider the wondrous works of God.
web.37:15: Do you know how God controls them, and causes the lightning of his cloud to shine?
web.37:16: Do you know the workings of the clouds, the wondrous works of him who is perfect in knowledge?
web.37:17: You whose clothing is warm, when the earth is still by reason of the south wind?
web.37:18: Can you, with him, spread out the sky, which is strong as a cast metal mirror?
web.37:19: Teach us what we will tell him, for we can’t make our case by reason of darkness.
web.37:20: Will it be told him that I would speak? Or should a man wish that he were swallowed up?
web.37:21: Now men don’t see the light which is bright in the skies, but the wind passes, and clears them.
web.37:22: Out of the north comes golden splendor. With God is awesome majesty.
web.37:23: We can’t reach the Almighty. He is exalted in power. In justice and great righteousness, he will not oppress.
web.37:24: Therefore men revere him. He doesn’t regard any who are wise of heart.”
web.38:1: Then Yahweh answered Job out of the whirlwind,
web.38:2: “Who is this who darkens counsel by words without knowledge?
web.38:3: Brace yourself like a man, for I will question you, then you answer me!
web.38:4: “Where were you when I laid the foundations of the earth? Declare, if you have understanding.
web.38:5: Who determined its measures, if you know? Or who stretched the line on it?
web.38:6: What were its foundations fastened on? Or who laid its cornerstone,
web.38:7: when the morning stars sang together, and all the sons of God shouted for joy?
web.38:8: “Or who shut up the sea with doors, when it broke out of the womb,
web.38:9: when I made clouds its garment, and wrapped it in thick darkness,
web.38:10: marked out for it my bound, set bars and doors,
web.38:11: and said, ‘You may come here, but no further. Your proud waves shall be stopped here?’
web.38:12: “Have you commanded the morning in your days, and caused the dawn to know its place,
web.38:13: that it might take hold of the ends of the earth, and shake the wicked out of it?
web.38:14: It is changed as clay under the seal, and presented as a garment.
web.38:15: From the wicked, their light is withheld. The high arm is broken.
web.38:16: “Have you entered into the springs of the sea? Or have you walked in the recesses of the deep?
web.38:17: Have the gates of death been revealed to you? Or have you seen the gates of the shadow of death?
web.38:18: Have you comprehended the earth in its width? Declare, if you know it all.
web.38:19: “What is the way to the dwelling of light? As for darkness, where is its place,
web.38:20: that you should take it to its bound, that you should discern the paths to its house?
web.38:21: Surely you know, for you were born then, and the number of your days is great!
web.38:22: Have you entered the treasuries of the snow, or have you seen the treasures of the hail,
web.38:23: which I have reserved against the time of trouble, against the day of battle and war?
web.38:24: By what way is the lightning distributed, or the east wind scattered on the earth?
web.38:25: Who has cut a channel for the flood water, or the path for the thunder storm,
web.38:26: to cause it to rain on a land where there is no man, on the wilderness, in which there is no man,
web.38:27: to satisfy the waste and desolate ground, to cause the tender grass to grow?
web.38:28: Does the rain have a father? Or who fathers the drops of dew?
web.38:29: Whose womb did the ice come out of? Who has given birth to the gray frost of the sky?
web.38:30: The waters become hard like stone, when the surface of the deep is frozen.
web.38:31: “Can you bind the cluster of the Pleiades, or loosen the cords of Orion?
web.38:32: Can you lead the constellations out in their season? Or can you guide the Bear with her cubs?
web.38:33: Do you know the laws of the heavens? Can you establish its dominion over the earth?
web.38:34: “Can you lift up your voice to the clouds, That abundance of waters may cover you?
web.38:35: Can you send out lightnings, that they may go? Do they report to you, ‘Here we are?’
web.38:36: Who has put wisdom in the inward parts? Or who has given understanding to the mind?
web.38:37: Who can count the clouds by wisdom? Or who can pour out the containers of the sky,
web.38:38: when the dust runs into a mass, and the clods of earth stick together?
web.38:39: “Can you hunt the prey for the lioness, or satisfy the appetite of the young lions,
web.38:40: when they crouch in their dens, and lie in wait in the thicket?
web.38:41: Who provides for the raven his prey, when his young ones cry to God, and wander for lack of food?
web.39:1: “Do you know the time when the mountain goats give birth? Do you watch when the doe bears fawns?
web.39:2: Can you count the months that they fulfill? Or do you know the time when they give birth?
web.39:3: They bow themselves. They bear their young. They end their labor pains.
web.39:4: Their young ones become strong. They grow up in the open field. They go out, and don’t return again.
web.39:5: “Who has set the wild donkey free? Or who has loosened the bonds of the swift donkey,
web.39:6: whose home I have made the wilderness, and the salt land his dwelling place?
web.39:7: He scorns the tumult of the city, neither does he hear the shouting of the driver.
web.39:8: The range of the mountains is his pasture, He searches after every green thing.
web.39:9: “Will the wild ox be content to serve you? Or will he stay by your feeding trough?
web.39:10: Can you hold the wild ox in the furrow with his harness? Or will he till the valleys after you?
web.39:11: Will you trust him, because his strength is great? Or will you leave to him your labor?
web.39:12: Will you confide in him, that he will bring home your seed, and gather the grain of your threshing floor?
web.39:13: “The wings of the ostrich wave proudly; but are they the feathers and plumage of love?
web.39:14: For she leaves her eggs on the earth, warms them in the dust,
web.39:15: and forgets that the foot may crush them, or that the wild animal may trample them.
web.39:16: She deals harshly with her young ones, as if they were not hers. Though her labor is in vain, she is without fear,
web.39:17: because God has deprived her of wisdom, neither has he imparted to her understanding.
web.39:18: When she lifts up herself on high, she scorns the horse and his rider.
web.39:19: “Have you given the horse might? Have you clothed his neck with a quivering mane?
web.39:20: Have you made him to leap as a locust? The glory of his snorting is awesome.
web.39:21: He paws in the valley, and rejoices in his strength. He goes out to meet the armed men.
web.39:22: He mocks at fear, and is not dismayed, neither does he turn back from the sword.
web.39:23: The quiver rattles against him, the flashing spear and the javelin.
web.39:24: He eats up the ground with fierceness and rage, neither does he stand still at the sound of the trumpet.
web.39:25: As often as the trumpet sounds he snorts, ‘Aha!’ He smells the battle afar off, the thunder of the captains, and the shouting.
web.39:26: “Is it by your wisdom that the hawk soars, and stretches her wings toward the south?
web.39:27: Is it at your command that the eagle mounts up, and makes his nest on high?
web.39:28: On the cliff he dwells, and makes his home, on the point of the cliff, and the stronghold.
web.39:29: From there he spies out the prey. His eyes see it afar off.
web.39:30: His young ones also suck up blood. Where the slain are, there he is.”
web.40:2: “Shall he who argues contend with the Almighty? He who argues with God, let him answer it.”
web.40:4: “Behold, I am of small account. What will I answer you? I lay my hand on my mouth.
web.40:5: I have spoken once, and I will not answer; Yes, twice, but I will proceed no further.”
web.40:6: Then Yahweh answered Job out of the whirlwind,
web.40:7: “Now brace yourself like a man. I will question you, and you will answer me.
web.40:8: Will you even annul my judgment? Will you condemn me, that you may be justified?
web.40:9: Or do you have an arm like God? Can you thunder with a voice like him?
web.40:10: “Now deck yourself with excellency and dignity. Array yourself with honor and majesty.
web.40:11: Pour out the fury of your anger. Look at everyone who is proud, and bring him low.
web.40:12: Look at everyone who is proud, and humble him. Crush the wicked in their place.
web.40:13: Hide them in the dust together. Bind their faces in the hidden place.
web.40:14: Then I will also admit to you that your own right hand can save you.
web.40:15: “See now, behemoth, which I made as well as you. He eats grass as an ox.
web.40:16: Look now, his strength is in his thighs. His force is in the muscles of his belly.
web.40:17: He moves his tail like a cedar. The sinews of his thighs are knit together.
web.40:18: His bones are like tubes of bronze. His limbs are like bars of iron.
web.40:19: He is the chief of the ways of God. He who made him gives him his sword.
web.40:20: Surely the mountains produce food for him, where all the animals of the field play.
web.40:21: He lies under the lotus trees, in the covert of the reed, and the marsh.
web.40:22: The lotuses cover him with their shade. The willows of the brook surround him.
web.40:23: Behold, if a river overflows, he doesn’t tremble. He is confident, though the Jordan swells even to his mouth.
web.40:24: Shall any take him when he is on the watch, or pierce through his nose with a snare?
web.41:1: “Can you draw out Leviathan with a fish hook, or press down his tongue with a cord?
web.41:2: Can you put a rope into his nose, or pierce his jaw through with a hook?
web.41:3: Will he make many petitions to you, or will he speak soft words to you?
web.41:4: Will he make a covenant with you, that you should take him for a servant forever?
web.41:5: Will you play with him as with a bird? Or will you bind him for your girls?
web.41:6: Will traders barter for him? Will they part him among the merchants?
web.41:7: Can you fill his skin with barbed irons, or his head with fish spears?
web.41:8: Lay your hand on him. Remember the battle, and do so no more.
web.41:9: Behold, the hope of him is in vain. Won’t one be cast down even at the sight of him?
web.41:10: None is so fierce that he dare stir him up. Who then is he who can stand before me?
web.41:11: Who has first given to me, that I should repay him? Everything under the heavens is mine.
web.41:12: “I will not keep silence concerning his limbs, nor his mighty strength, nor his goodly frame.
web.41:13: Who can strip off his outer garment? Who will come within his jaws?
web.41:14: Who can open the doors of his face? Around his teeth is terror.
web.41:15: Strong scales are his pride, shut up together with a close seal.
web.41:16: One is so near to another, that no air can come between them.
web.41:17: They are joined to one another. They stick together, so that they can’t be pulled apart.
web.41:18: His sneezing flashes out light. His eyes are like the eyelids of the morning.
web.41:19: Out of his mouth go burning torches. Sparks of fire leap out.
web.41:20: Out of his nostrils a smoke goes, as of a boiling pot over a fire of reeds.
web.41:21: His breath kindles coals. A flame goes out of his mouth.
web.41:22: There is strength in his neck. Terror dances before him.
web.41:23: The flakes of his flesh are joined together. They are firm on him. They can’t be moved.
web.41:24: His heart is as firm as a stone, yes, firm as the lower millstone.
web.41:25: When he raises himself up, the mighty are afraid. They retreat before his thrashing.
web.41:26: If one attacks him with the sword, it can’t prevail; nor the spear, the dart, nor the pointed shaft.
web.41:27: He counts iron as straw; and bronze as rotten wood.
web.41:28: The arrow can’t make him flee. Sling stones are like chaff to him.
web.41:29: Clubs are counted as stubble. He laughs at the rushing of the javelin.
web.41:30: His undersides are like sharp potsherds, leaving a trail in the mud like a threshing sledge.
web.41:31: He makes the deep to boil like a pot. He makes the sea like a pot of ointment.
web.41:32: He makes a path shine after him. One would think the deep had white hair.
web.41:33: On earth there is not his equal, that is made without fear.
web.41:34: He sees everything that is high. He is king over all the sons of pride.”
web.42:2: “I know that you can do all things, and that no purpose of yours can be restrained.
web.42:3: You asked, ‘Who is this who hides counsel without knowledge?’ therefore I have uttered that which I didn’t understand, things too wonderful for me, which I didn’t know.
web.42:4: You said, ‘Listen, now, and I will speak; I will question you, and you will answer me.’
web.42:5: I had heard of you by the hearing of the ear, but now my eye sees you.
web.42:6: Therefore I abhor myself, and repent in dust and ashes.”
web.42:7: It was so, that after Yahweh had spoken these words to Job, Yahweh said to Eliphaz the Temanite, “My wrath is kindled against you, and against your two friends; for you have not spoken of me the thing that is right, as my servant Job has.
web.42:8: Now therefore, take to yourselves seven bulls and seven rams, and go to my servant Job, and offer up for yourselves a burnt offering; and my servant Job shall pray for you, for I will accept him, that I not deal with you according to your folly. For you have not spoken of me the thing that is right, as my servant Job has.”
web.42:9: So Eliphaz the Temanite and Bildad the Shuhite and Zophar the Naamathite went, and did what Yahweh commanded them, and Yahweh accepted Job.
web.42:10: Yahweh turned the captivity of Job, when he prayed for his friends. Yahweh gave Job twice as much as he had before.
web.42:11: Then came there to him all his brothers, and all his sisters, and all those who had been of his acquaintance before, and ate bread with him in his house. They comforted him, and consoled him concerning all the evil that Yahweh had brought on him. Everyone also gave him a piece of money, and everyone a ring of gold.
web.42:12: So Yahweh blessed the latter end of Job more than his beginning. He had fourteen thousand sheep, six thousand camels, one thousand yoke of oxen, and a thousand female donkeys.
web.42:13: He had also seven sons and three daughters.
web.42:14: He called the name of the first, Jemimah; and the name of the second, Keziah; and the name of the third, Keren Happuch.
web.42:15: In all the land were no women found so beautiful as the daughters of Job. Their father gave them an inheritance among their brothers.
web.42:16: After this Job lived one hundred forty years, and saw his sons, and his sons’ sons, to four generations.
web.42:17: So Job died, being old and full of days.
